Well, when I were a young man we used to take fishing trips over to Catherby; The fishing over there - now that was something!
Anyway, we decided to do a bit of fishing with our nets, I wasn't having the best of days turning up nothing but old boots and bits of seaweed. Then my net suddenly got really heavy!
I pulled it up...
To my amazement I'd caught this little chest thing!
Even more amazing was when I opened it it contained a diamond the size of a radish! That's the best catch I've ever had!

Good day to you!

o.x: Good morrow sirrah/madam!

An adventurer eh? There is no service finer than serving the bountiful King Arthur, and I happen to know there's an important quest to fulfill.
Sir Knight! Many thanks for your assistance in restoring Merlin to his former freedom!
Hey, no problem.
We owe you a great debt for freeing us from that dungeon.
Awww, shucks. It was nothing.

Stankers will allow 308 pieces of coal in his coal truck, and you'll get bonuses when cutting maple and normal trees.

I'm not finished! Your Camelot Teleport spell can be switched to Seers' Village and Thormac will lower his prices somewhat. Phew! Oh, and how could I forget - you'll get a bonus when you use the altar in the chapel here, but you don't need to wear the headband for that.
Thank you, Sir Kay. I'll try not to harm anyone with my spinning.
You are most welcome. You may also find that the Lady of the Lake is prepared to reward you for your services if you wear the headband in her presence.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Seers' Village set, you are presented with a headband.
You will receive a better headband with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Seers' Village set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Seers' Village set rewards, speak to any seer in the village, Stankers out west by the coal trucks, or myself.

Young'un?

The 'Little Boss' is a bit strict with us, but don't get me wrong, we're all glad that The Skulls aren't causing trouble in Draynor anymore.

'Course he's just the best teacher. You don't need him to show you how it works. Not like in my day. Back then you had to go running all over the place before you so much as learned how to wipe muck off a leaf.
Still, that's what the kids are all like these days. No time to stop and listen to a teacher. With their 'rune armour', and their 'chilly-chompers' and their loud music...
Uh... thanks?

Sure, to earn the right to wear any skillcape you need to have mastered the skill to the highest level possible and it is no different for Herblore. When you have achieved a level of 99, come back and talk to me again.

b.x: Welcome to the church of holy Saradomin.
Welcome back to the church of holy Saradomin, my friend! What can I do for you today?

nodes.title: What would you like to say?

o.x: Surely you have heard of our god, Saradomin?
He who created the forces of goodness and purity in this world? I cannot believe your ignorance!
This is the god with more followers than any other...at least in this part of the world.
He defeated the evil Zamorak in the battle of Lumbridge nearby, and he defends us from evil!

o.title: Select an option

o.x: There is only one Saradomin.
Yeah. I, uh, thought you said something else.

o: Oh, sorry, I'm not from this world.

o.x: That's...strange.
I thought things not from this world were all, you know, slime and tentacles.

o.title: Select an option

o.x: Well, I can see that. Still, there's something special about you.
Thanks, I think.

o: I am! Do you like my disguise?

o.x: Argh! Avaunt, foul creature from another dimension! Avaunt! Begone in the name of Saradomin!
Okay, okay, I was only joking!

o: Can you tell me about the battlefield?

o.x: It is, isn't it? It was built over two centuries ago.

o: Can you tell me about the crater?

o.x: Ah, Lumbridge Battlefield - the site of the return of Saradomin! That was a momentous day for the church, and I was there!
In a titanic battle that lasted for months, the mighty Saradomin drove back the forces of Zamorak to the Underworld where they belong.
And now Saradomin is here, we can be sure that we will be safe under his divine protection.
All praise Saradomin!

o.x: Yes please.
Magic Guild Store - Runes and Staves
No thank you.

nodes.x: You need a Magic level of 66 for admittance to the guild. The magical energy inside the guild is unsafe for anyone below that level. For any other business please ring for attention.
Good day to you Sir.
Well hello my brave adventurer.
What are you up to?
Getting ready to go fishing of course. There's no time to waste!
I've got all the supplies I need from the shop at the end of the pier. They sell good rope, although their bailing buckets aren't too effective.

nodes.title: Choose an option:

o.x: What fish do you catch?
I get all sorts, anything that lies on the sea bed, you never know what you're going to get until you pull up the net!

o: Your boat doesn't look too safe.

o.x: Your boat doesn't look too safe.
That's because it's not, the darn thing's full of holes.
Oh, so I suppose you can't go out for a while?
Oh no, I don't let a few holes stop an experienced sailor like me. I could sail these seas in a barrel, I'll be going out soon enough.
Could I help?
Well of course you can! I'll warn you though, the seas are merciless and without fishing experience you won't catch much.
You need a fishing level of 15 or above to catch any fish on the trawler.
On occasions the net rips, so you'll need some rope to repair it.
Repairing the net is difficult in the harsh conditions so you'll find it easier with a higher Crafting level.
Right...ok.
There's also a slight problem with leaks.
Leaks?!
Nothing some swamp paste won't fix...
Swamp paste?
Oh, and one more thing... I hope you're a good swimmer?

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Actually, I think I'll leave it.

o.x: Actually, I think I'll leave it.
Bloomin' land lovers!!!
I'll be fine, let's go.
Aye aye! Meet me on board the trawler. I just need to get a few things together.
What's swamp paste?
Swamp tar mixed with flour which is then heated over a fire.
Where can I find swamp tar?
Unfortunately the only supply of swamp tar is in the swamps below Lumbridge.

Bob hands you a silver ring.
There. I think you will find this ring more suited to an adventurer of your talents.
It possesses all of your previous ring's functions, with the added bonus of an extra run energy charge as well as 30 charges of the Low Alchemy spell!
The spell will allow you to transform certain items in your inventory into coins.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: For completing the Lumbridge and Draynor set, you are presented with an explorer's ring.
This ring will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward. Most of the Lumbridge set's Tasks are straightforward, although you might find some require quests to be started, if not finished.
To claim the Lumbridge set reward, speak to Ned in Draynor Village, Explorer Jack in Lumbridge, or myself.

Every natural plant has powers locked within. Herblore is the art of unlocking these powers through potion-making.
You'll be able to brew potions to do just about anything. Most significantly, you can restore yourself when you feel depleted.
Every stage in the brewing of a potion will give you a little practise. You can also start out by cleaning herbs for use.

o: Tell me about the skills menu.

o.x: You have many skills you can train. The more you practice a skill, the better it gets. Higher skill levels unlock new activities: equipment to craft, locations to explore, quests to complete, and much more.
Perform actions associated with a skill to earn experience points (XP) in that skill. Earn enough XP and you'll gain a level in that skill.
Most skills start at level 1, and you unlock all their benefits by leveling the skill to 99. (Some skills have unlocks up to level 120.)
The bottom number next to a skill icon is your base level in that skill (un-modified by buffs or debuffs). It is used for most requirement checks.
The top number is your modified skill level (temporarily boosted or drained by skill buffs and debuffs - such as potions or spells). It is used for most skill checks.
Achieve 99 in all your skills to earn the coveted Max Cape!

nodes.title: What do you want to say?
o: Hey there. What is this place?

o.x: Hey there. What is this place?
Aha! Welcome to my obstacle course. Have fun, but remember this isn't a children's playground. People have died here.

This course starts at the ropeswings to the east. When you've done the swing, head across the slippery log to the building. When you've traversed the obstacles inside, you'll come out the other side. From there, head across the low
walls to finish. If you've done all the obstacles as I've described, and in order, you'll get a lap bonus.

o: What's wrong with the wall after the log balance?

o.x: What's wrong with the wall after the log balance?
The wall after the log balance? Nothing, really. I just put some tough material on it, giving people something to grip hold of.
Why would you do that?

b.x: So people like you can have a tougher route round this course.
Me and a mate got together and set up a new challenge that only the truly agile will conquer.
The extra stuff starts at that wall; so, if you think you're up to it, I suggest you scramble up there after the log balance.
Sounds interesting. Anything else I should know?
Nothing, really. Just make sure you complete the other obstacles before ya do. If you finish a full lap, you'll get an increased bonus for doing the tougher route.

If you manage to do 250 laps of this advanced route without a single mistake, I'll let you have a special item. I'll keep track of your lap tallies, so you can check how you're getting on with me any time.
So, players who are really agile can have a more challenging route. I suggest you stick to the normal route for now and come back when you are more experienced.
You need an Agility level of 90 or more to attempt Gunnjorn's improved course.

nodes.x: Greetings, your majesty.
Well hello there. What do you want?
I am looking for a quest!
Where did Zaros go?
Your predecessor has damaged the oubliette and released Raksha.
My predecessor?
The purple deity. He told me of your coming.
He told me of your strange new species.
He told me you can survive in this environment.
You must enter the inner chamber and stop Raksha.

o.x: Do you need anything else?
Wait, who are you?
I am the Keeper, the caretaker of the oubliette.
I maintain the apparatus that sustains and imprisons Raksha, the prisoner of this place.
I have maintained this vigil for many centuries, and the seals have never been broken until now.
Do you need anything else?
What about the creature?
What is it?
We call it Raksha. The One That Speaks.
But what is it? Zaros called it a 'shadow colossus'.
I do not know this term. Raksha is a unique being.
There were other dinosaurs, some truly titanic beings, but nothing like this.
Kerapac experimented on it. It had strange powers, which he cut from its strange flesh, but he could not remove its fundamental aspect.
Magic of a kind we had never seen before courses throughout its body.
It must be fed with that energy to remain alive - it does not generate it.
How was it captured?
We hunted it for weeks across the mainland.
When we cornered it, it poisoned me.
Transporting it here was a complex matter but the Kindra demanded it.
I am proud to say that there were no other fatalities.
Why did it stir now?
Kerapac somehow created a source of the energy it needs to survive.
After the curse, the supply of energy ceased.
We remained awake, the beast and I, for many more years, but eventually Raksha slipped into a coma, and I slumbered with it.
I do not know how long it has been since then.
Recently the supply resumed once more, drawing both of us into wakefulness, until it once more ceased.
Raksha would have slept once more if not for the purple deity's interference.
What about this place?
What is this place?
We are in the antechamber of the oubliette.
The oubliette was designed and built solely to contain Raksha.
Apparatus channels energy here to sustain the creature.
I was embedded here as its keeper, overseeing it.
What experiments were done here?
It is not my place to understand the details.
Syrtes, Aughra and Dactyl alike visited this place for their work.
When agitated, Raksha broadcasts hateful visions.
I remember one priest, Kranon, was quite touched by the experience.
He claimed that it had religious significance to him, though I cannot imagine what. I wonder what became of him.

b: If the player has completed Curse of the Black Stone:

b.x: He met a bad end.
Unsurprising.

o.x: Ask what you must.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Do you know anything about the 'Codex' Zaros mentioned?

o.x: Do you know anything about the 'Codex' Zaros mentioned?
I do not. He showed me the same visions he showed you.
We never learned the source of Raksha's powers.
Perhaps this Codex is linked to the same powers.
I know where it is.
Really?
We built the Archaeology Guild around it.
That seems unwise.

o: Can you tell me anything about your people?

o.x: Can you tell me anything about your people?
My people ruled this world, until the curse befell us.
I was interred here long beforehand, but I still felt it.
After that moment there was no interest in the oubliette or its prisoner. I have had no visitors.
Now the curse is gone, but my own vigil remains.
The purple deity told me that my civilisation is long gone.
Does that trouble you?
It makes no difference to me as long as Raksha remains contained.

o: Can you tell me anything about the city of Orthen?

o.x: Can you tell me anything about the city of Orthen?
This is our first city on this world.
There were other colonies but this was the capital.
There are archaeologists outside studying the ruins.
They would be fascinated to talk to you.
Are they like you? Are they able to survive in here?
No. Only I can do that. I'm kind of a special case.
Unfortunate.
What was your world like?
You have seen it yourself, have you not?
Well, this island is experiencing a... um... let's say time, uh, issue.
It's covered in jungle, but the rest of the world isn't.
What did the mainland look like in your time?
It was much like this island. Volcanoes, ferns, dinosaurs.
A young and vibrant world, the air sweet and clean.
Who do you want to know about?

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: What did Zaros tell you?
Who?
The, uh, purple deity.
He told me that I have been ripped from time.
He told me many thousands of years have passed, but I have stood still.
He told me the world is now under the control of lesser beings.
Do you know what he wanted?
He has removed part of the apparatus of the oubliette.
I instructed him not to but I could do nothing against a being of such potency.
He seemed confident that you specifically would deal with the aftereffects.

o: What can you tell me about yourself?

o.x: What can you tell me about yourself?
Once I was a hunter. It was I who captured Raksha and brought him here.
I was poisoned, but by Kerapac's machinations I was interred here.
The same apparatus that sustains Raksha sustains me.
We are linked, forever.

b: If the player has recovered Varanus's journals

b.x: You're Varanus!
I recovered your journals from the Orthen ruins.
Yes. That was my name.
But that's impossible. There's a huge sarcophagus with your name on it not far from here.
How are you alive?
Someone needed to contain Raksha. It had to be me.
Kerapac's methods can be extreme, but they were necessary.
I would not let the creature I died to capture go free, and I would not let another languish in this prison.
But the others would not have understood. They would have objected, maybe even damaged the oubliette.
An empty tomb was my final camouflage.

o: What's the big lever over there for?

o.x: What's the big lever over there for?

A balloon drop costs 1000 gold. For this, you get 200 balloons dropped across the whole of the party room. You can then have fun popping the balloons! Any items in the Party Drop Chest will be put into balloons as soon as you pull the lever. When the balloons are released, you can burst them to get at the items! For 500 gold, you can summon the Party Room Knights, who will dance for your delight. Their singing isn't a delight, though!

Any items in the chest will be dropped inside the balloons when you pull the lever.

Exactly! A word of warning, though. Any items that you put into the chest can't be taken out again, and it costs 1000 gold pieces for each drop party.
I wanna party!
I've won the Dance Trophy at the Kandarin Ball three years in a trot!

b: If the player has completed the Medium tasks in the Lumbridge and Draynor set and the rewards not claimed:

b.x: I've completed all the Medium Tasks in the Lumbridge set.
I can imagine! I'll expect you'll be wanting a reward, eh?
Yes, please.
It looks as though you've done a large amount of exploring, so I'll reward you well for your work.
Great! Thanks.
Ned hands you a brighter, gold version of the Explorer's Ring.
Now, as before, this ring will retain all the functions of your last two rings, however, this one is better.

Not only do you get a third and final run energy charge, but this particular ring was blessed by the Farming patch spirit herself! You might see her if you hang around Farming patches for a little while.
She gets anxious about people loitering or something odd like that.
Anyway, this ring allows you to travel on the dual-cabbageway!
Travel on the what?
Dual-cabbageway. It's a very secret method of travel not widely known across these lands. Using this ring will allow you to travel to the cabbage fields south of Falador.
That sounds amazing.
Well, you deserve it. Congratulations on completing all your tasks, my friend.
Wow, thanks!

You can also have this old lamp. I don't need it any more - I'm getting too old for adventuring myself. Now, if you should happen to lose that ring, you may come back to me to reclaim it. Anything else?

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: For completing the Lumbridge and Draynor set, you are presented with an explorer's ring.
This ring will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: You need to complete all Tasks in the set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward. Most of the Lumbridge set's Tasks are straightforward, although you might find some require quests to be started, if not finished.
To claim the Lumbridge set rewards, speak to Bob in Bob's Axes in Lumbridge, Explorer Jack in Lumbridge, or myself.

b.x: Thanks. Hmmm, do you know something? This rope has a funny smell.
Really?
Yes, It reminds me of...yaks. I was travelling in the Fremennik Isles recently and, do you know what? They made rope out of yak's hair.
What a coincidence?
There was a lady over there who sold wool, she said she traded rope for the wool.
Who would have thought it?
I don't think you make rope at all. I think you trade balls of wool for rope.

Oh, I confess. You have found the truth. I used to make the rope myself, but my fingers aren't as nimble as they used to be and so many people wanted my rope. nodes.x: Welcome, newcomer. I am the master chef, Lev. I will teach you how to cook food truly fit for a king.

Ha! You call THAT cooking? You're much more likely to burn your food if you cook on a log fire out in the open. You should cook at a blue whenever you can. Now, I am going to teach you the fine art of baking bread.
The master chef gives you an blue and a blue!
Fill the bucket with water from the sink, then use it to wet the flour into dough. Then bake the dough into bread on my range.

Ah, there's nothing like the smell of freshly baked bread. Be sure to carry a little food with you on your adventures. If you're injured in combat, eating is the best way to feel better. There are all sorts of food you can cook with the right ingredients and a high enough blue skill. Pies, cake, stews. You can even churn cream and butter or brew your own mead! You'll be a master chef before you know it. Now off to the next area with you!
Follow the path to the home of the quest guide.

Survival expert Hello there, newcomer. My name is Brynna. I'm going to teach you about skills you'll need to survive. You have many skills you can train. The more you practice, the better you get. I'll tell you about the blue, blue, blue and blue skills. Let's start with blue. Chop a tree until you get some blue in your backpack.
Survival expert Very good! Now let's put those logs to use. Light the logs in your backpack to make a fire.

Survival expert Well done! You can cook food on a fire. If you're ever injured, eating food will restore your health. We'll need something to cook. There are shrimp in the pond, so let's catch and cook some. Wherever you see bubbles in the water, there's probably some good fishing to be had there!

Survival expert Now you have caught some shrimp, let's cook it! You'll cook your shrimp on a fire. If your fire's gone out, chop a tree to get some logs and make a new fire. Then use the shrimp on the fire.

Survival expert Oh, you burnt your shrimp? Don't worry...that happens to everybody the first time. As you get more experience in blue, you'll burn food less often. Let's try again. First, fish some shrimps. Then use them on a fire. If your fire has gone out, chop some logs to make a new fire.

Survival expert Oh, well done! Now you have some food to eat whenever you feel poorly. I've taught you all I can about blue, blue, and blue. Open the gate, follow the path to the next area and talk to the master chef! He'll teach you more about blue!
Player Hi! My name's Player.

There are three basic ways to make money: skilling, combat and trading. Some people have work for an adventurer like you, and will reward you for completing quests. Many enemies will drop items when they die. You can sell them to a blue or on the blue in blue. By getting a high level in skills, such as blue, blue, blue or blue, you can create or gather your own items and sell them for pure profit. You can only carry so many items in your backpack. You can deposit items you want to keep and not sell into your bank.
You're nearly finished. The Prayer instructor would like to have a chat with you in the nearby church.

Mining instructor Greetings. My name is Dezzick and I'm a miner by trade. On either side of me are rocks containing tin and copper ore. Mine two tin ore and two copper ore. We're going to smelt and smith a melee weapon for you.

Mining instructor Great! A bronze pickaxe is the most inefficient pickaxe available, but is perfect for a beginner. The better the pickaxe you use, the faster you will get ore from the rock you're mining. Also, the better the pickaxe, the higher the blue level you'll require to wield it.

Mining instructor When you use a metal bar on an anvil, you'll choose the item you want to smith, as long as you have a high enough blue level and the correct number of bars. The higher your blue level, the better quality of metal you can work. You start off on bronze and work your way up as your blue skill increases. Start by smithing a bronze dagger at an anvil.
Mining instructor Excellent! Now that you have a melee weapon, you're ready to learn about combat.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: The Duel Arena has four arenas and a boxing ring where you can fight other players in a controlled environment. Duels are available to free players and members. We have our own dedicated hospital where we guarantee to put you back together, even if you lose. In between the arenas are walkways where you can watch the fights and challenge other players.

o: How do I challenge someone to a duel?

o.x: When you go to the arena, you'll go up an access ramp to the walkways that overlook the duels. From the walkways you can watch the fighting and challenge other players. You'll know you're in the right place as you'll have a 'Challenge' option when you right-click a player. There are two types of duels. There are 'Friendly' duels, in which you can duel against someone without staking anything, and there are 'Staked' duels, in which you can stake up to 50M coins.

o: What kind of options are there?

o.x: You and your opponent can offer coins as a stake. If you win, you receive what your opponent staked, but, if you lose, your opponent will get whatever coins you staked. You can choose to use rules to spice things up a bit. For instance, if you both agree to use the 'No Magic' rule, neither player can use Magic to attack. The fight will be restricted to Ranged and melee only. The rules are fairly self-evident, with lots of different combinations for you to try out!

o: This place looks really old. Where did it come from?

o.x: The archaeologists excavating the area east of Varrock have been working on this site as well. From these cliffs they uncovered this huge building. The experts think it may date back to the Second Age! Now that the archaeologists have moved out, a group of warriors, headed by myself, bought the land and converted it into the Duel Arena. The best fighters from around the world come here to fight!

Party items, you say?

o: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

o.x: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

b.x: Well, I don't know what to tell you really. This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin. So, we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to attack us.
South East of here is the castle of Lord Drakan, our master.
Lord Drakan? Who is that?
Ahhh... you must be new to these parts if you haven't heard of Lord Drakan! He's the lord of the land, and we all pledge allegiance to him.
In return for our allegiance, and the tithe of course, he keeps our land safe from any invaders and the Saradominists who want to kill us all.
Tithe? What do you mean?

Ah, well, in return for his protection, we have to give Lord Drakan a share of blood every week. If we don't have any to spare from our hunts, then we need to pick a member of the village to give their life in return for the blood so
that the tithe is fulfilled.
You mean you kill someone you know in order to meet the tithe?

That's right, but only if we haven't managed to get enough spare blood from our hunts. It's kind of severe if you look at it that way, but frankly, I think the price is fair in return for his protection and his tolerance of our
village. He could probably kill us all if he wanted us gone, so keeping on his good side is worth the sacrifice to us. Lucky we're not human really!
Why's that?
He hates humans! Apparently his brother Draynor is trapped in Misthalin, and adventurous little human wannabe-heroes keep trying to kill him!
He hates humans! Apparently long ago his brother Draynor was trapped in Misthalin and lost much of his powers, and was recently killed by some human!
Man, I'd hate to be a human around here, that's for sure. Drakan would really enjoy hunting them down and killing them!
Uh... thanks for the info...

Well, I don't know what to tell you really. This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin. So, we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to attack us.
Uh... thanks for the info...

o: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

o.x: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.
Hmmm? Why, who did you want to hear the gossip about?
Tell me what you know about Sbott the Tanner.

Hey, I won't hear a word said bad about that guy! He's an honest and hard-working wolf if I ever met one! He charges a lot for his job, but he's one of the best tanners I've ever seen - and I'm over four hundred years old! You
need stuff tanning, I recommend him!
Know anything interesting about Rufus the food seller?

Ah yeah... good old Rufus... He's kind of getting on in years and doesn't like to come out of his wolf form so often, but let me tell you this: that guy is a hunter through and through. You seen how much food he catches in a day? That

takes real dedication! Some of the young pups think that just because a wolf has a bit of grey in his fur then he's past it, but I've seen him put those pups to shame in a hunt! He's a real inspiration to us all!
Got anything to share about Barker the clothes seller?
Eh, I don't like the guy much, but you can't knock the quality of his stock. They're some fine quality threads that you can get yourself there.
What's wrong with him?
Eh... I can't really tell you to be honest. Something about the guy just gets my hackles up everything he opens his yap, know what I mean?
No, not really.
Lucky for you. I can't really explain it, I just don't like the guy. Does great clothes though, you got to give him that.
I bet you have some juicy gossip about Fidelio the general store owner.

That nut job? Oh sure, we all know about him. He was a real firebrand daredevil when he was much younger, always taking risks to make himself a quick buck... he got himself caught up in the smuggling trade, sneaking over the
border into Misthalin and pretending to be a human so he could buy exotic items to sell.
Exotic items? From Misthalin? Like what?
Oh man, you name it! Flour... buckets... tinderboxes... chisels... he could get the lot! He's been doing it so long now though, his nerves are shot.
Nowadays he's a disgrace, he can barely string a sentence together and jumps at his own shadow. Makes you feel ashamed to be a werewolf.

o: Tell me about the temple to the West.

o.x: Tell me about the temple to the west.
Well, I'm not old enough to remember the full story behind it, but it was a terrible day for our kingdom when it was built there.

Apparently Morytania had a once strong kingdom, with lands spreading far further west than they do today, and south into the desert, until the day when a sneak attack by the hated human forces who worship Saradomin burned
our villages and slaughtered our peoples in mass.
They then cursed the river, so that it would burn our kind should we touch it! Can you imagine? To make an entire river poisonous to us?

b.x: Luckily they seem to have calmed down somewhat recently, and tend to stay on their side of the river... but the wrong they have done my people will never be forgotten, and will never be forgiven. What is worse is

that they then had the nerve to build that gigantic statue on the river mouth to mock the slaughter of our people and the poisoning of our river! I can understand Lord Drakan's hatred for them even if I do not share it to his
extent.
Luckily, though, the curse has been lifted and we're free to travel into Misthalin for food. Most of us are too afraid of those evil humans, though, so we don't risk it.

o.x: So you hate humans too?
Absolutely! If I ever met one I would gobble him up where he stands! And then chew the bones for dessert!
Um, okay, thanks, bye.
Can I hear a story?
A story? Heh, well the only one I can think of right now is the one my dear old mammy told me as a pup...
Now how did it go... Ah yes!

Once upon a time a brave young wolf was walking through a forest, when he came upon a human dressed all in red. 'Aha!' he thought to himself, 'Here's a nice easy meal!' But the human talked to him, and he was always taught to
be a polite wolf, he spoke back to it.

Well, this cunning human told him that there was a better meal that would not run away in the house in the woods. As the brave young wolf could see that this human was not fully grown, he figured maybe he'd better get a better

meal at this house, so he ran as fast as his paws could carry him to the house the human told him about... inside he found an old human lying in bed, and although she was a little tough, as the human was older than he

thought, he had a good meal and decided to sleep it off in the house for awhile. He had not been asleep long though, when he was woken by a knocking at the door. The human in red had followed him to the house! Suspecting a human

trap, the brave young wolf put on the old humans clothes and jumped into the bed, so that he could pretend to be human and escape from this terrible trap! Well now, this human dressed in red came into the house, and pretended

to believe the brave wolf was really a human, and began to talk to him. But then the human started asking strange questions of the wolf, because the human knew that it was not a human at all! The brave young wolf decided to

try and escape, for it was only a young human, and not very strong, so the brave young wolf said he would eat the human if they did not let him escape! As he said this however, the human in red shouted at him: 'Aha! You

are a wolf!' and as the human shouted this another bigger human ran into the room from outside! This bigger human was much stronger and was carrying an axe, and the poor young wolf died in this terrible trap made for him by the
humans.
And do you know what the moral of this story is?
Um... no, not really.
It's 'Never trust humans' of course! My dear old mammy told me that story when I was a pup, and I'm still alive and well to tell it you today!
Pretty good story huh?
Um... yeah. It was great. Really.
Nothing thanks.
...I don't know why you talked to me if you don't want anything then...

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Tasks in the Fremennik Province set you get a pair of boots.
The more difficulty levels of the set you complete, the better the boots get - we'll tell you what they do when we give them to you.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Fremennik set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Fremennik set rewards, speak to Yrsa in Rellekka, Advisor Ghrim on Miscellania, or myself.

It provides the power to keep us ghosts from passing over into the next plane of existence.

You have to pour a bucket of ectoplasm into the fountain, a pot of ground bones, and then worship at the Ectofuntus. A unit of unholy power will then be created.

o: Where do I get ectoplasm from?

Necrovarus sensed the power bubbling beneath our feet, and we delved long and deep beneath Port Phasmatys, until we found a pool of natural ectoplasm. You may find it by using the trapdoor over there.
How do I grind bones?
There is a bone grinding machine upstairs. Put bones of any type into the machine's hopper, and then turn the handle to grind them. You will need a pot to empty the machine of ground up bones.

We disciples keep track of how many units of power have been produced. Just talk to us once you have generated some and we will reimburse you with the correct amount of Ectotokens.
How do I generate units of power?
You have to pour a bucket of ectoplasm into the fountain and then worship at the Ectofuntus with a pot of ground bones. This will create a unit of unholy power.

o: What happened to the folk of this town?

o.x: What happened to the folk of this town?
That's a long story, my friend, but you look like you have the time...
Do you know why ghosts exist?
A ghost is a soul left in limbo, unable to pass over to the next world; they might have something left to do in this world that torments them, or they might just have died in a state of confusion.
Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!
Why on earth would you do such a thing?
It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands. We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.
We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.
He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania. We had no choice but to agree to his demands.
As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands. Then, Necrovarus came to us.

He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest. Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.
Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power. He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.
Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm. He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.
Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working. But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.
Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely. Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.
The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.
We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.
We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.

So he's the god of this land. The desert is a harsh place; would that make him friendly or unfriendly? Or will you say, 'both', as usual?
You begin to understand. The desert is indeed harsh but it protects us from outsiders. Outsiders generally mean us no good, so he protects Menaphos through this harshness.
You humans have a saying, 'you have to be cruel to be kind', it seems to fit Tumeken.

The Menaphite pantheon is made up of four main deities.
Hang on... Pantheon? Deities? What are you talking about?
Sorry, I'm getting a bit ahead of myself. A pantheon is the collective name for the gods or deities of a group of people.
The main god which the Menaphites worship is called Tumeken. His wife, Elidinis, is the god of fertility and growth.
Does she have anything to do with the river?
That's very observant of you. The river Elid is named in her honour as it brings growth and life to the area during times of flood.
Some might also phrase it that she is named after the river, or that she is the river. It's a common area of theological debate.
So where do the other two main deities fit in?
Tumeken and Elidinis had two children: Icthlarin and The Devourer.
Tell me about The Devourer. With a name like that, it's no wonder she turned out to be messed up.
She was not always called such. She is thought of by her deeds, now, rather than her name.
The Devourer is the goddess of destruction; she craves only to destroy things.

Um, no, but it also creates heat.
Okay, we could have an overlong theological debate now, but to get to my point, recently - well, in the last age or so - The Devourer has taken to destroying humans.
And...?
Not just killing them; totally destroying them, body and soul. This has brought her into conflict with Icthlarin.
Ah hah, I see where this is going: the cats are used to protect the dead from The Devourer.
Indeed, The Devourer is terrified of cats for reasons I will not explain. Her followers - although few in number - are not, so I have to watch for them in my role as protector of cats.
I ensure the survival of cats and, for this service, Icthlarin grants me eternal life.
So, then, you are a follower of Icthlarin?
Nothing of the sort. As I've said before, I have no interest in humans. I look after my kind and, for that, Icthlarin looks after me.
So you protect the good cats against the follower of the bad god, the Devourer? That I can understand, at last.
No, it's not really that simple. Neither are either good or bad. Icthlarin is the god of the dead and takes care of the passing of souls from one plane to another.
He once even was worshipped by the Mahjarrat but they turned away from him in the Third Age to follow Zamorak.
Or maybe it was Zaros to whom they turned; it was a long time ago and not that important. Suffice to say, Icthlarin cares for the dead rather than creating them.

o: Tell me about the minor gods.

o.x: Tell me about Scabaras.
The Sect of Scabaras: a cult dedicated to the lesser deity Scabaras.
What's a lesser deity?

The Book of Light and Day says that Tumeken once fell into a deep sleep and dreamt for four days and four nights. The first night he slept and dreamt a good dream. He dreamt of a journey long and arduous. From the loins of his subconscious, Apmeken was born into reality, a physical manifestation of his dream. Tumeken continued to have pleasant dreams for a further two days and two nights. After each, a new deity came into being. On the fourth night, however, Tumeken dreamt a bad dream. He dreamt of himself and he dreamt of his increasing isolation caused by his extended sleep. This isolation sprung forth into the world and took on the form of Scabaras.
Okay, you could've just said...'a dream' or something. Where were we?

Yes, the followers of Scabaras used to be great architects of the subterranean. According to legend, they once planned to build a passage under the river Elid. No doubt Elidinis smote them because none of the followers were ever seen again.
That sounds interesting. Do they have any altars or temples left in the city?
Yes, there is a shrine dedicated to Scabaras in the Temple of the Lesser Gods in the north-east of this city. Jex there might know more about the minor deities.
Tell me about Het.
Het is the lesser deity concerned with strength and physical health. Sophanem is the city of the dead. so Het isn't worshipped much here.
Can you tell me any more?
Yes, there is a shrine dedicated to Het in the Temple of the Lesser Gods in the north-east of this city. Jex there should know more about Het.
Crondis is the lesser deity of resourcefulness and unassuming cunning. She has the head of a crocodile, which I don't see as being physically pleasant.
Coming from a mixed up creature like yourself, that's an interesting criticism. Any other information you can impart?
There is a place sacred to Crondis in the Temple of the Lesser Gods in the north-east of this city. Jex there should know more about this deity.
Apmeken has the head of a monkey and is the incarnation of friendship and jest. Good for a chat, but prone to exaggeration, by all reports.
You've met Apmeken?
That's for me to know and you to contemplate. By all accounts she's a feisty thing. It is said that, during Tumeken's Dream, she scampered upon Tumeken's very shoulders.
What did Tumeken do?
Turned her into a deity, of all things. I'm sure Jex at the Temple of the Lesser Gods can give more information, should you seek it.

o.x: I help the main man over there. He can get a bit cantankerous. Every now and then he'll just start attacking people without warning. I act as a sort of home help...
How do you mean, home help?

Well, sometimes he'll fly right off the handle and just start, you know, 'raising the dead' to do his 'bidding'. That kind of activity is just so anti-social, so it tends to attract a lot of hero types, you know!
Yes, yes, I know the sort. Full of themselves, aren't they?
Exactly! They come in shouting 'Have at thee!' and 'Death to you, evil one!' It's all a bit too dramatic for me, to be honest.
Anyway, he'll often end up getting killed, then nothing gets done around the house while he's awaiting his mortal return.
Mortal return? Sounds interesting.
Well, it's kind of interesting the first few times, but it's like falling off a bike...
What, you graze your knees a lot?
I was going to say that you soon get fed up with it. I guess it's one of those perks of the job, though, the ability to raise yourself from the dead.
You'd think he'd do better things with a gift like that, but all he does is get angry at people who come into his house without being invited, and then he's off again 'raising the dead'.
Thank you.

Have a nice day!

nodes.x: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!
Can you tell me more about the library?
Why, certainly, it is one of my favourite subjects!
I am Hugi, you see, I am the chief librarian here. Hugi, my parents named me that, it means 'personification of thought' in the ancient dwarvish tongue.
Quite like the name myself.
The books in this library have been collected for many centuries now, through various generous donations.
You'll find books dating from many different eras as well, such as the Era of Kings, the Rise of the Consortium and the Era of Prosperity, our current era.
How do these eras correspond with the Ages of the world?
Oh, they are quite different, and most of them take place in the Fourth Age.
Since we dwarves hid underground for a long time to sit out the wars that raged above the ground our history books differ slightly from those written by humans.
Thanks for the information!

o.x: Ssshhhh...
What can I help you with?
Help? What kind of help do you mean?
Looking for a book? A manuscript? Knowledge?
Oh, nothing in specific really.
I'll leave you to your browsing, then.
There is a lot of knowledge stored in this library, you know.
Oh, I'm sure.
And where do you come from, traveller?
From... out of town.
That I could've guessed.
We've been having more human visitors in the city recently, there is another one over there. Perhaps you'll want to talk to her.

nodes.x: Hello, can you help me?
Ssshhh, don't talk...
But I just want to ask you something.
Sssshhhh! Can't you read the sign?
What sign??
Don't be a cheeky human!
Ssshhhh.
Oh, that's nice, another human visitor to Keldagrim!
Indeed!
And what brings you to this city? Come to seek knowledge as well?
I think it's mostly fame and riches I'm after.
To each [his/her] own, I suppose.
Get out of my house!
Alright, alright, I was just leaving!
Come to visit my garden then, have you, human?

o.x: This is your garden?
No no, not quite. But I do look after it. It's the palace garden, you see. I keep it tidy, keep it living.
It's hard to grow much on these hard rocks deep beneath these mountains, you know.
I can imagine. Where do you get all your food from? Or even the soil for this garden?
We can grow a little food underground, but most of it comes from the extensive steamcart network that runs beneath the earth.
In the Era of Kings, many centuries ago, it was harder of course. Our steam technology was not developed as far yet and getting fresh supplies of food was always a problem.
Oh, I'm not boring you, am I?
Not at all! Please, go on!
Oh yes, as I was saying, it was difficult to make a decent living here. I'm afraid this garden was rather neglected during that time.
Why did you dwarves stay so deep under ground, then? Why not simply go above ground?
What, with the wars raging up there?
We dwarves went underground a long time ago, see. For a while the city of Keldagrim was completely cut off from the surface, simply waiting out the wars of the humans and the gods.
This made it hard, though, to determine when the wars above the ground were over. Perhaps Keldagrim had remained hidden for far too long.
Only when King Alvis heroically defended the city against an invasion of trolls did we dare to venture out and see how much the world had changed.
Of course, after that...
Ah well, enough history lessons I should say. I must really get back to my gardening.
Thanks for the info!
A little, yes. I don't really know what all this has to do with anything.
I suppose it doesn't, really, it's just the mumblings of an old dwarf.
Not really, no.
Oh, alright then.

Player.

Errr... I don't know... A quest, maybe?
[He/She] says [he's/she's] looking for [his/her] quest!
What makes [him/her] think [he/she] lost [his/her] quest in here?
What makes you think you lost your quest in here?
No no, I mean, do you have a task of some sort for me?
Now [he/she] says [he/she] wants a task!
Stop talking to that human and get back in here before I have a task for you!
No need to talk to me like that, Haera.
I'll talk to you in whatever way I like!
I think I hear someone calling my name in the distance...
What are you doing in our home?
I just came to ask you a question.
Hegir, why did you let this human into our home?
I didn't let [him/her] in, [he/she] let [himself/herself] in!
Now what do you want, human? Speak up, speak up!
I ehm, just wanted some information.
Well go ask someone else instead of barging into people's homes!
There's no need to be rude to the human, Haera dear.
Now don't you dear me. I'll do whatever I please.
I think this is my cue to leave...
Oh, leave an old dwarf in peace will you?
Why, what's wrong?
Ninety years down in the mines, and this is all I got out of it. All my life wasted away.
You've still got a nice house, don't you?
A crummy old house in East, that's all my life amounts to.
I'll leave you alone then.
Can you leave me alone please? I'm trying to get a bit of rest.
Do you mind? You're in my home.
I'm sorry, should I have knocked?
Very funny, human.
We can't all live in plush houses, you know. But that doesn't mean us mining dwarves don't work hard.
Where do you do your mining?
Normally the coal mine to the north. We need a lot of coal to keep our steam engines going, you know.
Can I do a bit of mining there as well?
I'm not sure, but as long as no one notices I don't think anyone is going to care.
Say, aren't you the human who got arrested here the other day, by the boat?
Yes, but we cleared up the whole situation.
Right, right.
Reinald Welcome to my home. I have a fine selection of home- made arm guards, as well as fine clothes imported from Thessalia in Varrock, if you're interested.

Well, first I came to this city just for the adventure and excitement, but then I knocked over this statue, you see. Well, I didn't really knock it over myself, I was on this boat.
A boat! Fascinating, go on!
Yes, well, this boatman was a bit rubbish, or there was something wrong with the ship, I don't know. And then I got arrested by the Black Guard.
Not the Black Guard!
Yes, and they took me to this Veldaban person, who pretended to be really angry but actually he was really nice and he asked me for my help.
During the Giant Dwarf:
After the Giant Dwarf:

No, it's just that no company has ever willingly left the Consortium before.
Companies have been forced out of the Consortium, then?
Oh yes. It hasn't happened for a long while now, but sometimes a company goes bankrupt. Or the value of the company becomes so low that it's relegated to being a minor company.
I see, thank you.
The Red Axe is defeated at last! I always knew they were up to no good - it was an ill omen that they left the city.

I'm afraid not.
Let me think for a moment...
No, I have nothing that I could possibly want doing. Try the shops of the market instead.

Perhaps!

b.x: There are things to kill all over the place! At your level, you might like to try wandering westwards to the Wizards' Tower or north-west to Gunnarsgrunn.
Non-player characters usually appear as yellow dots on your minimap, although there are some, such as the Lumbridge sage, that you won't be able to fight.
If you explore further afield, you may be able to find areas that are less crowded, but watch out for monsters that are stronger than you.
A monster's combat level is shown next to their 'Attack' option. If that level is coloured green, it means the monster is weaker than you. If it is red, it means that the monster is tougher than you.
Remember, you will do better if you have better armour and weapons and it's always worth carrying a bit of food to heal yourself.

o.x: How do I get cabbages?
There is a field a little distance to the north of here packed full of cabbages which are there for the picking.
How do I fish?
Fishing spots require different levels and equipment to use.
Depending on which fishing method you choose at a fishing spot, you may need additional items, such as bait, which you can buy at the fishing shop near Lumbridge market.
Your minimap has various icons showing the location of points of interest. This icon to the left shows where fishing spots are.
Where can I find meat?

I suggest you go and kill some chickens. The roads on either side of this river eventually go past a chicken farm. When you have killed some chickens, cook them. You could either make a fire or use a range.
Your minimap has various icons showing the location of points of interest. You can cook raw food by chopping down a tree and making a fire...
But you're much more likely to burn your food if you cook on a log fire out in the open. You should cook at a range whenever you can. There is a range at the southern end of this town.
As you increase your Cooking skill, you'll be less likely to burn food, and able to cook more advanced recipes that heal more life points.
Your minimap has various icons showing the location of points of interest. This icon to the left shows where Cooking ranges are.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: There are a few cheap weapons lying around in the world. For example, you can get an iron dagger if you cross the bridge and look in the little hut where some goblins live.
If it's not there, it probably means someone else has taken it. If you wait a while, a new one should appear. As you explore, you may find other weapons, too.

o: How do I make a weapon?

o.x: The Smithing skill allows you to make armour and weapons.
Lumbridge has a furnace, forge and anvil to the north of us, east of Lumbridge market.

Look for the left icon to locate a forge where you can heat and smith bars into equipment.

If you want a bigger choice, I suggest you head to one of the big cities.
If you follow the road east over the bridge and then head north, you will eventually reach Varrock, where you can buy all manner of things. You can use the world map to help you find your way.

o: I'd like to know about something else.
I'd like to know about something else.

o.x: There are many ways to make money in the game. I would suggest either killing monsters or doing a trade skill such as Smithing or Fishing.
Many enemies will drop items when they die. You can sell them to a general store or on the Grand Exchange in Varrock.
By getting a high level in skills, such as Cooking, Mining, Smithing or Fishing, you can create or gather your own items and sell them for pure profit.
Please don't try to get money by begging off other adventurers. It will make you unpopular. Nobody likes a beggar. It is very irritating to have other adventurers asking for your hard-earned cash.

Look for the left icon to locate a forge where you can heat and smith bars into equipment.
Your minimap has various icons showing the location of points of interest. This icon to the left shows where Mining sites are.
I suggest you go and mine some ore; find the Mining symbol - with the guide symbol near it - in the swamp south of here.

o: Where can I find a bank?

o.x: You'll find a bank upstairs in Lumbridge Castle - go right to the top - or there's a bank chest at Lumbridge market to the north.
Your minimap has various icons showing the location of points of interest. This icon to the left shows banks where you can store your items.
You can only carry so many items in your backpack. You can deposit items you want to keep and not sell into your bank.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: I am Phileas, the Lumbridge Sage. I am here to give information and directions to new adventurers.
In times past, people came from all around to ask me for advice. My renown seems to have diminished somewhat in recent years, though. Can I help you with anything?

o: Tell me about the town of Lumbridge.

o.x: Lumbridge is one of the older towns in the human-controlled kingdoms. It was founded over two hundred years ago towards the end of the Fourth Age. It's called Lumbridge because of this bridge built over the River Lum.
The town is governed by Duke Horacio, who is a good friend of our monarch, King Roald of Misthalin.

o: Where can I find more information?

o.x: What you'll want is the RuneScape Wiki! There's information and guides on almost everything, all easily searched and it's even written and maintained by players.
You can search the wiki with the /wiki command or by pressing the Wiki button in your local chatbox.
Good adventuring, traveller.

nodes.x: Greetings, Player.

b.x: Wait, wait, wait. Before we get started, are you here about my archaeology collection?
Do you want to talk about Archaeology?

nodes.x: So you're a wise old man, huh?
Less of the 'old' man, if you please!
But yes, I suppose you could say that. I prefer to think of myself as a sage.
So what's a sage doing here?

I've spent most of my life studying this world in which we live. I've strode through the depths of the deadliest dungeons, roamed the murky jungles of Karamja, meditated on the glories of Saradomin on Entrana,
and read dusty tomes in the Library of Varrock.
Now I'm not as young as I used to be, I'm settling here where it's peaceful.
It's a pity about that vampyre that keeps attacking the village. At least Saradomin protects me.
That's quite an exciting life you've had.
Exciting? Yes, I suppose so.
Now I'm here, perhaps I could offer you the benefit of my experience and wisdom?
Thanks! So how can you help me?
Well, I imagine you've gathered up quite a lot of stuff on your travels. Things you used for quests a long time ago that you don't need now.
If you like, I can look through your bank and see if there's anything you can chuck away.
Alternatively, you can bring items here and show them to me. If I see that it's something you don't need, I'll let you know. I might even be willing to buy it.
So you'll help me clear junk out of my bank?
Yes, that's right. Or I'd be happy to chat with you about the wonders of this world!

Well, if my concentration is broken while keeping this gate open, then, if we are lucky, everyone within a one mile radius will either have their heads explode, or will be consumed internally by the creatures of the Abyss.

If we are unlucky, then the entire universe will begin to fold in upon itself, and all reality as we know it will be annihilated in a single stroke. So leave me alone!
What are you doing here?

o.x: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.
The latest idea from the great Ali Morrisane. Desert travel will never be the same again.
So how does it work?
The carpet or the whole enterprise?
Tell me about how the carpet works.
I'm not really too sure; it's just an enchanted rug really, made out of special Ugthanki hair. It flies to whatever destination its owner commands.
Are they for sale then?
Do you think I'm mad? Do you think that Ali Morrisane would throw his magic carpet monopoly away?
Well, perhaps if I offered the right price.

Not a hope. Could you imagine the mess there'd be if people were constantly zooming through Al Kharid and Pollnivneach? It would be chaos. This way, we can keep the carpet traffic outside towns and other busy places.
I suppose getting stuck in a carpet jam could get a bit tiresome.
Just think of the friction burns you would get if you were in a carpet crash.
Can I help you with anything else?
Tell me about the enterprise.
It's quite simple really. Ali Morrisane has hired myself and a few others to set up carpet stations at some of the desert's more populated places and run flights between the stations.
So why has he limited the service to just the desert.

Why is that?

You're right, I guess. How's the business going?

Can I help you with anything else?

b: If the player is at the Bedabin Camp:

b: If the player is at Uzer:

b.x: You might not realise it, but this is quite a busy station.

b: If the player is at north Pollnivneach:

Malak. Not the most remarkable of names, not that it matters, you see everyone in town knows me as Flash.
Really?
No.
Right.

nodes.title: Select an option

o.x: How do I brew ales?
Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
How do I brew cider?
First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush. Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.

o.x: What are urns?
You don't know what an urn is? Inconceivable!
Urns are big, magical pots. You keep them in your bag, and they collect scraps and wastage while you perform activities that are related to that urn.
For example, a fishing urn collects guppies while your attention is on larger catches.
Once it's full, you can teleport the urn to me!
Sweet little guppies...

o.x: Why would I want to give you any urns?

You send me an urn, I reward you with know-how regarding the skill type of your urn. Some might call it...gaining experience.
That's a strange way to phrase it.
How do I make urns?
Oh, just use some soft clay on the pottery wheel and then fire the results in the pottery oven downstairs. Urns are big, so you'll need two batches of clay per urn.
Before you can start gathering scraps in your urn, you must attach a rune to it. This dissipates when you teleport the urn to me. Then I gather the precious, wonderful materials.
If you get stuck, just show me where you've got to and I'll give you some advice. You can also hand full urns to me in person, if you'd prefer.

Weaker demons leave impious ashes behind. Scarier demonic beasties leave accursed ashes, and the most dangerous demons leave infernal ashes. Scrum-diddly-umptious.
With lower Crafting levels, you are able to create impious urns, which collect impious ashes. Get your skill level up and you'll be able to make urns that collect a smorgasbord of ash types.

Ah, fishing urns! These collect my favourite little fish: guppies! All you need to do is keep the urn in your bag when you are fishing, and it'll gather up the delicious little guppies each time you make a catch.
Cracked fishing urns, made with lower Crafting levels, only collect guppies when fishing at level 10 or below. Higher level urns collect the brave guppies that swim around higher level fish.
When you are a master crafter, you will be able to make decorated fishing urns. These collect guppies from any kind of fish that you can think of!
Cooking urns collect lip-smacking food scraps while you are cooking on a fire or range.
Cracked cooking urns, made with lower Crafting levels, collect food scraps from meals that require a Cooking level of 10 or below.
Decorated cooking urns, made at the very highest Crafting levels, collect scraps from even the most complex of meals. These scraps are integral to my experiment!
Experiment?
Who told you about my experiment? Whatever you've heard is a lie!
Magical mining urns! These collect slivers of ore from the rocks you mine.
Cracked urns, made at the lower end of the Crafting scale, will magnetically attract slivers of ore that require a Mining level of 1.
Higher quality urns collect slivers of ore from higher level ores. When you're skilled enough to make decorated mining urns, you'll gather slivers from any ore that you could swing a pickaxe at!
Smelting urns collect metal scraps while you smelt bars.

Lower level urns only collect metal scraps from bars that require a Smithing level of 1. The highest level urns collect metal scraps from any bar, high level or low level, 'cept for chocolate bars. Trust me, I've tried.
A note to you: I prefer better quality metal scraps. They contribute a more distinctive taste to my delicious experiment.
Woodcutting urns! Wonderful things! These collect tasty woodchips when you chop wood.
While you are a crafter at lower levels, you will only be able to make cracked urns. These collect woodchips while you chop wood up to a Woodcutting level of 10.
When you are a master of the crafting art, you'll be able to make decorated woodcutting urns that collect from even the hardiest of logs.
Woodchips from magic trees make my lips tingle. I thought you'd like to know.
Wonderful divination urns! Wonderful things! These collect memory fragments.
While you are crafting at lower levels, you will only be able to make cracked urns. These collect memory fragments up to a Divination level of 10.
When you are a master of the crafting art, you'll be able to make decorated divination urns that collect from even the greatest of memories.
You might also want to know that these will collect extra special fragments when you deposit memories into a crater!
Runecrafting urns collect rune remnants when utilising rune essence.
Lower level urns will collect remnants from anything up to level 9. The highest level urns collect remnants from almost anything!

o.title: Ask about...

o.x: Ah hunter urns! These ones collect integument iotas from little critters.
Cracked urns, made at the lower end of the Crafting scale, will be able to collect iotas from creatures that require a Hunter level of 11.
If you manage to catch some of the big guys, you'll find my urns filling up in no time!
Farming urns collect the left over cuttings when farming.
The lowest level urns will work for anything up to level 12.

o: I have a few questions about urns in general.

o.x: That's all, thank you.
Good bye!

nodes.x: What do you want from me outerlander? It is our policy not to associate with those not of our tribe.

nodes.title: What would you like to ask about?

o.x: Where is your chieftain? I find it highly discriminatory to refuse to talk to someone on the grounds that they are not part of your tribe.

I don't rightly understand your speech outerlander, but my loyalty is with Chieftain Brundt. He resides in our long hall; it is the large building over there, you should speak to him for he speaks for us all.
So what are you doing here?
This should not concern you, outerlander. I am awaiting other Fremenniks to join me on an expedition to Waterbirth Island.

It is a small crescent-shaped island just north-west of here, outerlander. We have many legends about it, such as the tale of the broken sky, and the day of the green seas. The reason I am travelling there is more serious Fremennik business, however. I doubt an outerlander would be interested.

b.x: Hey, scary barbarian type guy, think I can join you on this expedition?
An outerlander join us on an honoured hunt??? Well.... I guess... I might be able to allow you to join us, although it is a breach of many of our customs...
Oh, pleeeeease? I really LOVE killing stuff!

Well... I remain unconvinced that it would be wise to allow an outerlander to join us in such dangerous battle, but your enthusiasm seems genuine enough... I will allow you to escort us, but you must pay me a sum of money first.
What? That's outrageous, why charge me money? And, uh, how much does it cost me?

Ah, the outerlanders have stolen from my people for many years, in this way you can help my community with a small amount of money... Let us say... 1000 coins. Payable in advance, of course. For this I will take you to Waterbirth Island on my boat, and will bring you back here when you have had your fill of the hunt. Assuming you are still alive to wish to leave, of course.

o.x: So do you have the 1000 coins for my service, and are you ready to leave now?

b: If the player does not have enough coins:

b.x: You can not afford that.
Ah, outerlander... I go beyond my duty to allow you to accompany me, and you attempt to swindle me out of a reasonable fee? This is no way even for an outerlander to behave...

b: If the player has enough coins:

b.x: Leaving Rellekka for Waterbirth Island.

b: First time travelling to Waterbirth Island:
If the player has not completed The Fremennik Trials:

As you wish. Come and see me when your bloodlust needs sating.
Hey, I have to say, that's a fine looking hat you are wearing there.
It is actually a helm, outerlander, but the sentiment is appreciated nonetheless.
Wow, you Fremenniks sure know how to party. Well, see ya around.
Actually, I don't think I have anything to speak to you about...

nodes.x: Hello there.
Hey there, buddy. You're an outerlander, huh? I'm not really supposed to talk to you.
Why not?
I dunno buddy. Some stupid tradition or other. We're always told not to talk to outerlanders unless the Chieftain has allowed it.
The Chieftain? Who is that?
His names Brundt, buddy. He's a real boring guy. You can find him in the long hall there.
Can you take me to see him?
Sorry buddy, I'm not allowed into the long hall. Don't worry, he's easy to spot. He's the one in the fancy helmet. Oh, and he only has one eye.
He's a cyclops?
Nah, nah, nah... He just wears an eyepatch! Well, see ya around buddy!
Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

Not much really... I run a local shop which earns me a few trading sticks, but that's about it. I keep myself to myself really.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: What are trading sticks?
They're the local currency Bwana, it's used in Tai Bwo Wannai, there's usually some odd jobs that need doing around the village which you could do to earn some trading sticks.
Or, if you have something which the local villagers might like, you could sell it to me and I'll pay you for it in trading sticks.

o.x: What sort of things do the local villagers like?

Gnome cocktails! It's amazing but we all just love them! Luckily I've managed to get stocks of the gnome made cocktails and I supply those to my favourite customers. However, many of the customers really like the cocktails
made by the adventurers passing through this way. If you ever happen to have any, bring them my way! I'll give you a good deal on it that's for sure!
How did the villagers ever get to try any gnome cocktails?

I think it was that gnome pilot who crashed his glider, perhaps he had a little mini-bar on board? Come to think about it, you'd expect the little guy to get his stuff together and move on out of here wouldn't you? He must love the jungle to have stayed here so long!

o: I want to ask another question.

Yes, it's the Tai Bwo cooperative... catchy name huh! We sell a few local village trinkets and tools. Also, there are a few items that we're actually looking to stock for the locals' sake.
If you happen across any of them please bring them to me, I'll pay a good price for them. I'm sure you'll find the prices very reasonable.

Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Cooperative
Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Drinky Store
None thanks...

Why, what's the difference?

I think it may just be that they're made fresher, or there is a slight twist in the flavour of the drink, you know, a little more of this, a little less of that, it all adds up and makes for an interesting tipple!

I want to ask another question.

Sure, what do you want to ask?
Ok, thanks.

Bwana, if anyone else asks me that question today, I'll explode! Go and ask Murcaily!
I'm just enjoying the sunshine, Bwana. Try asking Murcaily.
Well, I think that there's some work to be done...perhaps Murcaily can help you. He usually tends to the hardwood grove to the east of Trufitus' hut.
Sorry Bwana, I'm already busy, why not go and talk to Murcaily! He's around the village somewhere.
Ok, thanks.

No silly, it's someone who deals with preservatives and dyes. I didn't really enjoy the preservatives side of the things so I've chosen to deal solely in dyeing.

It's a dyeing trade! Oh gosh I'm sorry that was a truly dreadful joke.

Did you see who teleported you to Falador?
