o.x: Oooh.

nodes.x: Hello there. How can I help you today?

o.x: Me? What do you want to know?

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: I am the palace librarian.
Ah. That's why you're in the library, then.
Yes.
Although I would probably be in here even if I didn't work here. I like reading.
Some day, I hope to catalogue all of the information stored in these books, so all may read it.

o: Do you have anything to trade?

o.x: Only knowledge.
How much do you want for that, then?
No, sorry, that was just my little joke. I'm not the trading type.
Oh, well.

o: Do you know any heroic stories?

o.x: Do you know any heroic stories?
Yes, I do.
Years ago, a terrible creature slew King Roald's betrothed and terrorized the people. Varrock sent an embassy to Morytania to open a dialogue with Drakan about it.
What happened?
It didn't end happily. Poor Gar'rth, we didn't know he was... Well, it would be unfair for me to say. That's his secret, not mine.
What about the terrible creature?
It was brought to justice, but not before claiming many innocents.
Go on, tell me about Gar'rth.
Another time, perhaps? I have work to do.
Hmpf!

b: If the player has completed medium task set, but not claimed it yet:

b.x: I've finished all the Medium Tasks in the Varrock set.
Really? How extraordinary! Well, that certainly is a worthy achievement indeed.
Thanks. Was there a reward?
A reward? Well, yes, I suppose I can help you there.
Reldo takes the Varrock armour and attaches some more plate metal to it, filling it out to look like a proper suit of armour. He etches some words into the armour, which glows slightly before fading.

I have enhanced your body armour with a spell. You now have a chance to double your bars when smelting, ores when mining and progress when smithing mithril and adamant. I can also change your Varrock Teleport spell so that it takes you to the Grand Exchange, if you'd find that more convenient. As an extra reward, I have also given you a magical lamp to help with your skills.
Wow, thanks! What if I lose the armour?
Oh, that's not a problem. You can come back to see me and I'll get you another set.

b: If the player has lost their Varrock armour 2:

b.x: Don't tell me you lost the armour I gave you?
Yes, sorry about that. I don't know what happened to it.
Oh, well, no harm done. Fortunately, I have another set here - we get quite a lot of Varrock explorers these days, you know.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Varrock set, you are presented with some body armour.
This armour will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?

You need to complete all Tasks within a particular difficulty set, then you can claim your reward. Most of the Varrock set's Tasks are straightforward, though you might find some require quests to be started, if not finished.
To claim your Varrock set reward, speak to Rat Burgiss south of Varrock, Vannaka in Edgeville Dungeon, or me.

o: Could I buy a spare of the reward?

o.x: Varrock armour 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
You're handed another Varrock armour 1.
No thanks.
Varrock armour 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
You're handed another Varrock armour 2.
No thanks.
Varrock armour 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
You're handed another Varrock armour 3.
No thanks.
Varrock armour 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,00 coins.
You're handed another Varrock armour 4.
No thanks.

nodes.x: Hello there! I am known as the Makeover Mage! I have spent many years researching magicks that can change your physical appearance.
I call it a 'makeover'. Would you like me to perform my magicks on you?

o.x: Tell me more about this 'makeover'.
Why, of course! Basically, and I will explain this so that you understand it correctly.
I use my secret magical technique to melt your body down into a puddle of its elements.
When I have broken down all components of your body, I then rebuild it into the form I am thinking of.
Or, you know, something vaguely close enough, anyway.
Uh...that doesn't sound particularly safe to me.
It's as safe as houses! Why, I have only had thirty-six major accidents this month!
So, what do you say? Feel like a change?
Sure, do it.
You, of course, agree that if by some accident you are turned into a frog you have no rights for compensation or refund.
Makeover Mage

b.x: Two arm, two legs, one head; it seems that spell finally worked okay.
Hmm, you didn't feel any unexpected growths on your head just then, did you?
Er, no?
Good, good! I was worried for a second there.
Whew! That was lucky.
What was?
Nothing! It's all fine! You seem alive anyway.
Woah!
What?
You still look human!

Yes please!
Well then, if you hold still this shouldn't hurt too much.
You didn't mention it was going to hu-
Ow!
Wow! I sound so different, thanks!
Glad I could help. Was there anything else I could help with?
On second thoughts, I'll pass.
Is there anything else I could help you with?

I also have some speciality colours for you should you wish to take advantage of them.

Furthermore I have some speciality potions avaiable for you to purchase should you want to take on a more vibrant colour. I call them 'Chameleon extract', they are quite handy if that is what you are after but they are one use potions.
So, what do you say? Feel like a change?

o.title: Select an Option

Gosh, how did you escape?
Arrr, ye see, he made one mistake! Before he sailed away, he gave me a bow and one arrow so that I wouldn't have to die slowly.
So I shot him and took my ship back.
Right...

Ok Bwana, here's the deal. There are three gem bladed machete types, in order of quality and hacking proficiency, they're ordered from low to high as follows.
Opal bladed machete - Safta doc needs the following to make this machete : 3 opals - cut or uncut, 1 gout tuber plant and 300 trading sticks.
Ok Bwana, if you want to order the machete, I need 3 opals, either cut or uncut, 1 gout plant tuber and 300 trading sticks please.
Jade bladed machete - Safta doc needs the following to make this machete : 3 - cut or uncut, 1 gout tuber plant and 600 trading sticks.
Ok Bwana, if you want to order the Jade machete, I need 3 jades, either cut or uncut, 1 gout plant tuber and 600 trading sticks please.
Red Topaz bladed machete - Safta doc needs the following to make this machete : 3 - cut or uncut, 1 gout tuber plant and 1200 trading sticks.
Ok Bwana, if you want to order the Red Topaz machete, I need 3 , either cut or uncut, 1 gout plant tuber and 1200 trading sticks please.

o: Safta Doc: Ok Bwana, come back when you have them.

o.x: So Bwana, do you like the look of the machetes?

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: Why do you need gems?
They're tougher than just metal on its own, plus it's the only such resource naturally available in this region.

o: Why do you need a gout plant tuber?

o.x: Why do you need a gout plant tuber?

It's one of the harder to find resources which I mix with other ingredients in order to bind the ground down gem dust to the surface of the metal bladed machete. You can sometimes, if you're lucky, find the plant if you hack away at the jungle around here. You'll need to find a way to dig up the tubers though, they're the important part of the plant.
Why is it so expensive?

Expensive bwana, it's quite reasonably priced if you ask me. I can make it cheaper than Gabooty charges for it, that's for sure. And after all, I have to earn a living around here as well you know, I have children to feed!

o: Let me see the machetes again.

o.x: Ok, thanks.

o: No thanks, but I'd like to ask another question.
No thanks, I have to go.

o.x: No thanks, I have to go.

o: Is there anything interesting to do here?

o.x: Is there anything interesting to do here?
Bwana, if anyone else asks me that question today, I'll explode! Go and ask Murcaily!
I'm just enjoying the sunshine, Bwana. Try asking Murcaily.
Well, I think that there's some work to be done...perhaps Murcaily can help you. He usually tends to the hardwood grove to the east of Trufitus' hut.
Sorry Bwana, I'm already busy, why not go and talk to Murcaily! He's around the village somewhere.
Ok, thanks.

o.x: Bank

What is this place?
This is a branch of the Bank of Gielinor. We have branches in many towns.

o.title: What would you like to say?

o.x: And what do you do?
We will look after your items and money for you. Leave your valuables with us if you want to keep them safe.

o: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?

o.x: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?
Yes we did, but people kept on coming into our branches outside of Varrock and telling us that our signs were wrong. They acted as if we didn't know what town we were in or something.

nodes.x: Hello, dearie! Were you wanting to collect a costume, or is there something else I can do for you today?

nodes.title: What would you like to say?

o.x: I may be able to find your lost ghostly costumes, or I have my costume store. Which do you want?
(Reclaim interface opens.)
Some of these costumes even come with a free emote!
Just buy one piece of the mime or zombie costumes and I'll show you all of the relevant moves.
Iffie's Random Costume Shop
Aren't you selling anything?
Oh, yes, but only costumes. Thessalia sells some other clothes and runs the makeover mage service.

o: I just came for a chat.

o.x: I just came for a chat.
Oh, I'm sorry, but I'll never get my knitting done if I stop for a chit-chat with every young [lad/lass] who wanders through the shop!
You should go and see my sister, Elsie, upstairs in Varrock Church; she's always ready for a good natter.

b: Sergeant Damien may say any one of the following at random

b.x: Someone should whip these recruits into shape.
Yes, sir!
Are you eyeballin' me, [boy/girl]?
No, sir!
What a snivelling pile of maggots!
Yes, sir!
What is your major malfunction?
I wasn't aware I had one, sir!
It's like a circus in here!
Yes, sir!

nodes.x: At ease, soldier; I'm not on duty.
Then what are you doing here, Sergeant Damien, sir, if I might ask?
Balthazar's a buddy of mine, from my old unit. After the war - you know, THE war - old BB retired to civilian life; set up this little carnival of his.
Now my drill sergeant days are behind me, he offered me a job here as a roustie.
A roustie? What's that?
A roustabout, boy; a roughneck; a handyman!
I keep all the equipment in good repair, do all the manual labour, and - best of all - I get to keep the audience in line! There's no better work for an old soldier like me.
Run faster! Faster!
Excuse me?
Oh, sorry, I didn't notice you there.
I take it you're a coach?
That I am. Now get to the point, I'm very busy!

nodes.title: Select an option
o: What's the History of Gnome ball?

o.x: What's the history of Gnome ball?
Be more precise, stranger.

o.title: Select an option

o.x: How did it all start?
Strangely enough, by accident.
Accident?
Don't interrupt!
Sorry.
A great many years ago, before I was even born, there were two young Gnomes. Brothers to be exact.
They were always arguing with each other over the most trivial things - who was the faster runner or who was the tallest.
One day they were up at the swamp throwing stones at the toads.
As you do.
Yep. You know nothing tastes better than toasted toad?
Anyway, they decided to compete to see who could kill the most toads. This gradually became a daily game, to which they invited friends and family to join in. It all evolved from there.
Creating a playing arena, making up teams and leagues.
Interesting.
Anything else?

o: What is the ball made from?

o.x: What is the ball made from?
Toads of course
Toads?
What with the swamp nearby, and their robust skin, there is nothing better to stretch over some common sand.
I'd never have guessed.
Well, of course. You humans know nothing! Anything else?
Those nets are strange.
Ah, made from the finest thread in all the land.
And that is?
Gnome hair.
You're kidding, right?
I have no time for jokes. It's a serious matter, we go through plenty of nets every day.
So that's why you don't see many Gnomes with long hair?
Exactly.
The world makes sense at last.
Anything else?
Are there any special tactics?
Well of course, like what?
How about passing?
There's the good old one-two tactic.
And that is?
You don't know anything do you? You pass the ball onto a team mate, giving him all the attention of your opposition, and giving you the chance to run further ahead.
Then what?
Well, he passes back to you and you've made an advantage. It's useful in a variety of situations!
I'll remember that one.
Anything else?
How about teamwork?
Well, don't forget that you can block the opposition whilst a team mate has the ball. Very useful if you want to stop or slow down anyone approaching him.
Block for team mates. Got it.
Anything else?
What about my personal physique?
You'd look better if you were shorter.
I mean in regards to scoring more goals!

I see. Your agility is important if you want to avoid being tackled, so that would be a good attribute to improve. Also many Gnomes say that being able to attack well with a ranged weapon makes you better at scoring goals.
I suppose I should go away and work on those skills.

Yes, although playing the game itself will improve these skills too. Also you should remember that your distance from the goal affects your chance of scoring, so get close enough and your ranged ability won't matter as much.
Any information would be appreciated!
Hmm, some general facts?
Please!
OK. Have you noticed the different colour clothes for your opposing Gnomes?
Nope.

The colours correspond to their skill level. The red ones are the professionals. They've been playing since before you were born! The orange ones are in the middle of their careers, whereas the yellow players know very little. Just like you!
Thanks... Anything else?
It's always good to get a group of friends to play with you. That way you can score goals more easily, and if you take it in turns to score the goals you'll all reap the rewards.
Does the game bring fame?
You mean you've never heard of Speedy Sam The Striker or Norda 'Steal Arms' van Druman?
Afraid not.
Not even Great Thunder Legs MacKnee?
Nope.
Well, they're all richer than you'll ever be!
Good for them.
Indeed, anything else?
Yawn.
I beg your pardon?
Erm... thanks, catch you later.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: What happened to you?

b: Without a Ring of Charos (a) equipped:

b.x: That be a tale so heart-wrenchin' that it has so far wrenched the hearts from over a dozen sturdier men than thee!
A tale of such woe that none but the stoniest hearts can hear it without sheddin' a single, poignant tear...
And I'll never tell ye, not even if ye wore an item, such as a ring, with powers of mind control!
What if I said please?
Hmmmm...well alright...
Wait, no!
Get goin' landlubber before I take my splintery foot to yet behind!

b: With a Ring of Charos (a) equipped:

b.x: Well ye seem like a [lad/lass] that can handle such a tale...so I'll tell ye...
Well, it all starts with this albatross...
Wait, never mind, I'll skip forward a bit.
Are you sure?
I have to [lad/lass], Cap'n Donnie will flay what little is left of me if I told ye.
But anyway, I got recruited to the zombie pirates along with the rest of the crew in an unspecified incident involvin this albatross.
We was sailin' along happily, and I was partakin' of a little 'rum' in the crows nest.
Well, we hit either a really rough wave or some rocks.
Twas kind of hard for me to tell which, as I was well out of it by then!
Regardless, I toppled from the crows nest into the water.
Is that how you got so badly injured?
No [lad/lass]!
What happened next was that I discovered a new, previously uncharted reef of hard, spiky coral.
I made a mental note of its location, and to this day it is still marked on our fleet's charts as Lukes Reef.
I managed to grab a hold of our ship, the Inebriated, as it passed overhead.
And then I discovered another, taller, spikier reef of even sharper and more painful coral.
To this day it is still marked on our fleet's charts as The Other 50% Reef.
Owwwwwwwww...
It gets worse...
When they hauled what was left of me on deck, they dropped me onto the floor while they decided what to do with me.
Bear in mind this would be on a ghost ship, the planks of which sweat a thick mixture of stagnant water...and pure salt crystals.
Oh...my...god...
But on the good side, all my thrashin' and pained squealin' settled the matter in the Captain's mind, and he had the shipwright carve me half a body out of his Witchwood Planks.
Witchwood? What's that?

You know, the little guys...the ones that aren't dwarves.

o.x: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.
The latest idea from the great Ali Morrisane. Desert travel will never be the same again.
So how does it work?
The carpet or the whole enterprise?
Tell me about how the carpet works.
I'm not really too sure; it's just an enchanted rug really, made out of special Ugthanki hair. It flies to whatever destination its owner commands.
Are they for sale then?
Do you think I'm mad? Do you think that Ali Morrisane would throw his magic carpet monopoly away?
Well, perhaps if I offered the right price.

Not a hope. Could you imagine the mess there'd be if people were constantly zooming through Al Kharid and Pollnivneach? It would be chaos. This way, we can keep the carpet traffic outside towns and other busy places.
I suppose getting stuck in a carpet jam could get a bit tiresome.
Just think of the friction burns you would get if you were in a carpet crash.
Can I help you with anything else?
Tell me about the enterprise.
It's quite simple really. Ali Morrisane has hired myself and a few others to set up carpet stations at some of the desert's more populated places and run flights between the stations.
So why has he limited the service to just the desert.

I don't think Ali is prepared to take on Gnome Air just yet. Their gliders are much faster than our carpets. Besides that, I think we are in the short-haul business, something that would only work in harsh conditions like the desert.
Why is that?

I suppose because people would just walk. Getting lost isn't too much of a problem generally, but it's a different matter when you're in the middle of the Kharidian Desert with a dry waterskin and no idea which direction to go in.
You're right, I guess. How's the business going?
Not too bad. The hubs are generally quite busy, but the stations in Uzer and the Bedabin Camp could do with a bit more traffic.
A growth market, I guess.
Can I help you with anything else?

o: No, but I had some questions.

o.x: I have some other questions.
I'll help you as much as I can.

Such ignorance! I suppose I should come to expect it. People are forgetting the old ways of the desert around here. But then.. do those bureaucratic fools in Menaphos expect! If they're going to take so long to send
us a new priestess of She. Do you know we haven't had one for five years now!

She! Otherwise known as Elidinis, Goddess of growth and fertility, Lady of the river, Wife of Tumeken, Flower of the desert, Mother of Icthlarin.
That all sounds very confusing, I might just call her Elidinis for short.

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

o.x: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

Well young one, you have entered the Magic Training Arena. It was built at the start of the Fifth Age, when runestones were first discovered. It was made because of the many pointless accidents caused by inexperienced
mages.
Who created it?

Good question. It was originally made by the ancestors of the wizards in the Wizards Tower. However, it was destroyed by melee and ranged warriors who took offence at the use of this new 'Magic Art'. Recently, the current
denizens of the Wizards Tower have resurrected the arena including various Guardians you will see as you look around. We are here to help and to ensure things run smoothly.
Interesting. So what can I do here?

You may train up your skill in the magic arts by travelling through one of the portals at the back of this entrance hall. By training up in one of these areas you will be awarded special Pizazz Points unique to each room. With
these points you may claim a variety of items from my fellow guardian up the stairs.
How do you record the points I have earned?
You really are full of questions! You will need a special Pizazz Progress Hat! I can give you one if you so wish to train here.
Yes please!

b.x: Ah, I'm afraid I can't give it to you as you don't have room to carry it!

o.x: Here you go. Talk to the hat to find out your current Pizazz Point totals.
Talk to it?
Well of course, it's a magic Pizazz Progress Hat! Mind your manners though, hats have feelings too!
Er... if you insist.

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave the rooms by any method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.
Player: Can you explain the different portals?
They lead to four areas to train your magic: The Telekinetic Theatre, The Alchemists' Playground, The Enchanting Chamber, and The Creature Graveyard.
What's the Telekinetic Theatre?
In there you can earn Telekinetic Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.
What will I be doing in there?

That depends on how much of a time-waster you are! You are required to use the Telekinetic Grab spell in order to move a statue through a maze. Casting the spell will move the statue towards you until it reaches a wall. So by
standing on the different sides of the maze you can move the statue North, East, South or West. You will be rewarded Pizazz Points for each maze successfully solved.

It will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. There's a book you can buy from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
What's the Alchemists' Playground?
In the playground you can earn Alchemist Pizazz Points for trading with the rewards guardian upstairs.
What's in there?

You'll find eight cupboards containing items you can turn to gold using the low and high alchemy spells. The money you earn will be taken from you upon leaving the playground to pay for the upkeep of this training arena

and to help fund magic shops around Gielinor. You will be rewarded with 1 Pizazz Point for every 100 coins deposited and a percentage of the money you create. Keep in mind that you will not be able to take more than 1000 coins
back out with you.
Sounds simple.
I am afraid not, for the cost of the items varies, as does their locations in the cupboards. You'll see a list of item costs that will help you decide what you should be converting to gold.

Fear not, it will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
What's the Enchanting Chamber?
In here you will be able to earn Enchantment Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.
What will I have to do?

You will find yourself amongst various piles of shapes. You can pick up these shapes and use one of your enchanting spells upon it to morph it into an orb. You'll also see a hole in the centre of the room; put the orbs in here and for
every 20 we will credit you with a gift. You will get Pizazz Points for every 10 shapes that you convert and the amount of points depends on the spell you use.
What's the difference between the shapes?

Ah, you will be notified of a different shape that will give you a bonus Pizazz Point when you convert that shape. You should also look out for dragon stones, as these will give you more Pizazz Points when you convert them.
It will be clearer when you arrive and there's a Guardian through the portal that will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
What's the Creature Graveyard?
In here you will be able to earn Graveyard Pizazz Points for trade upstairs.
But what do I have to do in there?

Patience young one. A great many creatures die in this world and much of their remains can cause clutter. We have taken it upon ourselves to teleport many bones from these creatures into this graveyard for a use. It's up to

you to practice your bones to bananas spell in order to put these bones into immediate use - nutritious food for monsters! Just convert the bones and put them in the holes in the walls. There is a drawback to this room
however, the bones often fall on people so you may want to eat some of those bananas to stay alive. When people die we confiscate Pizazz Points for the effort of teleporting incompetent mages.
What else do I get from this besides bruises?
As well as the Pizazz Points for giving us the bananas, you will be credited with runestones for your efforts, and you may be able to save up for a new kind of spell to use in the graveyard!

It will be clearer when you arrive and one of my fellow guardians through the portal will be able to tell you more. You can also buy a book from the Rewards Guardian upstairs that will explain it all.
Thanks, bye!
Use what you have learned.
None, I don't really care.
You won't gain with that attitude.

o.x: Why are you laughing?

Whose joke are you talking about?
Why, the vine's joke, of course. Can you hear someone else round here? Perhaps you're going crazy?
Why do you refer to the vine as 'she'?
Because she is female.
How do you know? I mean...she's a plant.
Heh heh heh, she told me that she's a lady. She's telling you now, can you not hear her?
Yes I can hear her.
Oh good, ah am so glad you can hear her. She has been nagging me since you arrived. Between you an' me, she can be quite annoying at times.

Ah. You sadden me. I had hoped you could hear her beautiful singing, but you clearly cannot. I pay you no ill will, the loss is yours my friend.

o: I thought her joke wasn't that bad.

o.x: I thought her joke wasn't that bad.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: Obviously not. You're clearly mad.

What is this place?

Oh, I see you have taken an interest in this little vine. I grew this vine from a root cutting of the Jade Vine to the north. She was a little clumsy and cut me while I took it. I have since imbued the cutting with my own magic, to help make her what she is today. She grows food for her jadinkos and extends her arms so that they can find home in her shade. And she grows different tings; each ting is nectar to one type of jadinko... but poison to another. Encourage her to grow different combinations of plants and watch as different jadinkos are drawn into her embrace.
What would be the point of attracting different jadinkos?

Aside from the joy of seeing nature's majesty? Ah suppose you could hunt the jadinkos you attract. They have special properties you could use. I have some special marasamaw traps that will catch them, if you have the skill. The jadinkos here are part of the vine herself. They are infused with her magic. Once hunted, they could provide ingredients for powerful new potions, if you have the know-how.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: What are jadinkos?
Heh heh, that is the name I's given to the strange creatures that live here. It has a nice ring to it, I's thinking.

o.title: Select an Option
o: So, you say that different plants attract different creatures?
Tell me about the potions I can make.
So, you say that different plants attract different jadinkos?

o.x: So, you say that different plants attract different creatures?

Oh yes. The vine is home to many variations of the strange jadinkos that wander here. Each one is attracted by different combinations of plants and environmental features. And some can only be attracted by those who have used a special juju potion on the flowers. Drawn to the magic like a moth to a flame, they are. Most jadinkos, they like the same ting and will always be attracted by that combination. But there are jadinkos whose tastes are fickle and their requirements change every week or so. These fickle creatures, when captured, give you ingredients that can enhance your mastery of this strange habitat. They can be used to make your experience here...more rewarding... ...if you can attract 'em and catch 'em, that is.
Is there any reason to catch them all?
Heh heh heh, of course! If you are skilled enough to catch one of each jadinko type that wander 'ere, come and speak to me. I will have a reward for you.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Tell me about the potions I can make.
Tell me about the potions I can make.

o.x: Tell me about the potions I can make.

These potions are different from others you can create. First, they be uniquely tied to you, your essence. No other can benefit from them. Second, they open up new ways of seeing the world and finding new rewards. Each is different and provides a special benefit. Perhaps, most important, is the juju hunter potion you can create, for this potion will attract new creatures to this vine. These juju potions cannot be made in a normal potion vial. They must be made in a specially created juju vial, for only they can hold the power.
Where can I get a juju vial from?
Heh heh heh. I's only one that sells them, strangely enough. Heh heh heh.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: I am Papa Mambo, shaman and protector of this vine. Once, I was the shaman of Shilo Village, and now I's a keeper of this vine.

I'll leave you be for now.
You may be wanting to visit the druid. He's learning about this habitat, like you, and may be able to share the knowledge he has gained. Goodbye, ma friend.

I'm Player. What are you doing all the way out here?
I've been contracted to retrieve artefacts from the top of this magnificient pyramid.

Well, it's me back...an old injury I picked up in Sophanem has come back to haunt me. I was working for Varrock Museum, but the gold they gave me wasn't even enough to pay for the carpet rides, let alone any decent equipment.
But that was a long time ago... I can't even lift a chisel right now. There's no way I can climb all the way up there.

I'll tell you what. I'll give you 1,000 coins for every artefact you get for me.

Is what still where?
The THING, the THING! It was just outside my house! Has it gone away yet? Or is it still lurking out there, waiting for me to go outside?

Ohhh, it was HORRIBLE! It was an enormous THING, with TEETH and EYES and... and... and THINGS!

o.x: What's going on here?

This is where we launch our landers to combat the invasion of the nearby islands. You'll see three landers - one for novice, intermediate and veteran adventurers. Each has a different difficulty, but they therefore offer varying rewards.
And this lander is...?
The novice.
So how do they work?

Simple. We send a lander out every three minutes, however we need at least five volunteers or it's a suicide mission. The lander can only hold a maximum of twenty five people though, so we do send them out early if they get full. If you'd be willing to help us then just wait in the lander and we'll launch it as soon as it's ready. However you will need a combat level of 35 to use this lander.

Not very good I'm afraid. His bosses are pretty cheep.
Groan. Don't give up the day job Pete.
Hello, adventurer. Welcome to Mill Lane Mill. Can I help you?

o.x: I'm Miss Millicent Miller, the Miller of Mill Lane Mill. Our family has been milling flour for generations.
Don't you ever get fed up with flour?
It's a good business to be in. People will always need flour.
This is Mill Lane Mill, source of the finest flour in Gielinor, and home to the Miller family for many generations.
We take wheat from the field nearby and mill it into flour.
Making flour is pretty easy. First of all, you need to get some wheat. You can pick some from wheat fields. There is one just outside the mill, but there are many others scattered across the world.
Feel free to pick wheat from our field! There always seems to be plenty of wheat there.
Then I bring my wheat here?
Yes, or to one of the other mills in Gielinor. They all work the same way.
Just take your wheat up two levels to the top floor of the mill and place some into the hopper.
Then you need to start the grinding process by pulling the lever near the hopper. You can add more wheat, but each time you add wheat you'll have to pull the hopper lever again.
So, where does the flour go then?
The flour appears in this room here. You'll need an empty pot to put the flour into. One pot will hold the flour made by one load of wheat.
You can buy empty pots from the general store in Lumbridge, south-east of here. You can also buy them from the Grand Exchange in Varrock or make them yourself.
That's all there is to it and you'll have a pot of flour.
Great! Thanks for your help.

o: Can you tell me how to milk a cow?

o.x: It's very easy. First, you need an empty bucket to hold the milk.
You can buy empty buckets from the general store in Lumbridge, south-west of here, or from general stores in RuneScape. You can also buy them from the Grand Exchange in Varrock.
Then find a dairy cow to milk - you can't milk just any cow.
How do I find a dairy cow?
They are easy to spot - they have a cowbell around their neck and are tethered to a post to stop them wandering around all over the place. There are a couple in this field.
Then you just need to use your bucket on the cow and you'll get some tasty, nutritious milk.

o: Can I buy milk off you?

o.x: I'm afraid not. My husband has already taken all of our stocks to the market.

You could get some by milking the dairy cows yourself. If you would still rather buy it, you can probably get some at the Grand Exchange in Varrock, just north of here. A lot of adventurers sell their goods there.

Let's see... We currently have Herman & Franklin Caranos, Arnold Lydspor, Devin Mendelberg and Ramara du Croissant. And me, of course.

Herman and Franklin are brothers, as you'll know. Herman's always been a fishing nut. Franklin's not all that bothered about fishing, but he does like tinkering with machinery. They're originally from East Ardougne.
Arnold's a bit more of a mystery. We think he might be from one of the barbarian tribes, but he never talks about that. He's always up for a chat, if you can understand his accent.
Devin Mendelberg comes from some town in Morytania - ghastly place! I'm not surprised he moved about as far west as he could go! He helps Franklin with the machinery, among other things.

Ramara's another Ardougnian. Her father's a baker there, but she didn't want to spend her whole life baking and doing his accounts. Also, you probably know what Ardougne's crime rate is like - it can't be easy running a market stall in that city! I went there once, and some wannabe adventurer started following me around trying to pick my pockets! I kept hitting him, but he kept coming back again and again!
You haven't told me about yourself yet.
Oh, I used to work with my sister, Emily, in the Rising Sun in Falador, but I wanted an outdoor job. The pay's better out here too, and the work's not too bad.

o: Who are you, and what is this place?

o.x: Who are you, and what is this place?
Arrharrharr!
Do you not recognise me? I am the famous dandy pirate 'Fancy' Dan!
Yes, of course, any pirate knows who you are.
But of course.
As for what this place is, it is my glorious still, producing the best quality 'rum' this side of Braindeath Island.
Oh, and the run-down swill-producing ditch that San Fan over there calls a still.
So with two stills you have plenty of 'rum' right?
Well we would do, if that hatchet-faced harridan wouldn't keep trying to torch the place!
I say!
A little while ago we had some real problems getting rum to the island, hence the two stills.
However, after a little misunderstanding involving San's still and a barrel of gunpowder our relationship seems to have become a little strained.
Apparently it is perfectly within the pirate code to burn each others stills, so long as nobody directly attacks the other person's crew, so run production has taken a slight dip of late.
Can I help out?
Yes, probably. I have a bunch of jobs that need doing, if you feel up to it.
What would you like to know about?

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: How do I help you brew 'Rum'?
Well the stills we have set up are based on the ones on Braindeath Island... well roughly at any rate.
All you have to do is help put the ingredients into the hopper and keep the boilers burning.
If you add enough ingredients to the hopper's then you have the ability to pick up a single bottle of rum when it brews.

So, if ye add 5 buckets of water to the hopper's, then ye get access to one bottle. If you add 3 bowls of coloured water you get access to one bottle, and if you add one of anything else you get access to one bottle.
This is cumulative, meaning that if you add (for example ) 10 buckets of water, 3 sweetgrubs and 6 bowls of coloured water, then you have a chance to collect 7 bottles of rum for the team.
The boilers are easy as pie to sort out. You just put some logs in, light them with a tinderbox, and then keep putting logs in until they are good and hot.
Three logs should do it, but it's best to keep heaping them in just in case.
The ingredients are; Bitternuts, Scrapey Tree Bark, Sweetgrubs, Buckets of Water and some Coloured Water.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: Where can I get Bitternuts?
There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.
Send it up the tree? How does that work?
Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.
Wait a second, dye?
Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs to.
That makes sense...I think...
Anything else?

o: Where can I get Scrapey Tree Bark?

o.x: Where can I get Scrapey tree bark...and why do I get the feeling I won't like the answer?
Inside this walled area there are a few Scrapey trees. They are the big, ill looking ones, you can't miss them.
Basically, you cut them down and then carve the bark off with a knife.
It's pretty simple, except the sap tends so make people feel kind of ill if they get any on themselves.
How ill?
Don't worry, we aren't talking deadly ill or anything.
It's more like you'll feel quite dizzy and weak for a bit.
Joy...
Anything else?
Sweetgrubs? What are they?
Well, lacking any sluglings in the area, we add these little grubs called Sweetgrubs. If you ignore the gag-inducing aftertaste, they are quite sweet.
How... how can you drink the stuff?
Quite easily!
Pirates are renowned as being tough for a reason.
So where do I get these grubs from anyway?
Well, there are a few sweetgrub mounds inside there. We have a handful of rat meat that you can use on the mounds to draw the grubs to the surface.
Mind your fingers though, they are voracious little things.
And here was me thinking that nothing could be more disgusting than Braindeath 'Rum'.
Arr, that's where ye'd be wrong lad, 'cos new, improved Braindeath 'Rum' Classic is now 200% more disgustin' then any leadin' competitor!
Legal disclaimer; the dangerous amount of disgustin' in new Braindeath 'Rum' Classic be too much for pregnant women, donkeys and anyone with more than seven letters in their last name.
What was that?
What was what?
Is there anything else?

o: Where can I get buckets of water?

o.x: How do I get...
Wait, no, that question makes me sound like I haven't a clue what I'm doing.
Where can I get buckets in there?
There are a few lying about. Help yourself.
There is a pump in the still, so long as it's working you should have almost unlimited water.
Hold on, do I have to add anything disgusting and/or potential lethal to the water before I pour it in?
Perish the thought!
Ok, just checking.
Anything else?

o: Where can I get coloured water?

o.x: What sort of coloured water are we talking about here?
Well, the other still has an area of waste ground with a flower growing on it. If you go and grab one of the flowers and jam it in the kettle, the water will boil out the colour.
We use the colour to keep our rum easily identifiable.
So I just empty the kettle into the hopper, right?
No, no, you'll need to take an empty bowl and fill it from the kettle.
That way you can use the stuff on a monkey if you need to.
Use it on a monkey...of course.
Anything else?
How do I repair the still?
Well, assuming those scurvy dogs have managed to set any of it on fire, then you will need to tip a bucket of water on it before you can repair it.
Then, it all comes down to what part of it was damaged.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: How can I repair hoppers?
Well, assuming that they are not on fire, all you need to do is use the heavy lumber patches. They are big enough to cover most holes.
Will I need a hammer?
No, just shove it into place and whack it until it lines up.
Anything else?

o: How do I repair Pipes and the pump?

o.x: How do I repair pipes and the pump?
Well, if you use a pipe section on the damaged part you should be able to replace it easily.
Will I need a hammer?
No, likely you'll just need to whack the old one out and slot the new one in with your hands.
Anything else?
How do I repair bridges?
Well, we have these handy bridge sections you can use to repair the bridges.
The main problem is, while a still will keep working if a bit of it is only damaged, the bridges are completely out of commission if they are even slightly damaged.
Is that going to be a problem? I mean, I can jump across I think.
Don't try that! Our lawyers tell us we aren't covered for injuries sustained while jumping over burned bridges.
Seriously, just keep off the bridges until they are fixed.
Anything else?

o: How do I get repair items?

o.x: Where do I get all this stuff anyway?
We have a load of items already on a table inside the still. You can also make new ones if you grab some logs.
How does that work?
We have a worktable set up in the still. If you use the logs in it can craft up a handy replacement for part of the still.
Don't worry about them fitting, the things are held together by nails, replacement parts and soot by now.
Well...how sanitary...
Anything else?

o: Ok, I think I've heard enough

o.x: Ok, I think I've heard enough.
Fine. Glad I could help.
(Dialogue ends)
So...how would I go about sabotaging the enemy still?
Ok, here's what you need to do.
The wood around here is really dry and flammable, so take one of the torches, light it up, and then go and attack the enemy still with it.
That's it?
Most of their still is soaked in 'alcohol' and made from tinder dry wood.
Essentially, if it isn't ours, try using a torch on it and see what happens.
Ok, I get you.
Anything else?
So what will you give me for helping out?
Hahahaha! What a mercenary attitude! You'll do fine here.
Well, for each bottle that your team produces, I'll give you one piece of eight.
If you managed to set something on fire then I'll toss in another, same for repairing the still.

See Honest Jimmy there? He will trade you some pretty nice stuff for them.
Great!
Anything else?

o: So, what's Summoning all about, then?

o.x: Whatchoo talkin' about, yooman?
Yes, I think so.

I gots da pouches and spirit shards, but no charms. Yooman gotta get dem himself. Yooman just gets a club and yooman goes whackin' things till monsters drop charms. Der'es loads of things that gots charms. Dere is loads of charms all over da place, gold, blue, green, crimson...even some real rare ones like obsidy-un charms as well.
I'll be sure to keep my eyes open for them.

If yooman wants to learn Summonin' good, den yooman needs to make da Summonin' pouches. Yooman also gets learnin' from da Summonin' and da scrolls and da splittin' Summonin' pouches. Da Summonin' pouches is da bestest way of learnin' of them all. Yooman got it, or yooman stoopid?
Sure!

Hah! Yooman is smart for a little ting! Da last ting is da pets. Da more summony you is, da more you understand der birds and der bees and der rocks and stuff. Der bigger yooman's summonyness is, da stronger der pets yooman will be able to keep. Real big summoners gets to raise animals like lizard tings, including dragons! Now if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about somefin' else?

Summoned familiars are da main ting in Summonin', as if yooman didn't be guessing. There's all kinds of tings yooman can summon. Der bigger der yooman's summonyness, der bigger der tings yooman can summon. Ting is, dem familiars not really, REALLY animals, if yer get me. Dey are really REALLY spirits dat are stronger than der real animal, wiv all kinds of powaz dat der rest don't. Dat's why dey are not runnin' around all da time - it's cos der summoner puts dere Summonin' skill points inta summonin' em, and keeping em here.
So Summoning skill points are like food to dem - sorry, them?

Yah! Dat's right! Der bigger der ting, der more ya gotta feed it, and der more often it gets hungry. Dat's why only der big summony types, like me, have enough Summonin' skill points for der biggest familiars. And der bigger der yooman's Summonin' level, der easier it is to be feedin' der littler tings for longer.
I'm starting to get a little hungry now.

It's like if yooman be holdin' bags of wheat. Der bigger der bags yooman be holdin', der bigger der yooman's arms get, so de bigger bags dey can hold next time. If da youman feeds a little ting den dey will have lots of wheat left over too!
Great! So, what can these familiars do?
What can dey not do, more like? Dere is a load of dem - tons, lots and lots - and each of dem is not like der uvvers.
Well, can you give me some hints, then?

Well, Bogrog only calls on der ones dat fight! Dey hang around until Bogrog be fightin' and den dey leap in! I suppose yooman like you will be wantin' the ones that just make yooman more skilful, or dem ones dat lug around tings dat yooman's arms too puny to lift.
Amazing!
Now, if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about someting else?

If you cuts up one of dem Summonin' pouches, over at der obelisk, den da energy gets mushed up real good, transformin' into a big stack of scrolls. Dese scrolls can den be used to make da familiars do a speshial move! Hur, hur, hur! Der spirit wolfies, fer example, dey can make little tings run away real good if dey perform dere Howl speshial move.
Or longer, in the case of that giant wolpertinger!
Hur hur hur, me hearing about dat from da spirities! Yooman can't mix up der scrolls, though - spirit wolfies get real growly if ya try to make 'em perform dreadfowl speshial move!
So, what sort of special moves are there?

Dere is lots of dem - like da familiars! If yooman's confoosed, den just think of dis; the attackin' familiars got a lot more of der attackin' speshial moves, and der soppy, non-attackin' ones gots da non-attackin' speshial moves. Yooman will want da non-attackin' ones to heal dem, or get dem stuff, or make dem better at uvver tings.
Are the special moves and the familiar's normal abilities similar?

Naah, dem's mostly diff'rent. Da spirit wolfies' are sim'lar though. Dey's got da Howl speshial move, but dey's also got a howly normal ability. You can get der spirit wolfy to use Howl on anyt'ing you see, but it can only uses its howly normal ability on tings you is fightin'. If der familiar with the normal ability is fighting with a yooman, den it makes der normal ability when it sees an openin'. Der speshial moves though - dey never use dem unless yooman tells 'em to wiv a scroll.
I see. Thanks for the information!
Now, if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about somefin' else?

Der petties? Well dey's not real summony stuffs, but if yooman trains hard, then yooman gets to be friends wiv dem. Der summonier der yooman gets, der more like nature der yooman gets, so da little petties like yooman better. So, der petties dat would be runnin' away don't, and even der nasty petties get real quiet too. An' when dey not runnin' or bitin', den da yooman gets ta feed 'em and pet 'em and keep 'em.
So what will I need to do to raise the animals?
Dey just walk behind da yooman, so yooman just gives dem food, more food and good foods. Da bestest summoners wants to pet themse'ves a dragon!
Wow! Imagine riding around on a dragon, and fighting with it!
Yooman is too stoopid.
What?

One, you too puny to make a dragon do as you sez. Two, when yooman gets a pet, yooman remembers it's still alive, an' yooman's friend. Pets are not like der spirity familiars - dey die if you kills dem! What friend pokes his friend in der head and says 'We go fight now. I gets on your back and you fights for me'?
I didn't realise.
Dat's 'cos yooman's stoopid. Petties not toys or clubs, or ridy-tings. Dey is livin' tings dat yooman be raisin' from birthyness. If you a bad, petty yooman, I club you!
I'll take good care of them.
Now, if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about somefin' else?

o: Can I buy some summoning supplies?

o.x: Can I buy some summoning supplies, please?
Hur, hur, hur! Yooman's gotta buy lotsa stuff if yooman wants ta train good!
Summoning Supplies (Bogrog)

o: Are you interested in buying pouches or scrolls?

o.x: Are you interested in buying pouches or scrolls?
Des other ogres's stealin' Bogrog's stock. Gimmie pouches and scrolls and yooman gets da shardies.
Ok.
(Summoning Trade In interface opens.)
*sigh* Not another one.
Another what?
Another 'archaeologist'.
I'm not going to let you plunder my master's tomb you know.
That's a shame. Have you got anything else I could do while I'm here?
If it will keep you out of mischief I suppose I could set something up for you...
I have a few rooms full of some things you humans might consider valuable, do you want to give it a go?

o.title: Hmm. Pyramid Plunder or questions?
o: I'd rather talk about artefacts a bit more.

o.x: I'd rather talk about your fine artefacts a bit more, on behalf of a...friend.
Oh, really. What exactly is it you want to know? I've told you all I am willing to reveal.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: I'd like a recap, please.
Oh, really. What exactly is it you want to know?
My, umm, business associate, Simon Templeton would like to inspect some of your artefacts.
What? His effrontery knows no ends. Did he inform you that the last time he was here he tried to make off with some of my bandages? He claimed they were useful in some sort of cure for his injuries.
I'm sure he's a reformed man, now. All he wants to do is have a look.
Never. He'd sell his own mummy for a profit. Tell him that if he ever comes back here, he'll be wearing my bandages alright...around his neck...tightly!
I'm not sure which is more irritating: running out of drinking water all the time or being subjected to this humour.
One might call it dry humour...
Taking your loot will be heaps more pleasureable after suffering through that pun.

o: In that case, I'll be about my business.

o.x: In that case, I'll be about my business.

o: The sounds like fun; what do I do?

o.x: That sounds like fun; what do I do?
You have five minutes to explore the treasure rooms and collect as many artefacts as you can.
The artefacts are in the urns, chests and sarcophagi found in each room.
There are eight treasure rooms, each subsequent room requires higher thieving skills to both enter the room and thieve from the urns and other containers.
The rewards also become more lucrative the further into the tomb you go.
You will also have to deactivate a trap in order to enter the main part of each room.
When you want to move onto the next room you need to find the correct door first.
There are four possible exits... you must open the door before finding out whether it is the exit or not.
Opening the doors require picking their locks. Having a lockpick will make this easier.
{{tselect|Do you have any more questions?}}
Not right now.
Well, get out of here then.

o: I know what I'm doing, so let's get on with it.

o.x: Goodbye.
But I didn't say anything?

nodes.x: Ouch!
Are you alright?
I'm fine, I'm fine. Just a scratch.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Who are you then?
Me? I'm Tarik.
That hat you're wearing doesn't look like it comes from around here?
It was a present, my employer thought it would suit me. I'm not sure what it does, though it does keep the sun off very well.
Who is your employer then?
Simon Templeton, though I haven't seen him since the town gates were closed off.
Simon Templeton ... that name seems familiar?
He's an archaeologist, I worked as an assistant for him. Though I work for myself now.
So what have you been up to?
Simon suggested that there might be riches to be found in that pyramid over there.
So how did you get injured?
I've been investigating that pyramid over there.

o: Do you know anything about this pyramid?

o.x: So what's in the pyramid?

Well, I'm not sure. First of all there's something odd about the doors on the place. There's four of them - but three of them lead to an empty tomb. The other one is guarded by something - I keep getting knocked out. If I make it through the door there's a Mummy waiting. But which door the right one is seems to change, it's all quite confusing.
What about this Mummy?
I don't think he likes people. However he does allot you to enter some of the rooms in the tomb. They are dangerous though.
Bah, I laugh in the face of danger!

Well, if you go into that pyramid then you'll be laughing a lot then. It's full of poisonous snakes and scarabs, and rather nasty Mummies as well. You could die in there. I managed to get into one room, but the next room was harder. My lockpicking skills weren't good enough, maybe I should have brought a lockpick.
The first room in the pyramid requires a thieving level of 21. Each subsequent room requires an extra 10 levels of thieving skill to enter.
There are also lots of poisonous snakes in the urns. They'll bite you if they can. You might be able to charm them if you know how. I'd bring some antipoison anyway if I were you.
It all sounds like fun to me. So is there anything valuable in there?
There are lots of artefacts, you should be able to sell them on the black market, I mean, to a legitimate trader, for some money.
You mean Simon Templeton?
Well, he's a 'legitimate' as you can get, if you can get out of this city and get to him.
I'll find a way. Is there anything else of value in there?
I have heard a rumour that there is a valuable magic sceptre in there as well.
Ah, now you have piqued my interest. What do you know about this sceptre?
Not a lot. It is apparently made of gold and covered in jewels, and used to be owned by one of Tumeken's sons.
Tumeken?
Tumeken, the sun god and head of the gods. His sons were the rulers, chosen by him to rule in his name.
So these sons were rich and powerful then? This sceptre should be pretty good then.
Hmmm. Well it is supposed to have some magical powers.
Magical powers? This sounds good. What are they?
I'll let you know when I find it!
Not if I find it first!
Hey! If you find it I deserve a share of the profits! You wouldn't have known it existed without my help.
I'll think about it... Right, I think I'd better investigate this place.

Lunar Isle - why don't you go have a look around town.
Hello there.

o.x: Baba Yaga's Magic Shop

o: It's a very interesting house you have here.

o.x: It's a very interesting house you have here. Does he have a name?
Why of course. It's Berty.
Berty? Berty the leg house?
Yes.
May I ask why?
It just has a certain ring to it, don't you think? Beeerteeee!
You're ins...
Insane? Very.
I'm good thanks, bye.

nodes.x: Take me to your leader.
Wot?
Isn't that what you're supposed to say when you meet a new race of people?
Well, mate, we don't av no leader, so I ain't gonna take ya to um. We auw av eqwuw right's un stuff, yeah? But if ya wont an intro go live it up wiv da Onerimancer.
OK. Is he rich and powerful?
No man, SHE, is dead-wise yeah? She is responsible for initiation wituals an stuff.
Great. Thanks. And where is she?
She angs out int souf east of ouw island.
Okey dokey....yeah.
Huh?
Hello there.
Hi. Welcome to the general store. How might I help you?

o.x: Moon Clan General Store
I have a question...
About magic of course.
Sorry?
I said about magic of course. You know, in response to your question.
But I didn't ask anything yet.
Yes, but you were thinking of asking me how I was floating.
That's true!
How could you possibly know that?
Don't you realise we can read your mind.
Oh, of course. How do you manage to do that?

It's quite simple, everyone has a resonance that is responded to by the moon. This resonance changes depending on what we are thinking. You can tune yourself in to listen to this resonance with practice - it's a life long
quest for the members of the Moon Clan, but especially easy to read with outsiders like yourself, as you are far louder and unguarded.
I see. I best be careful what I think of then.
That's disgusting!
Sorry.
I'm good thanks, bye.

nodes.x: Can you tell me a bit about your people?
Ok. Like what?
How about the values of the Moon clan!
Let me see... We value knowledge of self because it is this that gives us our strength! It is most important!
Well... I know things about myself. I know I like hot chocolate!
I was meaning something a little deeper than that. We also like to see someone listen. You know how they say a wise man listens?
Did you hear me?
... I'm listening.
Most wise.
Huh?
Hello there.
Welcome to the clothes store. How might I help you?

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Moon Clan Fine Clothes

o: Do you have any use for suqah teeth or hides?

o.x: Do you have any use for suqah teeth or hides?
Most certainly! The hides are great for making clothes and the teeth are particularly useful for broaches, necklaces and the like. I'll trade you any you can find for pure essence if you like.

b: With suqah teeth or hides in backpack to exchange:

b.title: Trade your hides and teeth for [number] pure essence?

o.x: There you go!
Fair enough, come back anytime if you do.

b: Without suqah teeth or hides in backpack:

b.x: That's good to know. I don't have any with me at the moment, but at least I know where to come when I do!

b: Having exchanged 28 suqah teeth or hides for the day:

b.x: Most certainly! I'm only happy to let you exchange 28 each day though. Otherwise I'm swamped with teeth and hides that I can't use. You've reached that limit.

b: Having not completed the elite Fremennik tasks:

b.x: You need to complete the Fremennik elite tasks to unlock this facility.

o: It's a very interesting island you have here.

o.x: It's a very interesting island you have here.
Why thank you. It's been our haven for a great many generations.
Everything seems to have a magical feel to it.
Of course. We integrate magic into all areas of our lives. It is a part of everyone, so why deny it? It's best to make the most of this innate gift we have all been given.
What sort of things do you use your magic for?

Take a look around. We use it in our day to day lives, from making a cup of tea, to travelling around the island. You see our ancestors were the ones that found the first rune essence and put it to use! The various factions were
eventually created, with people having different ideas on how the essence should be used (or not in some cases!)
What has kept you so secluded on this island?
It may be a bit beyond you, but although magic comes from within, we are all very strongly linked to the moon and the effects it has on us cannot be denied!
It can't?
Of course not. This very island has a great link to our moon, which helps us understand ourselves - especially our dreams, which is the path to understanding magic.
I think I will just have to take your word on that.
I'm good thanks, bye.

nodes.x: Good day, how may I help you?

Watering the pretty flowers, you want to help?
I don't have time to water flowers, I have people to save!
Pft, you should take time to enjoy the simple things.
I'm not a simple person.
So it seems.
Hello there.
Don't talk to me outerlander! I don't have time for the likes of you!
What makes you say that?

b.x: You've experience yet to gain. Especially in keeping with the Fremenniks and their trials!/You're not yet a worthy enough adventurer to talk to me! You have some questing to do.

b: After completing The Fremennik Trials, but without the requirements to start Lunar Diplomacy:

b.x: Only people who've travelled on quests far from here can talk to me!

nodes.x: Oh.

Hey, I think I'm learning a thing or two from these Moon Clan ladies.

o.x: Oi! I need another lens, boy.

b.x: But you don't have space.
Good point.
Huh, oh ok, I suppose I owe you one.

o.x: I think I'll pass. But thanks..

nodes.x: What are you cooking?
'Beefy' Burns: My speciality! What else could I be cooking?
Ok, and your speciality is...?
'Beefy' Burns: Boiled shark guts with a hint of rosemary and a dash of squid ink.
I think I'll stick to making my own food.
'Beefy' Burns: Your loss!
What do you do for fun on this ship? You know, when you're not doing pirate stuff.
'Eagle-eye' Shultz: All sorts! Hide and seek, pin the patch on the pirate, walk the plank!
What a life! Wait a minute. 'Walk the plank'? Surely that's a bit dangerous?
'Eagle-eye' Shultz: Well of course, but where's the fun without a few deaths?
I think I'll stick to Runelink.
What does it take to become first mate on a ship?
First mate 'Davey-boy': Good question. We have a diplomatic consession at the turn of the financial year. Said pirate is chosen should the existing mate be absent without leave.
I had no idea. I always figured it was all about popularity.
First mate 'Davey-boy': It is. I'm just pulling your leg.

Yar! We be pirates, yar! Avast, ye scurvy land-lubbing lychee!
Please don't talk like that, it is extremely irritating.

Oh. Okay. Sorry.
Hello.
Hello.

Not as such. If any of us get sick we kidnap a doctor and don't let him go until we're better.

Hello.
Sorry, can't stop, the Captain will have my guts for garters if he catches me slacking off talking to the stowaway.

nodes.x: Hello there!
Hello, what's in those boxes?
Aha, interested in my crossbows are you?
Are they any good?

They're dwarven engineering at its best. If you've got enough skill in crafting, smithing and fletching, you can even make them yourself. You can buy some of the parts here and make the rest yourself.

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: How do I make one for myself?

o.x: How do I make one for myself?
Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.
Wood fletched into stock... check.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Which goes with which?
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamant and Mahogany and finally Rune and Yew.
Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?

Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows. You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.
What about magic logs?

Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable. I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want anything to do with it!
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
What about ammo?

You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though. There's also the option of tipping any untipped bolt with gems then enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.
Oh my poor bank, how will I store all those?!
Don't you worry, I have just the thing here, a bolt pouch designed specially for holding 4 different types of crossbow bolt.
Wow, how much?

b: If the player does not already own a bolt pouch:

b.x: Well let's see now... for you? 1500 gold pieces should do the trick.

b.title: Would you like to buy a pouch?

o.x: Yes I'll pay the 1500gp.
Hand it over then.

b: If the player does not have enough money:

b.x: Oh, I don't have that much on me.
Best go make some money then, shouldn't take you too long.

b: If the player has enough money:

b.x: You hand over your gold and receive a well made leather pouch.
Hmm... didn't I see you down here buying one the other day? You can only have one at a time I'm afraid.

o.x: Player: Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.

nodes.x: You don't have a sapling planted in that patch. Plant one and I might agree to look after it for you.
You don't have a sapling planted in that patch. Plant one and I might agree to look after it for you.
'Ello, Player.
Hello, what's that you've got there?
A crossbow, are you interested?
Maybe, are they any good?
Are they any good?! They're dwarven engineering at its best!

nodes.x: Good day. How can I help you?
I was just wondering what you were up to.
I work for Aluft Aloft Gnome Food Delivery Service. It's a growing business you know. We get more customers every day!
So do you have any spare jobs then?
Aluft Gianne jnr. is in charge - he'll be able to help you.
Thanks.
Have a nice day.
Busy Busy Busy.
Why are you so busy?
Aluft Aloft is a bustling new business, here in the Gnome restaurant. We're getting food orders all the time.
Do you have any jobs then?
If you want to get a job, talk to Aluft Gianne jnr. I'm sure he has plenty. Have a nice day.
I hate this job. All the other staff are so happy all the time. It depresses me.
Why don't you get a new job?

I can't find any other work. I wanted to be a Gnomeball player but I wasn't big enough. I came up with some clever tricks using my feet, but I was told they weren't fit for gnomeball. 'Gnomeball is played with the hands,' they said. Well, even Mad Donna isn't as good as I am with my feet.

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Can you show me your tricks?

o.x: I'd love to, but I'm supposed to be at work right now. Besides, the other gnomes laugh at me. They don't appreciate skill when they see it!

Mad Donna is a genius with a gnomeball! She invented a trick using everything except the hands to control a gnomeball. It's called the Mad Donna Seven. Other gnomes call her mad because her trick doesn't involve holding the gnomeball. But she's my inspiration to invent new and exciting tricks!
OK, whatever.
Aren't you going to wish me a nice day?
Have a day. It can be nice if you can be bothered. I know I can't.
... nice.

nodes.x: You're a long way from home, what are you doing here?
I'm on an expedition to try and extend the bounds of gnome knowledge. King Narnode has sent out a number of gnome explorers to map the furthest reaches of Gielinor.
Seems like a hard job.
Oh no, I enjoy it - I've always had itchy feet ever since I was a little gnome.
Still, you seem to have drawn the short straw here - there's nothing but snow...
Oh, I like it - very peaceful. Avoiding those Trolls can be tricky though.
Tell me about it...
It's a bit hot and dry round here for a gnome isn't it? I thought you gnomes liked your home comforts.
Certainly I miss home cooking, but gnomes are also fundamentally curious people. I'm here exploring the furthest reaches of the world for the King.
Found anything interesting?

Sophanem is a curious place, if you can get into the blighted place. There are several pyramids round here as well. Fascinating architecture, I've heard stories that some of them contain treasure tombs and mummies. Cats seem to have considerable importance round here, they certainly seem tied into their religion. The Gods round here seem very alien to me - I've never heard of them before.
Thanks.
Are you hunting animals, then?
I'm exploring the region for the good of the gnome people.
You're not tracking down huge beasts to kill - you look equipped for it.
Well, if I find anything interesting I'll try and bring it back to the King. That might include animals, I suppose. I'd rather not kill it, though - most animals are more useful alive.
How would you get it home, then?
Never underestimate the ingenuity of a gnome, friend.
Have you found anything else interesting around here?

I've heard strange rumours about something the locals call the Broodoo. I haven't quite worked out what they are but they seem to be some sort of undead whose ghastly fate depends on the way they were killed. I think they may be sacrifice victims - but I'm not sure why they are sacrificed. Either way the locals seem to be very scared of them.
That's interesting. Thanks.
I can't believe that I've been made to wait so long.
What are you waiting for?
I have been waiting for an audience with the King for days!
Well, he's clearly a busy man.
Bah! I think he's just trying to insult the gnome nation, by making me wait. The cheek of these humans. Just because they're vertically challenged they think they can ignore us.
I'm not ignoring you.
Hmm. I should be thankful for small mercies, I suppose.
Fascinating, fascinating. It's remarkable what these young dwarves have managed to create. Oh, hello young man.
Hello, what's a gnome like you doing in a place like this?
Ah, well I have been sent by the King to talk with the dwarves here and find out more about their recent advances in technology.
Found anything interesting?
The rideable carts are a very handy way to get to mining sites, and the Blast Furnace is a magnificent beast of a machine.
I'll have a look, thanks.
Hiya! Do you want to buy me a drink?
I think I'll pass on that.
Fine, I'm sure someone else round here will know how to treat a woman...
Greetings, human!

o.x: Oh no, I come from the Gnome Stronghold. I've been sent here by King Narnode to learn about human magics.
The stronghold's in the north-west of the continent - a long way away. You should visit us there some time. The food's great, and the company's delightful.

nodes.title: Choose an option:

o.x: Apologies! Allow me to introduce myself: my name is Aeonisig Raispher, special advisor to King Roald on spiritual matters.
Special advisor on spiritual matters? What does that mean?
It means that some decisions the King has to make might have unforeseen repercussions on the nation's spiritual sensibilities. My duty is to ensure that Saradominist ideals are not stomped underfoot.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: How did you come to be an advisor to King Roald?

o.x: My main function is to ensure that King Roald is apprised of all options, especially those that favour the righteous followers of Saradomin.

o.x: The King of Misthalin, like any great leader, always requires the best advice and the best advisors. He very often summons occasional advisors to help him in certain situations, but it was felt by the Church of Saradomin that a full time advisor on religious matters was needed to ensure fair treatment of Saradomin's followers.
How come he doesn't have an advisor for any other religious denominations?
Because I simply won't stand for it, that's why! Now, enough of your impertinent questions. I have work to do!

o: I'm lost... Can you help me?

o.x: I'm lost... Can you help me?

Well, you're in sector [one/two/three/four/five/six], but if you were hoping for any other help then I'm very sorry. I find it hard enough to help myself. Life's so very hard here. Before too long they'll be wanting to have another blood tithing and then I'll feel just awful again.
What's a blood tithing?
You must be new here, else you'd know for sure. It's where we have to give a blood tithe to the vampyres. They do it on a weekly basis, a different sector each week so they don't kill us all off.

o: Do you know about the Myreque?

o.x: Do you know about the Myreque?
It's probably best not to talk about that, friend.
I need to make contact with them. Please don't worry - I'm on their side.

o: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

o.x: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

Yep, that's where we are at the moment. This place, Meiyerditch, is just one large ghetto. The city is sectioned off so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill us all off in one go.

o: What do you know about the vampyres?

o.x: What do you know about the vampyres?

They're monsters, I know that much. I've never known anything else, but I have a feeling it might be nice to not have to live in fear the whole time. Worrying if I'm going to make the next blood tithe quota. I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres, most likely converted from some sort of bipedal creature, probably human. Juvinates are initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to get some special powers. After that you have the vyrewatch - they're nasty... really nasty.
