nodes.x: Miaoww
Miaoww
Hello.
Hello! Welcome to my workshop. My name is Sani. Feel free to use any of my anvils, I can't use them all at once!
Thanks!

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: My name is Wilfred and I'm the best woodsman in Asgarnia! I've spent my life studying the best methods for woodcutting. That's why I have this cape, the Skillcape of Woodcutting.

o: What is that cape you're wearing?

o.x: This is a Skillcape of Woodcutting. Only a person who has achieved the highest possible level in a skill can wear one.

o: Can you help me with the sentinel outfits?

o.x: Player: Can you help me with the sentinel outfits?

b: If the player can't receive sentinel fragments and hasn't unlocked the blueprint required to make the outfit pieces:

b.x: At level 70 you can start to collect fragments to make elite skilling outfits. When you get to that level you will automatically start collecting fragments. Then you can use them with a blueprint to make yourself any remaining elite outfit pieces for this skill.

b: If the player can receive sentinel fragments but hasn't unlocked the blueprint required to make the outfit pieces:

b.x: You are set up to receive fragments. When you get to level 80 you will be able to create outfit pieces.

b: If the player can receive sentinel fragments and has unlocked the blueprint required to make the outfit pieces:

b.x: You are set up to receive fragments. When you have 3600 fragments you can use them to create an elite outfit piece.
Simply go to an Invention workbench to create the pieces.

b: If the player owns the full nature's sentinel outfit or all of the outfit pieces required to craft it:

b.x: You have already created all of the possible outfit pieces. I will make sure you do not receive any further fragments.
Remember you can combine the base outfit pieces to make the high tier versions, to get the additional benefits.

nodes.x: Good day. How may I help you?

b: If the player has items waiting for them in the Grand Exchange:

b.x: Before we go any further, I should inform you that you have items ready for collection from the Grand Exchange.

nodes.title: What would you like to say?
o: I'd like to access my bank account, please.

o.x: Bank

o: I'd like to check my PIN settings.

o.x: Bank PIN

o: I'd like to see my collection box.

o.x: Grand Exchange collection box
What is this place?
This is a branch of the Bank of Gielinor. We have branches in many towns.

o.title: What would you like to say?

o.x: And what do you do?
We will look after your items and money for you. Leave your valuables with us if you want to keep them safe.

o: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?

o.x: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?
Yes we did, but people kept on coming into our branches outside of Varrock and telling us that our signs were wrong. They acted as if we didn't know what town we were in or something.

nodes.x: Hello adventurer, welcome to the Entrana furnace.
Would you like me to explain my craft to you?

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Yes please. I'd be fascinated to hear what you do.

o.x: Yes please. I'd be fascinated to hear what you do.
I'm extremely pleased to hear that! I've always wanted an apprentice. Let me talk you through the secrets of glassblowing.

Fritz the Glassblower: Glass is made from soda ash and silica. We get our soda ash by collecting seaweed from the rocks - the prevailing currents make the north-east and south-west corners of the island the best place to find it, it can also be found in

your nets sometimes when you're fishing, on Karamja island or at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony in the nets there. To turn seaweed into soda ash, all you need to do is burn it on a fire. Feel free to use the range in my house for
that; it's the one directly west of here. Next we collect sand from the sandpit that you'll also find just west of here, there are others located in Yanille and Shilo Village.

b: If the player has not received an empty bucket from Fritz the Glassblower:
If the player has an empty bucket:

b.x: I see you already have a bucket that you can use for carrying it in.

b: If the player does not have an empty bucket:

b.x: You'll need a bucket to carry it in. Tell you what, you can have this old one of mine.

b: If the player has already received an empty bucket from Fritz the Glassblower:

b.x: You can use the bucket I gave you earlier.

b: If the player has an empty bucket:
If the player does not have an empty bucket:

b.x: I'm afraid I don't have that bucket with me. Could you give me another one, please?
Do I look like I'm made of buckets? You'll just have to buy another from a general store.
And don't interrupt me when I'm speaking - it's rude. Anyway, as I was saying ...

o.x: Fritz the Glassblower: Bring the sand and the soda ash back here and melt them together in the furnace, and there you have it - molten glass!

There are many things you can use the molten glass for once you have made it. Depending on how talented you are, you could try turning it into something, like a fishbowl, for example. If you'd like to try your hand at the
fine art of glassblowing you can use my spare glassblowing pipe. I think I left it on the chest of drawers in my house this morning.
Alternatively I am always happy to buy the molten glass from you, saves me running about making it for myself.
That sounds good. How much will you pay me?
Tell you what, because you've been interested in my art, I'll pay you the premium price of 20 gold pieces for each piece of molten glass you bring me.

o: No thanks, I doubt I'll ever turn my hand to glassblowing.

o.x: No thanks, I doubt I'll ever turn my hand to glassblowing.
Ok, suit yourself. Nobody seems to be interested in the skilled crafts these days.
If you should change your mind, come back and talk to me.

nodes.x: Can I help you at all?

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Who are you?
My name is Ignatius Vulcan. Once I was - like you - an adventurer, but that was before I realised the beauty and power of flame! Just look at this...
Yeeouch!

Stare into the flame and witness the purity and power of fire! As my attraction to flame grew, so did my skills at firelighting. I began to neglect my combat skills, my Mining skills and my questing. Who needs such mundane skills
when one can harness the power of fire? After years of practice I am now the acknowledged Master of Flame! Everything must be purified by fire!
Okaaaay! Err, I'll be going now. Umm, get better soon.

o: Do you have anything for trade?

o.x: Do you have anything for trade?
Ignatius's Hot Deals

o: What is that cape you're wearing?

o.x: What is that cape you're wearing?
This is a Skillcape of Firemaking. I was given it in recognition of my skill as the greatest firemaker in the lands! I AM the Master of Flame!
Hmm, I'll be going now. Keep a sharp look out for those men with their white jackets!
No, thanks.
Okay, keep the fire burning.

nodes.x: What can My Arm do for you today, Player?

o.x: How's your farming coming along?
My Arm is getting good at dis. I growin' plenty of goutweed for Burntmeat, an' he very happy.
Good, good.
Anyfing else?
Nothing, thanks.
Dat okay, Player. Come back anytime you like.
Nothing, thanks.
Dat okay, Player. Come back anytime you like.

nodes.x: Do you want to go on a trip to Brimhaven?
The trip will cost you 30 coins.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Yes please.

b: If the player has enough money:

b.x: You pay 30 coins and board the ship.
The ship arrives at Brimhaven.

b: If the player does not have enough money:

b.x: Oh dear, I don't seem to have enough money.
You can not afford that.

b: If the player has completed the Easy Karamja achievements:

b.x: Wait a minute, didn't you earn Karamja gloves? Thought I'd seen you helping around the island. You can go on half price.
You pay 15 coins and board the ship.
The ship arrives at Brimhaven.

o.x: No thank you.

o: (With a ring of charos (a) equipped:) Or I could pay you nothing at all...

o.x: Or I could pay you nothing at all...
Mmmm, nothing at all, you say...
Yes, why not - jump aboard then.
You board the ship.
The ship arrives at Brimhaven.

nodes.x: Ah, 'tis a fine day! Can I help ye with tool storage, or a trip to Winkin's Farm, or what?
Choose...
I'm sick of this place.
What I wouldn't give for a good nights rest.
I feel so weak I could faint.
I'm sick of this place.
What I wouldn't give for a good nights rest.
I feel so weak I could faint.
Hey leave me alone, can't you see that I'm busy?
Hey leave me alone, can't you see that I'm busy?
Yeah, what do you want?

o.x: What is this place?
It's none of your business now get lost.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Perhaps five gold coins will make it my business?

o.x: Perhaps five gold coins will make it my business?
Well, it certainly will help... -- The guard takes the five gold coins. -- Now then, what did you want to know?
What is this place?
It's just a mining camp. Prisoners are sent here from Al Kharid. They serve out their sentence by mining. Most prisoners will end their days here, surrounded by desert.
So you could almost say that they got their ... 'Just Desserts'
You could say that... -- There is an awkward pause --
But it wouldn't be very funny.
When they talk about 'the silence of the desert', this must be what they mean.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Can I take a look around the place?

o.x: Can I take a look around the place?
Not really. The Captain won't let you in the compound. He's the only one who has the key to the gate. And if you talk to him, he'll probably just order us to kill you. Unless...

o.title: Select an Option
o: Does the Captain order you to kill a lot of people?

o.x: Does the Captain order you to kill a lot of people?
-- The guard snorts. -- *Snort* Just about anyone who talks to him.
Unless he has a use for you, he'll probably just order us to kill you. And it's such a horrible job cleaning up the mess afterwards.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Not to mention the senseless waste of human life.

o.x: Not to mention the senseless waste of human life.
Huh? Them's your words, not mine.

o.title: Select an Option
o: It doesn't sound as if you respect your Captain much.

o.x: It doesn't sound as if you respect your Captain much.
-- The guard looks around conspiratorially. --

Well, to be honest. We think he's not exactly as brave as he makes out. But we have to follow his orders. If someone called him a coward, or managed to trick him into a one-on-one duel many of us bet that he'd be beaten.
And how could I trick him into a one-on-one duel?

Like all cowards, he likes to be made to feel important. If anyone insults him outright, he just gets us to do his dirty work. However, if he thinks he's better than you, if you compliment him, he may feel that he can defeat you. And
if he initiated a duel, all the men agreed that they wouldn't intervene. We think he'd be slaughtered in double quick time.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Can I have a bet on that?

o.x: Can I have a bet on that?
Unless what?
Unless he has a use for you. He's been trying to track down someone called 'Al Zaba Bhasim'. You could offer to catch him and that might put you in his good books?

o.title: Select an Option
o: Where would I find this Al Zaba Bhasim?

o.x: Where would I find this Al Zaba Bhasim?
Well, he could be anywhere. He's a nomadic desert dweller. However, they say that he's frequently to be found to the west in the hospitality of the Tentis.
The Tentis, who are they?
Well, we're not really sure what their proper name is, but they live in tents so we call them the 'Tentis'.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Is Al Zaba Bhasim very tough?

o.x: Is Al Zaba Bhasim very tough?

Well, I'm not sure, but by all accounts, he is a slippery fellow. The Captain has been trying to capture him for years. A bit of a waste of time if you ask me. Anyway, I have to get going, I do have work to do.
The guard walks off.
What are you guarding?
Well, if you have to know, we're making sure that no prisoners get out. -- The guard gives you a disapproving look. -- And to make sure that unauthorised people don't get in.
-- The guard looks around nervously. -- You'd better go soon before the Captain orders us to kill you.
What are you guarding?
Get lost before I chop off your head!

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: Okay, thanks.
Yeah, whatever!

o: Perhaps these five gold coins will sweeten your mood?

o.x: Perhaps five gold coins will sweeten your mood?
5 coins have been removed from your money pouch.
Well, it certainly will help!
The guard takes the five gold coins.
Now then, what did you want to know?
What is this place?
It's none of your business now get lost.
What are you guarding?
Get lost before I chop off your head!

nodes.x: Yeah, what do you want?

o.x: What is this place?
It's none of your business now get lost.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Perhaps five gold coins will make it my business?

o.x: Perhaps five gold coins will make it my business?
Well, it certainly will help... -- The guard takes the five gold coins. -- Now then, what did you want to know?
What is this place?
It's just a mining camp. Prisoners are sent here from Al Kharid. They serve out their sentence by mining. Most prisoners will end their days here, surrounded by desert.
So you could almost say that they got their ... 'Just Desserts'
You could say that... -- There is an awkward pause --
But it wouldn't be very funny.
When they talk about 'the silence of the desert', this must be what they mean.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Can I take a look around the place?

o.x: Can I take a look around the place?
Not really. The Captain won't let you in the compound. He's the only one who has the key to the gate. And if you talk to him, he'll probably just order us to kill you. Unless...

o.title: Select an Option
o: Does the Captain order you to kill a lot of people?

o.x: Does the Captain order you to kill a lot of people?
-- The guard snorts. -- *Snort* Just about anyone who talks to him.
Unless he has a use for you, he'll probably just order us to kill you. And it's such a horrible job cleaning up the mess afterwards.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Not to mention the senseless waste of human life.

o.x: Not to mention the senseless waste of human life.
Huh? Them's your words, not mine.

o.title: Select an Option
o: It doesn't sound as if you respect your Captain much.

o.x: It doesn't sound as if you respect your Captain much.
-- The guard looks around conspiratorially. --

Well, to be honest. We think he's not exactly as brave as he makes out. But we have to follow his orders. If someone called him a coward, or managed to trick him into a one-on-one duel many of us bet that he'd be beaten.
And how could I trick him into a one-on-one duel?

Like all cowards, he likes to be made to feel important. If anyone insults him outright, he just gets us to do his dirty work. However, if he thinks he's better than you, if you compliment him, he may feel that he can defeat you. And
if he initiated a duel, all the men agreed that they wouldn't intervene. We think he'd be slaughtered in double quick time.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Can I have a bet on that?

o.x: Can I have a bet on that?
Unless what?
Unless he has a use for you. He's been trying to track down someone called 'Al Zaba Bhasim'. You could offer to catch him and that might put you in his good books?

o.title: Select an Option
o: Where would I find this Al Zaba Bhasim?

o.x: Where would I find this Al Zaba Bhasim?
Well, he could be anywhere. He's a nomadic desert dweller. However, they say that he's frequently to be found to the west in the hospitality of the Tentis.
The Tentis, who are they?
Well, we're not really sure what their proper name is, but they live in tents so we call them the 'Tentis'.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Is Al Zaba Bhasim very tough?

o.x: Is Al Zaba Bhasim very tough?

Well, I'm not sure, but by all accounts, he is a slippery fellow. The Captain has been trying to capture him for years. A bit of a waste of time if you ask me. Anyway, I have to get going, I do have work to do.
The guard walks off.
What are you guarding?
Well, if you have to know, we're making sure that no prisoners get out. -- The guard gives you a disapproving look. -- And to make sure that unauthorised people don't get in.
-- The guard looks around nervously. -- You'd better go soon before the Captain orders us to kill you.
What are you guarding?
Get lost before I chop off your head!

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: Okay, thanks.
Yeah, whatever!

o: Perhaps these five gold coins will sweeten your mood?

o.x: Perhaps five gold coins will sweeten your mood?
5 coins have been removed from your money pouch.
Well, it certainly will help!
The guard takes the five gold coins.
Now then, what did you want to know?
What is this place?
It's none of your business now get lost.
What are you guarding?
Get lost before I chop off your head!

nodes.x: Hello?
Sorry soldier, you don't have permission to speak with me yet. Go and talk to the Captain.
Hello. What's this place?
Why you wretched Son-of-a-Big-Nosed-Warty-Smelly-Goblin! How dare you speak to a commanding officer like that?
I...err... What?
Stand straight! Chest out, shoulders back!
Okay, okay.
You'll address me as captain!
Yea...yes, captain!
Better. Now what is a low-life, pathetic excuse for a human being doing sniffing around my arena?
Exploring, captain. Looked like a chance for combat, sir!
And you think you have what is necessary to take on the Penance? No chance.
With respect, captain, I don't understand what this place is.
You really are useless, aren't you? Very well, make the most of this because I don't suffer idiots easily! This is the Barbarian Assault arena. You want to sign up with us?

o.x: Sir, yes sir!
Then listen closely.
Barbarian Assault tutorial

nodes.x: Hi there.
Don't suppose you've seen a battleaxe around here?
A battleaxe? Nope, afraid not.
The captain is going to kill me if he finds out I've lost my weapon.
Hello. So you're just a private?
Show some respect! It's more than you'll achieve.
I beg to differ. I'm in perfect shape!
Prove it!
How?
Give me five star jumps!
Five sit-ups!
Run on the spot!
Okay. Maybe you have what it takes. Best you speak with the captain.
Hi.
Shhh. Don't talk to me.
What? Why?
If I'm seen slacking off by talking to you, I'll be in deep trouble!
Oh... Sorry.
Hello, Player. It is good to see you again. My enterprise has grown since we last met. I've expanded all over Gielinor!
If you'd like to go to a new location, you will have to help fly the balloon again. Some of the routes are very dangerous!
But each route you complete will earn you Firemaking experience.
Once you've opened a route, it only costs 1 log of the corresponding type to travel there again, from any location you've already opened!
I have also hired assistants to watch over the balloons at each new location we go to. They will help you get where you want to go.
Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.
Hello there.
Greetings. Can I help you at all?

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Do you have any quests I could do?

o.x: Do you have any quests I could do?
A quest? What a strange notion. Do you normally go around asking complete strangers for quests?
Er, yes, now you come to mention it.
Oh, ok then. Well, no, I don't; sorry.
What is this place?
A good question; straight and to the point. My name is Matthias, I am a falconer, and this is where I train my birds.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Do you have any quests I could do?
That sounds like fun; could I have a go?
That doesn't sound like my sort of thing.

o.x: That doesn't sound like my sort of thing.
Fair enough; it does require a great deal of patience and skill, so I can understand if you might feel intimidated.

o: What's this falconry thing all about then?

o.x: What's this falconry thing all about then?

Well, some people see it as a sport, although such a term does not really convey the amount of patience and dedication required to be proficient at the task. Putting it simply, it is the training and use of birds of prey in hunting quarry.
So it's like keeping a pet then?

Not exactly, no. Such a bird can never really be considered tame in the same way that a dog can. They can be trained to associate people or places with food though, and, as such, a good falconer can get a trained bird to do as he wishes.

o: Could I have a go with your bird?

o.x: Could I have a go with your bird?

Training falcons is a lot of work and I doubt you're up to the task. However, I suppose I could let you try hunting with one. I have some tamer birds that I occasionally lend to rich noblemen who consider it a sufficiently refined sport for their tastes, and you look like the kind who might appreciate a good hunt. I'd have to request a small fee, mind you; how does 500 gold pieces sound?
Ok, that seems reasonable.
The falconer gives you a large leather glove and brings one of the smaller birds over to land on it.
Don't worry; I'll keep an eye on you to make sure you don't upset it too much.
I'm not interested then, thanks.
Well, you're welcome to come back if you change your mind.

b: If the player is wearing any items in their main- or off-hand slot, or their glove slot

o.x: Sorry, you really need both hands free for falconry. I'd suggest that you put away your weapons and gloves before we start.

nodes.x: Greetings, friend. My business here deals with Hunter- related items. Is there anything in which I can interest you?

nodes.title: Choose an option:
o: What kinds of items do you stock?

Take a look for yourself.
Nardah Hunter Shop

o: I'm not in the market for Hunter equipment right now, thanks.

o.x: I'm not in the market for Hunter equipment right now, thanks.
Maybe another time, then.

o: Do you have any Hunter wisdom to share?

o.x: Do you have any Hunter wisdom to share?
Some creatures can be particularly fond of certain food. If you bait your trap you are more likely to succeed.
So I need to use bait?
Sometimes it's essential. Creatures in Isafdar, for example, won't go near a trap that isn't baited. They are clever animals but quite greedy, it seems.

o.title: Select an option
o: Can you tell me more about hunting in Isafdar?

o.x: Can you tell me more about hunting in Isafdar?
There are two animals ideal for hunting there: the pawya and the grenwall. Grenwall hunt for pawya, so pawya meat is a good bait to catch them.
And what about catching pawya?
From the Hunter tales I've heard around campfires, they seem to find papaya fruit irresistable.
Is there anything else in which I can interest you?
Thanks for your help.
It's always a pleasure to share Hunter knowledge.
Is there anything else in which I can interest you?

nodes.x: Hello.
Hello, hello, and a most warm welcome to my Hunter Emporium. We have everything the discerning Hunter could need.
Would you like me to show you our range of equipment? Or was there something specific you were after?

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Okay, let's see what you've got.

o.x: Okay, let's see what you've got.
Aleck's Hunter Emporium
I'm not interested, thanks.
Well, if you do ever find yourself in need of the finest Hunter equipment available, then you know where to come.
Who's that guy over there?
Him? I think he might be crazy. Either that or he's seeking attention.
He keeps trying to sell me these barmy looking weapons he's invented. I can't see them working, personally.

o: Do you have any Hunter wisdom to share?

o.x: Do you have any Hunter wisdom to share?
Some creatures can be particularly fond of certain food. If you bait your trap it's more likely that you'll catch the critters.
So, I need to use bait?
Sometimes it's essential. I remember when I was hunting in Isafdar, the animals there wouldn't even look at a trap unless I used bait. Those pawya and grenwalls aren't easily fooled.

o.title: Select an Option
o: How did you find out which bait to use?

o.x: How did you find out which bait to use?
After watching them for a while I noticed that the grenwalls ate the pawya, so I realised I could use pawya meat to catch grenwall.
But how did you catch the pawya to start with?
That was harder to figure out. I could tell they didn't eat meat, so I tried other baits and found out that they couldn't resist papaya fruit.
Anyway, would you like me to show you our range of equipment or was there something specific you were after?
Thanks for your help.
It's always a pleasure to share Hunter knowledge.
Would you like me to show you our range of equipment or was there something specific you were after?

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Ardougne set, you are presented with a cloak.
This cloak will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Ardougne set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Ardougne set rewards, speak to Ardougne's town crier, Doctor Orbon in East Ardougne church, or myself.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: What is this place?
This is Aleck's Hunter Emporium. Basically, it's just a shop with a fancy name; you can buy various weapons and traps here.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Can I buy some equipment then?

o.x: Can I buy some equipment then?
Oh, this isn't my shop; the owner is Aleck over there behind the counter.
I experiment with weapon designs. I'm here because I've been trying to convince people to back my research and maybe sell some of my products - like this one I'm holding - in their shops.
Aleck doesn't seem to be interested, though.

o: Can I have a go with your crossbow?
What is that thing you're holding?
Can I have a go with your crossbow?

o.x: Could I have a go with your crossbow?
I'm afraid with it being a prototype, I've only got a few for my own testing purposes.
Of course, for the right price, it might be worth my while to make another prototype.
How much?
To you, 1300 gold pieces.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: Ok, here you go.

b.x: Well, you look a little overburdened there at the moment. Maybe you should free up some space to carry it in first.
You can not afford that.
Oh, actually I don't have enough money with me.
You hand over the money and the weapon designer presents you with a prototype crossbow.
Here, you might as well take this one. Aleck over there doesn't seem interested and it'll save you a wait.

o: I'll give it a miss, thanks.

o.x: I'll give it a miss, thanks.
Your loss; they'll probably become highly valuable and sought after once I convince someone to market the things.

o: Does it use normal crossbow bolts?

o.x: Does it use normal crossbow bolts?
Ah, I admit as a result of its er...unique construction, it won't take just any old bolts.
If you can supply the materials and a token fee, I'd be happy to make some for you.
What materials do you need?
Kebbit spikes. Lots of 'em. Not all kebbits have spikes, mind you. You'll be needing to look for prickly kebbits or, even better, razor-backed kebbits to get material hard enough.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Let's see what you can make then.

o.x: (Hunting Bolts interface opens.)

o: I'll give it a miss, thanks.

o.x: I'll give it a miss, thanks.
Well, if you ever find yourself in need of that innovative edge, you know who to contact.
Er, yes, of course.

o: Can't I just make my own?

o.x: Can't I just make my own?
Yes, I suppose you could, although you'll need a steady hand with a knife and chisel.
The bolts have an unusual diameter, but basically you'll just need to be able to carve kebbit spikes into straight shafts.
Great; thanks.
What are you holding there?
This? This is a prototype for a new type of crossbow I've been designing.
It looks pretty weird.
It's good, isn't it? It includes the bones of various animals in its construction.
It's also a fair bit faster than an ordinary crossbow too; it'll take you far less time to reload between shots.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: That's crazy, it'll never work!
That's what they said about my wind-powered mouse traps, too.
And did they work?
Well, they only ran into problems because people kept insisting on trying to use them indoors.

o: Could I have a go with it?
Does it use normal crossbow bolts?

nodes.x: Ah, this is a wonderful area for a spot of hunting, don't you think?

nodes.title: Choose an option:

o.x: I don't know, is it?

Oh, absolutely! There's a huge variety of creatures to catch around here. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds, skillchompas, and even kyatts! Surely one of those piques your interest.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Where would I find polar kebbits?

o.x: Where would I find polar kebbits?
Funnily enough, you've just put your finger on the problem. With polar kebbits, finding them is the hardest part! You'll have to track them down.
How would I go about doing them, then?

The easiest way to get started is by looking somewhere you can be sure a kebbit will have been and then working from there. You see the holes around here leading down into the ice? They're kebbit burrows!
You'll be hard pressed to find a polar kebbit in its home, but if you search around the entrance to a burrow then you might be able to find a trail.

Now, kebbit trails are usually fairly easy to follow once you've found them, but if the trail does peter out, you should try inspecting the surrounding scenery for clues as to where the creature may have gone.
Good places to look for clues include hollow logs in which the kebbit may have hidden or vegetation which may have been chewed or damaged.
There are also tunnels running through the ice that the kebbits use, so you should check those out as well.
What's more, these tunnels can often help to shelter a trail from further snow, making it even easier for you to pick them up again.
Eventually, of course, the kebbit will have probably hidden somewhere. Polar kebbits don't hang about in the open for too long for fear of their natural predators.
If you suspect a kebbit is close by, try looking around for signs of disturbed snow. Polar kebbits will often bury themselves in snow drifts as a means of hiding.
If you think you've found a kebbit, use a noose wand to haul the creature out from the snow.
Wow, that's quite a lot to remember.
Don't worry, if you find yourself struggling to follow a trail, just come and ask me and I'll see if I can help.
But remember, the best place to start is by searching around their burrows.
Great, thanks.
How do you hunt birds?
Ah, you can get cunning little bird snares for just that. You should be able to find them in specialist Hunter shops. Try to lay them in fairly open areas with lots of birds.
Do I need to place any bait on these traps?

No, that’s not necessary. The idea is that the bird will see the trap as somewhere to perch. If the bird lands on the trigger stick, it should drop away and a small loop of wire should close around the bird’s feet.
And remember, it’s important to collect any captures from your traps fairly quickly, otherwise, you risk losing them to various wild scavengers.

o.title: Select an Option
o: I’d like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

o.x: How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Ah, the key there is concealment, both of yourself and your traps.
The most obvious point is to stay out of sight of your own traps. If possible, hide around a wall, hedge or similar. Failing that, make sure you’re a good few feet away from your trap.
You can hide yourself even better by wearing clothing appropriate to the area in which you are hunting.
Your best bet is to use the skins of creatures native to the area. There is a very good tailor in east Varrock who may be able to help you in making clothing out of such skins.
Finally, a lot of creatures may avoid your traps if they can smell a human scent on them.This is where smoking a trap may be useful.
It takes a bit of practice, but by using the smoke from a torch, you can mask any other scents that may surround a trap.
Wow, thanks for your help.
Thanks for your help.
What's so special about butterflies?
That depends entirely on the butterfly.
I’ll admit that the activities of many butterflies may be of no interest at all. However, we are lucky around here in having some fine examples of thaumic butterflies.
These butterflies reputedly have magical powers that, when released, can make a person stronger or heal otherwise critical wounds.
At this point, I should offer a word of caution: it is also said that these powers will not manifest themselves if the butterflies are captured for selfish purposes.
Rather, they are gifts that must be used by one person to aid another. Of course, you’ll have to catch them first.
And how do I do that?
Why, with a butterfly net of course! You should also carry some empty butterfly jars with you in which to keep the butterflies.

o.title: Select an Option
o: I’d like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?

o.x: How can I capture a sabre-toothed kebbit?
Ah, now for these creatures I would recommend using a deadfall trap. Deadfalls are quite easy to set up,and yet you can catch some very reasonably sized creatures with them.
Deadfall traps basically work by having a large dead weight, such as a boulder, positioned so as to be delicately balanced above some form of bait.
You will need to make sure you have a knife and some wood with you to create appropriate supports and a trigger for this sort trap.
In the case of sabre-toothed kebbits you should use some form of raw meat to bait your trap, but other animals may prefer other baits, such as fish or vegetables.

o.title: Select an Option
o: I’d like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

o.x: What are skillchompas?
Good question. They seem to be a sort of mutated chinchompa, except instead of getting very excited and exploding in combat situations, they've taken a liking to a variety of natural resources.
What sorts of things do they go for then?
Well, they've clearly been watching humans who have been training their skills and abilities. They seem to get very excited around the divination energy, fishing spots, mining rocks and even trees!
How would I hunt them then?
They're very similar to chinchompas, so you'll need some box traps. If you really want to attract them you can use some bait as well. Spicy food seems to do the trick.

o.title: Select an Option
o: I’d like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?

o.x: Oooh, kyatts sound interesting. I want to catch one of those.
Well, you've set your sights high, kyatts are incredibly fearsome creatures, but with determination like that I'm sure you'll make it.
Now, you're not going to be able to catch a kyatt with just a small box or a noose or a stick. You need a much bigger trap.
Pit traps are a good bet. You'd be best off finding a natural dip in the ground as the basis for your trap. If you dig a pit yourself, you risk creatures noticing the disturbed ground nearby.
Once you've found an appropriate spot, you'll need some logs and a knife. The logs serve two purposes.
Some can be carved into sharp skewers for the bottom of the pit; hopefully the kyatt will die when it falls onto these. Others can be used to conceal the trap.
Of course, even then the pit is going to look suspicious, so you're going to need to lure the kyatt onto the branches in some way. What actually tends to work best is, well, yourself!
What? I don't like the sound of that.
Yes, that's the normal response, but I kid you not. If you really want a kyatt to follow you over that pit then just give it a good poke!
Of course, I suggest you use something long to poke it with. Poking a kyatt with your finger is likely to end in permanent limb loss.
Fortunately, you can get very good sticks for poking from most Hunter shops.

Once you have...got the creature's attention, try to lead it to one of your traps. Make sure to jump the branches when you reach the trap yourself, of course; it would be embarrassing to fall into your own trap.
Then, if the kyatt is giving you all of its attention, hopefully it won't notice the trap, and with any luck, it will stumble right into the pit.
That sounds a bit hit or miss, and kind of suicidal too!
Well that's what makes it exciting, isn't it? But honestly, if you want to capture a kyatt, that's your best bet.

o.title: Select an Option
o: I’d like to ask about another creature.
How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Can you teach me out to hunt?

o.x: Can you teach me out to hunt?
Why certainly. I reached the peak of my abilities some time ago, but I'm more than happy to help newcomers to the field. Was there anything in particular you had in mind?

o.title: Select an Option
o: Where is the best place to start?

o.x: Where is the best place to start?
I always say a good starting point is to learn how to follow the creatures you want to capture. Around here, that means practicing on polar kebbits.
So how do I track them down, then?

o: What sort of creatures are there to hunt around here?

o.x: What sort of creatures are there to hunt around here?
Well, there's pretty much anything you could want to hunt. You've got butterflies, polar kebbits, sabre-toothed kebbits, birds, skillchompas, and even kyatts! Surely one of those interests you.

o: Do you have anything for sale?

o.x: Do you have anything for sale?
I reckon I've got some hunting gear knocking around that you might be interested in.
Hunting Supplies (Rellekka Hunter area)

o: How can I improve my chances of capturing a creature?
Sorry, I'm not that keen on hunting.

o.x: Sorry, I'm not that keen on hunting.
What a shame, you looked like someone who could have had some promise.

nodes.title: What would you like to talk about?
o: Can you help me with the trapper outfits?

o.x: Can you help me with the trapper outfits?

o.x: Whoah there, stranger, careful where you're walking. I almost clobbered you there; thought you were a larupia or something.

o.title: Select an Option

o.x: What are you doing here?
Me? Oh, I'm just having some fun, capturing wild animals, living on the edge, stuff like that.
Hey, want me to teach you how to catch the critters around here? Ain't come across anything yet that I couldn't capture.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Okay, where's a good place to start?

o.x: Ok, where's a good place to start?

Your easiest bet around here is probably to go for some of the birds. Go for the crimson swifts; they're the bright red ones that hang around near the coast. They're as obliging as can be, or maybe they're just plain dumb, but either way they just seem to throw themselves into traps half the time.
What sort of traps should I use?
Just use a standard bird snare and you'll be fine. You can get them in any decent shop that sells Hunter gear.
How do they work, then?

Well, they're kind of sneaky, really. You've got a tall post with what appears to be a little perch sticking out the side. Now, the bird will see this as somewhere to sit, but the perch is actually rigged such that when the bird lands on it, it'll drop away.
Further, as the perch drops, it releases a noose that tightens around the bird's feet and captures it. Neat huh?
So, was there anything else you wanted to ask about?

o.title: Select an Option
o: What other sorts of things are there to catch around here?

o.x: What other sorts of things are there to catch around here?
Thanks for your help.
Not a problem, any time.

o: What sort of things are there to catch around here?

o.x: What sort of things are there to catch around here?
What're you interested in? You've got anything from birds for beginners up to larupias for the pros - not to mention weasels, butterflies, barb-tails, chinchompas and skillchompas.

o.title: Select an Option
o: How would I go about catching birds?

o.x: How would I go about catching birds?
There are a couple of varieties that you can try your hand at catching around here, but the technique for both is essentially the same. You need to set up a bird snare.
How do they work, then?

Well, they're kind of sneaky, really. You've got a tall post with what appears to be a little perch sticking out the side. Now, the bird will see this as somewhere to sit, but the perch is actually rigged such that when the bird lands on it, it'll drop away.
Further, as the perch drops, it releases a noose that tightens around the bird's feet and captures it. Neat, huh?
So, was there anything else you wanted to ask about?

o.title: Select an Option
o: I'd like to ask about another creature...
How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
How do I get hold of a weasel?

o.x: How do I get hold of a weasel?

Not with large quantities of rice and treacle as many people would have you believe. Besides, the Feldip weasel isn't technically a weasel, but, as is typical with any sort of colloquial name, it's been called that often enough now that it's stuck.
Anyway, the Feldip weasel's main survival technique is in hiding; other than that, it's pretty stupid. So, if you can actually find one, then you've probably got a fairly good chance of catching one.
And how would I actually go about finding one?
The best place to start would probably be just south of here. You'll find lots of kebbit burrows there. Take a close look at some of them, follow the trails and you can't go far wrong.

o: Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...

o.x: Well, seeing as you seem to like larupias so much...
Ah yes, yes, larupias are fun; just think of them as big kittens.
Uh huh, big kittens that just want to rip your throat out!
Indeed, and you can use this to your advantage. If a larupia is keen to chase you then let it; that way you can happily lead it straight into your trap without any fuss or waiting around.
Into what sort of trap should I lead it?
A pit trap should do you. There are some appropriate pits to the east of here that you can use. Cover one with a few logs and branches, tease the kitty and then lead it to the pit. Simple.
Barb-tails sound interesting.

They do sound interesting, don't they? Unfortunately, they're actually just another type of kebbit; those things get everywhere. Still, the tails of these particular kebbits can be useful for fishing.
So, how would I go about catching one them?
Just squash them with a boulder, quick and simple.
What, you mean just pick up some boulders and start throwing them at kebbits? That doesn't sound simple.
No silly, you let the creature squash itself. Just use some sticks to hold a boulder in a nice precarious position, place some bait underneath and let the creature knock itself out.

o.title: Select an Option
o: What on earth is a chinchompa?

o.x: What on earth is a chinchompa?
Awwww, chinchompas are great. They're highly volatile little balls of fluff. Cute as you like, but for some reason they do have this tendency to spontaneously combust.
What? Why?
Probably something to do with the fact they'll eat anything and everything, especially spicy food.
Anyways, if you want to capture a chinchompa, I suggest using a box trap. That way, if the little fluffball does explode, then at least most of the blast will be contained within the box.
A skill-what now?
A skillchompa! They seem to be a sort of mutated chinchompa, except instead of getting very excited and exploding in combat situations, they've taken a liking to a variety of natural resources.
What sorts of things do they go for then?
Well, they've clearly been watching humans who've been training their skills and abilities. They seem to get very excited around the divination energy, fishing spots, mining rocks and even trees!
How do I hunt them then?
They're very similar to chinchompas, so you'll need some box traps. If you really want to attract them you can use some bait as well. Spicy food seems to do the trick.

o: Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.

o.x: Somehow butterflies don't strike me as your sort of thing.
Not really, but some people like them. The ones around here are at least vaguely interesting, though. The black ones are supposedly magical butterflies.
Doesn't that make them harder to catch?
Not particularly; you can still catch them using an ordinary butterfly net. Oh, and you'll probably need some butterfly jars in which to keep them as well.

o: How can I improve my chances of making a capture?

o.x: How can I improve my chances of making a capture?
There are four key factors that will affect your chances: what bait you use, how close to the trap you are, your appearance and your smell.

o.title: Select an option

o.x: How does bait help?

Unfortunately, creatures don't just jump into traps for the fun of it nearly as often as we as hunters might like. However, it is possible to improve those odds if you can find the right bait to use on your trap - something your

prey really craves - then hunger overrides fear and the creature is just that little bit more likely to bounce to its furry little doom. Some creatures, in fact, will not even approach a trap unless it is baited correctly.

o: Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

o.x: Why is it important how close I am to the trap?

However well you might be blending in, if you're standing with your nose pressed right up against your own trap, the poor little critters ain't going to go anywhere near it. So, you need to make sure you put a sensible distance -
I'd say at least four strides - between yourself and your trap.

o: Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

o.x: Why would the creatures care about my appearance?

You're a human. From the point of view of a lot of creatures, you're big and scary. So, it'd be best if the furry little monsters didn't notice you. You need to blend in like the creatures themselves.
And how do I do that?

Easy, dress up like one of them. Even easier, dress up using the furs of the creatures themselves; then you're bound to get the colour right. And, I suppose, if you don't fancy just slinging a dead fur over your shoulders, you
can probably get them made into something more appealing. I hear there are tailors in Varrock who are good at that sort of thing.
What's wrong with my smell?

I'm sure there's nothing wrong with your smell...from a human point of view. But to your prey, any trap that you've set up will reek of human, and that's going to work against you if you don't do anything about it.
So what should I do?

You need to mask that lovely human scent of yours with something else. Smoke works well. Take a lit torch and waft it around the trap a bit. You'll quickly overpower most of the other smells around the trap.

o: Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?

o.x: Where can I get clothes and equipment like yours?
Well, the equipment isn't too hard to get hold of. You've got specialist shops like Aleck's in Yanille that'll see you right. He's a bit pricey, mind, but it's pretty decent kit.
The clothing is a tad trickier to get hold of, the materials required being rather difficult to separate from their reluctant owners.
But, if you can get the furs, there are shops like the tailor's in east Varrock that can help you.

If you want to be successful as a hunter you've got to be as stealthy as a kyatt, as quiet as a mouse and blend in like a, well, like a larupia, I guess!

nodes.x: I think that Ur-tag is trying to move too quickly. First, he opens the city to humans, and now he wants to invite these dwarves into the city. I think we should exercise more caution in dealing with surface-dwellers.
The dwarves are not surface dwellers. They live in an underground city, like us!
Why does that mean we can trust them? Are you forgetting the machine that nearly destroyed us was made by dwarves?
You shouldn't judge all dwarves because of that!
I know that! And I know not all humans want to kill us, but I still never thought we should open the city.
You can't deny it's done some good. Think of how happy everyone is trying surface foods in the market!
I'm not denying that, I just don't think it's worth the risk. Our guards have their work cut out as it is, protecting us from renegade humans, without having to worry about dwarves as well.
Please don't be offended by my friend's attitude, surface- dweller. I'm sure you understand why we need to be cautious.
Of course.
Ah. Player, I presume?
That's me.

o.x: What are you doing?
I'm writing the definitive history of Dorgesh-Kaan!
Actually, I wonder if you could help me...
I know the ruler of Lumbridge is called Horacio, but I don't know what his title is. Can you tell me?
He's a duke.
Duke Horacio. Thank you.
He's a general.
General Horacio. Thank you.
He's a king.
King Horacio. Thank you.
He's a lord.
Lord Horacio. Thank you.
You've talked to the goblins on the surface, haven't you? Do you know the name of the god that the surface goblins worship?
Nobody knows.
Oh well. Thanks anyway.

Ah, thank you.
It was Zamorak.
Ah, thank you.
It was Guthix.
Ah, thank you.
It was Saradomin.
Ah, thank you.
It was Player.

b: If the goblin scribe thinks the war was because Guthix wanted to preserve balance:

b.x: In order to preserve balance, the god Guthix made the other gods fight against one another. The goblins were sent to fight in many bloody battles against each other and other races.

o.x: The war lasted for thousands of years, and millions of goblins died. Eventually, the evil god sent the Dorgeshuun tribe to fight a battle that they could not win.
But General Bloodfist of the Dorgeshuun refused to fight in this battle. Instead, he commanded the Dorgeshuun army to march down into a fissure in the ground.
General Bloodfist stood at the mouth of the fissure and defied the might of the evil god.
The evil god smote him with a mighty blast that shook the earth, but that blast also closed the fissure, sealing the Dorgeshuun away from the reach of the gods.
Lieutenant Strongaxe, now the leader of the Dorgeshuun, led the tribe deeper into the caves. They found this cavern, and here they founded Dorgesh-Kaan, city of the Dorgeshuun.
Can you tell me about the Dorgeshuun civil war?
Certainly! *Ahem*
At first, Dorgesh-Kaan was ruled over by generals, just as the tribe had been when it was on the surface. Each general succeeded the last by defeating him in combat.
The generals were advised by a council of elders, but the Dorgeshuun were no longer an army, and many of the people felt that the Council should have authority.
The people voted to become a republic, but General Bonehelm refused to give up power, and so the Dorgeshuun Civil War began.
The republican faction was larger, but the military faction contained most of the trained warriors and controlled the magical equipment that the tribe had brought from the surface.
General Bonehelm was driven from the city, but dug his own base out of the caves nearby.
General Bonehelm's army attacked the city using archers mounted on giant frogs. There was a bloody battle, and General Bonehelm was driven back again into his base.
But General Bonehelm's mining had weakened the stone around his base, and the retreating army's footsteps caused the roof to collapse, crushing his army.
That was the last time one Dorgeshuun has raised arms against another. Since then, the city has been ruled peacefully by an elected council.
Can you tell me about recent years?
Ah, this is where you come in! *Ahem*

In the twenty-ninth century since the founding of the city, one of the miners broke through a wall into the cellar of a surface dwelling. The miners blocked up the tunnel and went back into their mines.

o.x: How can I sell food?
Most of the people wandering around the market want to buy food. Since the passage to the surface opened up there's been a craze in exotic food from up there.
To sell something, simply use a piece of food on one of the gourmets in the market, then name your price, and the gourmet will tell you how many they are interested in buying for that price.
If you want a rough idea of how much something will sell for, show it to me and I'll try to estimate.
But you should also take into account the gourmet's reactions when naming your price. If someone likes the look of a food, they will pay more for it.
Also remember that the novelty of new foods quickly wears off. If people have been eating a lot of something lately, then they won't pay as much for it.
If someone especially likes your food then you might even start a craze for it! If there's a food that's in fashion like that, then the gourmets will pay more for it.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Varrock set, you are presented with some body armour.
This armour will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in the set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Most of the Varrock set's Tasks are straightforward, though you might find some require quests to be started, if not finished.
To claim your Varrock set reward, speak to Reldo in Varrock Library, Vannaka in Edgeville, or me.

Hah! I knew it! I expect you want my Aphro-Dizzy-Yak spell! Want someone to fall madly in love with you, eh?
That spell sounds very interesting, but I didn't mean to disturb you!

Well, I see that you do have some manners. I'm glad to see that you use them. Now, if it's all the same, I am very busy at the moment. Unless you want something specific, please come back another time.
Yes, of course. Goodbye!

o.x: Who are you?

Sorry! I didn't mean to pry!
That's alright. My name is Louisiana Jones, although most people call me Anna. I'm an archaeologist.
Oh. Do you work for the Varrock Museum?
Hah! No. I used to, but now I prefer to work freelance for independent employers.
I see.

Hi there.
Dakh'thoulan Aegis: Hello, young one. What brings you to our humble dwelling?
I was wondering what this place was?

Dakh'thoulan Aegis: These are the Tunnels of Chaos. They radiate with the energy of chaos magic. At the far end of the tunnel, you will find a portal to the Chaos Altar itself where chaos runes are crafted!

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Why is the tunnel so short?

o.x: Why is the tunnel so short?
Dakh'thoulan Aegis: The nature of chaos magic itself is mysterious and hard to understand.
What do you mean?

Dakh'thoulan Aegis: The tunnel is here, and yet it is not here. We also are here, where we should be, yet we are somewhere else. And so, the tunnel goes from one place to another, yet touches neither.
I really don't understand.

Dakh'thoulan Aegis: I told you you wouldn't. The best way to think of it is that the tunnel is like a gateway that allows you to travel from one place in the world to another in a more safe and convenient way.
Oh, I think I see. So it is like a magical alternate route?
Dakh'thoulan Aegis: Exactly! Well done! And at the end, there is a portal which will transport you to the Chaos Altar.
Oh, ok.

o.title: Select an Option

What does that mean?
Dakh'thoulan Aegis: It means we cannot always believe what we are told to believe. You would do well to remember that.
I will! Thank you!

o: Why are there only three of you?

o.x: Why are there only three of you?
Dakh'thoulan Aegis: Our order is a secret one and those of us that remain and survive through the ages choose to hide ourselves away.

Dakh'thoulan Aegis: We have built or found many tunnels such as these. This is not the only one. Rest assured, there are many more of us around.

Dakh'thoulan Aegis: Yes, I can understand you would expect it to be since the tunnel leads to the Chaos Altar. And yet, the tunnel does not enter the Wilderness, no. Rest assured, you are safe here and should not come to harm.
