o: I need a Rated Clan Wars badge.

b: If the player is not in a clan

b.x: You need to be in a clan to get a badge. I can't just give them out to just anyone. Talk to the clan scribe over there. He can help you set up a clan.

b: If the player is in a clan
If the player does not have an Rcw badge in the inventory

b.x: The sergeant hands you an RCW badge.

b: If the player has an Rcw badge in the inventory

b.x: You've already got a badge. Don't waste my time.

o.x: See you around.

nodes.x: Good day, sir. How may I be of assistance?
Choose an option:
Hello.
Quickly - Tell me, is it still there?
Is what still where?
The THING, the THING! It was just outside my house! Has it gone away yet? Or is it still lurking out there, waiting for me to go outside?
I didn't see any THING out there, just a couple of guards. What did it look like?
Ohhh, it was HORRIBLE! It was an enormous THING, with TEETH and EYES and... and... and THINGS!
Um... would you care to be more specific?
I can't. I only saw it in the dark.
You only saw this THING in the dark?

I was sleeping peacefully one night, when suddenly I woke up and saw it through the window. It was LOOKING at me! I haven't dared go out since then. It's had me trapped in here for days! I've packed my
bags so I can escape, but the THING's still out there waiting for me to come out! If I have to stay in here much longer I'll go mad! MAD!! MAD!!
There's no THING outside. Just come out and get some fresh air before you go funny in the head.
You want me to go outside?
I think you might just have dreamed about the THING.
You want me to believe that it's not real?
Please come outside!
No! No! I know what you are! You're in league with the THING! It keeps sending people in here to trick me into going outside! They keep stealing from me too! GO AWAY!
I'm not trying to trick you!
Get thee gone, trickster!
Sheesh...
Hello, how's it going?

b.x: I'm fine. How are you?
Very well, thank you.
I'm very well thank you.
Hello there! Nice weather we've been having.
I'm a little worried - I've heard there's lots of people going about, killing citizens at random.
Not too bad, but I'm a little worried about the increase of goblins these days.
Don't worry, I'll kill them.
Hello.
Not too bad thanks.
Who are you?
I'm a bold adventurer.
Ah, a very noble profession.
I'm sorry I can't help you there.
I'm busy right now.
Get out of my way, I'm in a hurry.
Do I know you? I'm in a hurry!
How can I help you?

b.title: Select an Option

o.x: No, I have nothing I wish to get rid of. If you want to do some trading, there are plenty of shops and market stalls around though.

o: I'm in search of a quest.

o.x: I'm sorry I can't help you there.

o: I'm in search of enemies to kill.

o.x: I've hear there are many fearsome creatures that dwell under the ground...

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Can I have a newspaper, please?

o.x: Can I have a newspaper, please?
Certainly, [Guv/Missus]. That'll be 50 gold pieces, please.

o.title: Select an Option

b: If the player does not have enough money:

b.x: You can not afford that.
Oh dear, I don't seem to have enough money with me.
Well, no cash, no paper. Live in ignorance.

b: If the player has enough money:

b.x: Read All About It

o: Uh, no thanks, I've changed my mind.

o.x: No, thanks.
Ok, suit yourself. Plenty more fish in the sea.

o: How much does a paper cost?

o.x: How much does a paper cost?
Just 50 gold pieces! An absolute bargain! Want one?
Yes, please.

o: Varrock Herald? Never heard of it.

o.x: Varrock Herald? Never heard of it.

For the illiterate amongst us, I shall elucidate. The Varrock Herald is a new newspaper. It is edited, printed and published by myself, Benny Gutenberg, and each edition promises to enthrall the reader with captivating
material! Now, can I interest you in buying one for a mere 50 gold ?
Anything interesting in there?
Of course there is, mate. Packed full of thought provoking insights, contentious interviews and celebrity scandalmongering! An excellent read and all for just 50 coins! Want one?

nodes.x: Hello.
Ahh, many greetinks and welcomes to ze Museum!
Choose an option:
Hello!
Hello there, welcome to Varrock Museum! Can I help you?

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Tell me about the Museum.
Well, as you can see we have recently expanded a great deal to cope with the influx of finds from the Dig Site. Also, of course, to prepare for the new dig we're opening soon.

o.title: Select an Option
o: Tell me about the new dig.

o.x: Tell me about the new dig.

Well, we recently had a large chunk of funds donated to us, so we sent out all sorts of explorers - I'm sure you'll meet them as you go around the world. People like Simon down in the desert near the pyramid as well as

Aristarchus in Pollnivneach, Varmen and, of course, Anna Jones. Anyway, we think we have discovered an island that has massive archaeological significance. We can't say much beyond that at this point, as we haven't researched
it. If you have the qualifications and help us out around the Museum, I'm sure we could offer you a place on the dig when we're ready to go.
That would be very nice.

o: I have some information that might be of use in your displays.
Tell me about other sections of the Museum.

o.x: Tell me about other sections of the Museum.
I'd be delighted to; which areas are you interested in?
Tell me about the Natural History exhibit.

Ah, our newest expansion. The Natural History exhibit in the basement was set up to inform our citizens of the weird and wonderful diversity in our environment today. Indeed, I am sure you will recognise some of the
creatures down there. Hopefully, our lectures will teach you some things you didn't know about them!
So where does the 'history' bit come in?
Ah, I see. The 'history' refers to that of the species - it doesn't necessarily mean it's died out. After all, we have human history and we're still here!
I guess that makes sense.
Tell me about the Dig Site exhibit.
Ahh, those. We're slowly filling them up with the help of people who have their Earth Sciences exams completed at the Dig Site. If you have, feel free to give us a hand. We'd appreciate it.
Tell me about the Dig Site find cleaning area.

The cleaning area, yes. Well, we have some really good archaeologists on site right now. They're cleaning up the finds that are shipped over from the Dig Site to the east of here. If you have the right qualifications, you can help
them clean the finds.
What qualifications?
Level 3 Earth Science exams. You can take them over at the Exam Centre on the Dig Site.

b: If you have not completed The Dig Site:

b.x: Oh, I don't have those.
I'm sure you can get them easily enough. Just pop over to the Exam Centre on the Dig Site and speak to one of the examiners there.

b: If you have completed The Dig Site:

b.x: Oh, I already have those!
That's excellent. If you feel like helping us out, pop downstairs and clean some finds for us.

o.x: Tell me about the Timeline exhibit.

Ahh, my speciality. Being a historian, matters of the past are my passion. Collated on this floor and the one above are just part of my life's work. I am still working on updating and finding out more everyday, so if you find any
information on your travels that may be useful, please do let me know.
You can follow the timeline of the history of Gielinor from the creation of the world to the present day, simply by walking around this display. A wondrous journey, I think you'll agree!
Wow, that's a lot of information. I'm sure in my travels and quests I'll pick up a few bits of information for you.

o: I have some information that might be of use in your displays.

o.x: I have some information that might be of use in your displays.
That's grand! We're always glad to have more facts. Now, tell me what you know...

b: If no relevant quests have been completed and not yet explained:

b.x: On second thoughts, you seem to have everything I know covered here!
No matter. I'm sure you'll find more. Look around the Museum, explore the city and maybe do some quests, and I'm sure you'll find out something worth telling.
Yes, I'll go do some quests or something...

b: If Shield of Arrav has been completed but not yet explained:
If the Shield of Arrav was completed in solo mode:

b.x: Well, I infiltrated two of the gangs here in Varrock...
We have gangs?
Erm, yes...anyway, I managed to recover both halves of the Shield of Arrav.
Halves?
Yes. The gangs had a bit of a tiff, you see. Anyway, I re-assembled the shield and presented it to King Roald to get my reward.

b: If the Shield of Arrav was completed with a partner:

b.x: Well, I infiltrated one of the gangs here in Varrock...
We have gangs?
Erm, yes...anyway, I managed to get half the shield back.
Only half?
Yes. The gangs had a bit of a tiff, you see. A friend helped me get the other half and I returned it here to get my reward.

Yes, yes, we were most pleased to have the shield returned - as was the King, I imagine. This is wonderful news, I shall make sure the display is updated at once! Display number 24, 4th Age, year 700-800. Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.
Oh, random bits of tat. Thank you very much.
You're welcome!
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
You receive an old lamp.
You receive an old lamp.

b: If Observatory Quest has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I helped to rebuild the Observatory near Ardougne. I had to fight to do it, and learn how to use the telescope too. I can draw you a diagram of the Observatory if it would help.
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
That would help immensely. Restored it, eh? And it works, you say? Excellent, perhaps we can get to some real stargazing now! Display number 17, 5th age, year 70.

b: If Merlin's Crystal has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I helped to free the wizard, Merlin, by using Excalibur...
Is that some kind of spell?
No, it's a sword. King Arthur's sword.
What kingdom does he rule then?
Ananka - one of the kingdoms of Teragard.
Where on Gielinor is that?

It's not! That's what I've trying to tell you. I found that King Arthur and his knights are really biding their time here in Gielinor until they are called back to their own world, when they are needed!
That's amazing! So he's really from another world! Well, this is interesting, I'll make sure a display is put up immediately. Well done, Player! Display number 9, 5th Age, year 132.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp laying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.
Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.
You're welcome!
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
You receive an old lamp.
You receive an old lamp.

b: If Demon Slayer has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: Well, I recently defeated Delrith, a demon! I did it by using a sword called Silverlight, which is apparently the only sword that could do it. I can give you a description if you want?
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
Delrith! Incredible! I am grateful to you for letting me know. Please tell me more about Silverlight and I'll get a display erected. Display number 25, 5th Age, year 20.

b: If The Grand Tree has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I helped to save the gnomes' Grand Tree!
Oh? You mean those little green fellows with their gliders?
Yes, I uncovered this nasty character called Glough and ended up being ambushed by a black demon...
A black demon! How did you survive!?
Oh, I was fine. After the demon it was downhill all the way, and King Narnode allowed me to use the mine under the Tree, and free passage on gnome gliders.
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
You mean that those flimsy things can fly with more than a gnome in? That is unexpected. I shall update the display immediately. Display number 10, upstairs in the middle of the room!

b: If Making History has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I found out more about King Lathas's ancestors.
Oh? I'd be interested to hear this, we have a painting of him upstairs.
Indeed, it turns out that there was a big battle in the year 98 of the 5th Age. One of his ancestors became king because he survived it...
Ahh, is this relating to that small museum near Ardougne?
Yes!
Ahh yes, we've been meaning to make a display on that for some time. They sent us some information, too; I'm glad you reminded me, I'll get that done now. Display number 46, 5th Age, year 98.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around...and since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.
Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.
You're welcome!
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
You receive an old lamp.
You receive an old lamp.

b: If Priest in Peril has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: Some disturbing and heroic news from Morytania concerning the River Salve and the seven priests.
Oh?
Yes, it seems that these seven priests were also warriors and drove back the nasty things coming out of Morytania. Then Saradomin blessed the Salve to stop them getting back.
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!

Quite worrying that it's just a bit of water keeping them there, but Saradomin will protect us, I've no doubt. Thank you for the information, I'll get a display put up. Display number 23, 4th Age, year 1100-1200.

b: If In Aid of the Myreque has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: Some disturbing and heroic news from Morytania, concerning the River Salve and the Temple Knights.
Ahh, the Temple Knights...little is known of them.
Yes, it seems that these seven knights drove back the nasty things coming out of Morytania, and Saradomin blessed the Salve to stop them getting back.
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!

Quite worrying that it's just a bit of water keeping them there, but Saradomin will protect us I've no doubt. Thank you for the information, I'll get a display put up. Display number 23, 4th Age, year 1100-1200.

b: If Glorious Memories has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I uncovered the secrets of a glorious Fremennik adventure!
That doesn't sound very historical. What were they doing?
There was a prophecy inscribed on five stone tablets. The adventurers were searching for the last one to complete the set.
That sounds much more relevant: we like prophecy. What do the tablets say? Where are they now?
Only the last tablet has survived, but I have it here.
That's excellent! Hmm, this inscription doesn't make much sense: who's [Fremennik name]?
Well, actually, that's-
No matter. I'll sort the display immediately. It will be in display number 48, on the top floor.

b: If Meeting History has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I discovered about the origin of humankind!
Are you sure?
Yes, we came from another place, through a portal! Guthix was there to meet us and he was also the one to create rune stones for us to use.
That's incredible. I shall make a display for that straight away. Display number 13, the second display of the 1st Age.

b: If A Tail of Two Cats has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: You know Bob the Cat?
The little black cat that wanders around sometimes? Sure, most people know him.
The little black cat that used to wander around sometimes? Sure, I remember him.
I found out a lot about his background...turns out he was once human and helped to defeat a dragonkin once!
Dragonkin? Tell me more!
Well, you see, it started when Bob went missing...and involved a big sphinx in Sophanem, the City of the Dead, and me taking care of Unferth...
This is starting to sound familiar...
It must...you know Reldo, the Varrock librarian - he knows all about Robert the Strong.
You mean that was Bob? Wow... I will get a display erected immediately about the history of this brave warrior. Display number 20, 4th Age, year 1-100.

b: If Temple of Ikov has been completed but not yet explained:
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl:

b.x: Well, I was asked to retrieve the Staff of Armadyl, from the Temple of Ikov, by Lucien, but instead, I helped the guardians of the staff and banished Lucien from this plane of existence, so that he could never again return. I saw the staff and can describe it to you if you want?

b: If the player sided with Lucien:

b.x: Well, I was asked to retrieve the Staff of Armadyl, from the Temple of Ikov, by Lucien. When I returned it he grew in power unimaginably. I held the staff and can describe it to you if you want?
Yes! Please do!
You describe the staff in detail while the historian takes notes.
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
That's excellent, I'll get a display put up straight away! Display number 28, end of the 2nd Age.

b: If Defender of Varrock has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: Well, we got rid of the marauding zombies.
That's handy: zombies tend to leave horrible muddy footprints around the place.
Erm, yes. Anyway, did you get the shield back?
Yes, Dimintheis returned it to us. I have two questions. What actually happened today, and is it safe to put the shield back on display?

Well, Zemouregal the mahjarrat sent his zombie army against Varrock; however, we figured out how to stop him. I found out that the descendant of the founder of Varrock could use the shield to stop the zombie army. It turns out that the leader of the tribe that founded Varrock was of the Fitzharmon bloodline. Dimintheis is a member of that bloodline, so he defeated the zombies.
My, my, that is all very interesting. I shall make sure the display is updated at once! Display number 24, 4th Age, year 700-800.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around. Since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.
Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.
You're welcome!
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
You receive an old lamp.
You receive an old lamp.

b: If Hazeel Cult has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I discovered the truth behind the Carnillean family fortune!
Oh? Is that the family over near Ardougne?
Yes. I got a bit involved in family business...
And?
I found a secret cult in Ardougne and found that the Carnillean family started building the city of Ardougne from a house they'd captured from a Zamorakian lord.
The historian pulls out his writing implements and listens while you explain the whole story....
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
How exciting, I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 7, 5th Age, year 7.

b: If What Lies Below has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: I discovered a tunnel and a cult of chaos mages here in Varrock!
Oh! Whatever can we do!
Calm down, I have arrested the ringleader.
Oh, thank Saradomin for that. So, tell me the story!
Well, I met Rat and he asked me to fill his folder, and I got mixed up with Surok...
A rat asked you to fill a folder?
No, no, no - Rat Burgiss. But anyways, it turns out that this cult had been trying to get to the King, but I stopped them.

b: If you have the Dagon'hai history book in your inventory:

b.x: The historian is scribbling furiously on his pad, and finally turns to you.
Actually, to save you some writing, I have this book here that has lots of information. You can have it if you want...
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
Why, thank you... Yes, this is a bit of a revelation! I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 3, 5th Age, year 70.

b: If you don't have the Dagon'hai history book in your inventory:

b.x: The historian looks a little overwhelmed, but also skeptical.
I don't suppose you have any evidence of this cult?
Not with me, but there is a book I can get you from the library.
That sounds good - bring me that and we'll create a display.

b: If Rune Mysteries has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: The mages let me in on the secret to runecrafting!
Ah. That. Tell me more.
Hmm I can't tell you much, but I do know that rune essence can be mined from a secret place, then, using the altars and talismans, I can change it into runes.
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
Sounds like magic to me! I'll get a display put up immediately. Display number 21, the first display of the 5th Age.

b: If The Curse of Zaros has been completed but not yet explained:

b.x: Well, I found out more about the Staff of Armadyl from a ghost. It seems that Zamorak was a mortal when he got hold of the staff, and he used it to, well...spear Zaros, and somehow ended up becoming a god. It was a bit confusing.
Now that is what you call a story. Tell me more so that I can put it up on the display.
You recount the tale of the battle between Zaros and Zamorak as you heard it from the ghostly swordsman.
This is wonderful, I shall have a display made immediately to go with the staff model. Display number 28, end of the 2nd Age.
Oh, and before I forget, we found this old lamp lying around. Since you've done such a sterling job, we'd like you to have it.
Oh, random bits of tat, thank you very much.
You're welcome!
You have earned Kudos with the Museum!
You receive an old lamp.
You receive an old lamp.

o.x: No thanks.

nodes.x: Hey! You leave that plinth alone. It's for the statue of Saradomin we're going to build.
Hello there. Welcome to Varrock Museum! Feel free to look around.

nodes.title: Choose an option:
o: Yes, how can I help out?

o.x: Yes, how can I help out?

b: When you don't have the equipment:

b.x: Well, you'll need to get your equipment first - it's all there on the tool rack. Use what you learned from your Earth Sciences exams. You'll need to be wearing your leather gloves and boots as well as have access to your trowel, rock pick and specimen brush.

b: When you're wearing leather boots and gloves and have the trowel, rock pick and specimen brush in your inventory:

b.x: I see you have your equipment -well done.

To really give us a hand, you could clean some finds for us. They're mostly done - just some fine work to finish off. Take a find from the pile that the workmen are bringing in, then there are spare tables over there to clean them on. If you find anything interesting, let us know and we'll see if it's good enough to go on display.

o: I have a question about the Statue of Dahmaroc.

o.x: I have a question about the Statue of Dahmaroc.

o.title: Select An Option
o: Tell me again where the statue comes from.

o.x: Tell me again where the statue comes from.

Well, we've only been able to piece bits together here and there, but it appears that Dahmaroc was a mage of great power who was caught up in an almighty battle back in the Second Age. It seems this battle was over who should have the lion's share of the runes that the sentient races had found around RuneScape.
Runes? As in the ones I use for magic now? Surely they're unlimited.
Now they are, yes, but back then there was a limited supply. At least, that's what the scraps of information we've found indicate.
Interesting. So what happened to Dahmaroc?
As far as we can gather, he lost, was turned to stone and then cursed. It's said he was doomed to spend eternity with the thing he loved most...
That doesn't sound so bad. Did he have a wife?
Well, we're not sure about that. We do know that he loved to gain knowledge and skill in new disciplines. No taste for fighting, though. Indeed, it was combat that proved to be his downfall.

o: Twin? How do I get its twin?

o.x: Twin? How do I get its twin?
Well, I'm not sure, but I suspect the same way you got the first one.
Why do I even need a twin?
Because, rather intriguingly, they interlock in pairs to make up the whole statue without any kind of adhesive being required.

o: How do I add it to the statue?

o.x: How do I add it to the statue?

If you have strange rocks you've found from training, simply use the pairs of parts on the plinth over there. If you mean one of the replicas we made for you, use the pairs of replica parts on the plinth in your house.

o: I'll have to keep a list of pieces.

o.x: I'll have to keep a list of pieces.
Yes, that would be wise. Here's some paper to use.
The archaeologist hands you a piece of paper which you quickly scribble on.
No, just here to watch.

What's a gnome doing here?
I'm an investigator. I'm watching the implings.
Why would you want to do that?
My client has asked me to find out where certain missing items have been going.
Who is this client?
I'm not at liberty to discuss that. Investigator-client confidentiality don't you know.
What do you want to ask?
Hello, my name is Player. Who are you?
Oh hello Player. I'm Aeryka. Aery for short.
Airy Fairy?
That's right. What can I do for you?
What's that crop circle thing doing here?
Crop circle? Oh, you mean the Puromantic portal?
The pyromanic what?
The Puromantic portal. At least that's what we call them. It's the way the implings travel from Puro-Puro to other planes.
Puro-Puro?
The impling home. We call it Puro-Puro. The implings just call it home, I think.
Are they here? Are they there? Are they elsewhere?
Are what where?
This gate's sisters...
I didn't know gates had relations.
Oh yes. This one here: she is calm and boring. She stays here all the time. She doesn't like to move, but her sisters are fidgety and refuse to stay in the same place for more than half an hour.
So, where are the, errr, fidgety sisters at the moment?
Oh well. I don't know what you humans call these places. Let me show you.
Hi assistant.
Wait a minute.
What's your real name?
My real name?
I only know you as the professor's assistant. What's your actual name?
Patrick.
Hi, Patrick, I'm Player.
Well, hello again, and thanks for helping out the professor.
Oh, and, believe it or not, his name is Mambo-duna-roona, but don't tell him I told you.
You made that up!
No, honest! Anyways, you've made my life much easier. Have a drink on me!
The assistant gives you some wine.
Scorpvino
Thanks very much.
No problem. Scorpius would be proud.
Sorry?
You may want to check out the book on the table, and perhaps look around for a grave...
Hello.
Shush! I'm concentrating.
Oh, sorry.
Hi there.
Hey, ids me matesh!
Sorry, have we met?
Yeah! you wazsh wiv me in dat pub overy by hill!
I have no idea what you're going on about.
Glad yeeash remembers.
Where did you get that lens?
From that strange metal thing up on the hill.
You should give that back!
Even if it's cracked?
Ah, well, I suppose it's of no use. But, still.
The little goblin appears to be fast asleep, and yet still fishing...
I think I'd rather not wake him.
Pirates have launched a raid on Port Sarim's jail! The prison guards are calling for support!
Pirates have launched a raid on Port Sarim's jail! The prison guards are calling for support!
Pirates have launched a raid on Port Sarim's jail! The prison guards are calling for support!
Pirates have launched a raid on Port Sarim's jail! The prison guards are calling for support!
Pirates have launched a raid on Port Sarim's jail! The prison guards are calling for support!
Hi, how can I help you?

o.x: What's going on here?

This is where we launch our landers to combat the invasion of the nearby islands. You'll see three landers - one for novice, intermediate and veteran adventurers. Each has a different difficulty, but they therefore offer varying rewards.
And this lander is...?
The intermediate.
So how do they work?

Simple. We send a lander out every three minutes, however we need at least five volunteers or it's a suicide mission. The lander can only hold a maximum of twenty five people though, so we do send them out early if they get full. If you'd be willing to help us then just wait in the lander and we'll launch it as soon as it's ready. However you will need a combat level of 70 to use this lander.

nodes.x: Hi, how can I help you?

o.x: What's going on here?

This is where we launch our landers to combat the invasion of the nearby islands. You'll see three landers - one for novice, intermediate and veteran adventurers. Each has a different difficulty, but they therefore offer varying rewards.
And this lander is...?
The veteran.
So how do they work?

Simple. We send a lander out every three minutes, however we need at least five volunteers or it's a suicide mission. The lander can only hold a maximum of twenty five people though, so we do send them out early if they get full. If you'd be willing to help us then just wait in the lander and we'll launch it as soon as it's ready. However you will need a combat level of 100 to use this lander.

nodes.x: Greetings to the court of King Arthur! I am proud to have you as a member of the Round Table.
Thank you.
Good day to you!

o.x: Good morrow sirrah/madam!

b.x: Morning. Know where an adventurer has to go to find a quest around here?
An adventurer eh? There is no service finer than serving the bountiful King Arthur, and I happen to know there's an important quest to fulfill.
Sir Knight! Many thanks for your assistance in restoring Merlin to his former freedom!
Hey, no problem.
We owe you a great debt for freeing us from that dungeon.
Awww, shucks. It was nothing.

b: If the player has completed the hard tasks in the Seers' Village set and the rewards not claimed:

b.x: Greetings, Sir Kay. I have completed all of the hard tasks in the Seer's Village set. May I have a reward?

b: If the player does not have the Seer's headband in backpack

b.x: I would love to, but you will need to bring me your seer's headband after you have received the rewards for the Easy and Medium tasks.
Okay, well, I'd better get busy then.
That's the spirit, young man.

b: If the player has the Seer's headband in backpack

b.x: Well done, young sir. You must be a mighty adventurer indeed to have completed the Hard Tasks.
You hand Sir Kay your headband and he concentrates for a moment. Some mysterious knightly energy passes through his hands and he gives the headband back to you, along with an old lamp.

While wearing it, 'Flax' will give you 120 flax per day, it will make you faster at spinning, you'll be able to see better in the dark and both your Prayer and defence against magic attacks will be boosted.
Stankers will allow 308 pieces of coal in his coal truck, and you'll get bonuses when cutting maple and normal trees.

I'm not finished! Your Camelot Teleport spell can be switched to Seers' Village and Thormac will lower his prices somewhat. Phew! Oh, and how could I forget - you'll get a bonus when you use the altar in the chapel here, but you don't need to wear the headband for that.
Thank you, Sir Kay. I'll try not to harm anyone with my spinning.
You are most welcome. You may also find that the Lady of the Lake is prepared to reward you for your services if you wear the headband in her presence.

b: If the player has completed the elite tasks in the Seers' Village set and the rewards not claimed:

b.x: Greetings, Sir Kay. I have completed all of the Elite Tasks in the Seer's Village set. May I have a reward?
Well done, young sir. You must be an awesome adventurer indeed to have completed the Elite Tasks.
You hand Sir Kay your headband and he concentrates for a moment. Some mysterious knightly energy passes through his hands and he gives the headband back to you, along with a few old lamps.
'Flax' will give you 200 flax per day, Stankers will ship 200 of your mined coal back to the bank, and you may find your skills with a crossbow and those fantastic enchanted bolts is improved.
Ah, and you may find Excalibur is further enhanced. Thank you for your work around the area.
Thank you, Sir Kay.
You are most welcome.

I've lost it.
Luckily, I have a spare headband that you can have.
Sir Kay hands you a seer's headband.

I've lost it.
Luckily, I have a spare headband that you can have.
Sir Kay hands you a seer's headband.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Seers' Village set, you are presented with a headband.
You will receive a better headband with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Seers' Village set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Seers' Village set rewards, speak to any seer in the village, Stankers out west by the coal trucks, or myself.

o: Could I buy a spare of the reward?

o.x: Seer's headband 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
You're handed another Seer's headband 1.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
You're handed another Seer's headband 2.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
You're handed another Seer's headband 3.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
You're handed another Seer's headband 4.
No thanks.

o.title: What would you like to say?

We will look after your items and money for you. Leave your valuables with us if you want to keep them safe.

o: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?

o.x: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?
Yes we did, but people kept on coming into our branches outside of Varrock and telling us that our signs were wrong. They acted as if we didn't know what town we were in or something.

nodes.x: So, I think I've found an entrance to Arposandra. I found this hatch and I saw what looked like talking terrorbird guards in there, but they ran away and I can't open the door to get in.
Talking terrorbirds? There must be some strange magic being practised in there. Though, that doesn't really prove that it is Arposandra.
Well no, but who else, other than gnomes, would go to the effort of making terrorbirds talk?

I agree, but I think you'll need more than that to persuade any gnomes that we've found the legendary lost city of Arposandra. So far, we've only found some rather dangerous sewers, some rather warped creatures and a
couple of talking terrorbirds. Everyone will think that we're insane.
I'm used to that, but we do need to find a way in.

nodes.x: Well met, fellow adventurer! How can I help you?

b: If the player has items they can collect from the Grand Exchange:

b.x: Before we go any further, I should inform you that you have items ready for collection from the Grand Exchange.

nodes.title: What would you like to say?

o.x: Who are you?
How frightfully rude of me, my dear [chap/lady]. My name is Eniola and I work for that most excellent enterprise, the Bank of Gielinor.

o.title: Select an Option
o: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?

o.x: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?
My presence here is the start of a new enterprise of travelling banks.
I, and others like me, will provide you with the convenience of having banking facilities where they will be of optimum use to you.
So...what are you doing here?

The Z.M.I., that is, the Zamorakian Magical Institute, requested my services upon discovery of this altar. We at the Bank of Gielinor are a neutral party and are willing to offer our services regardless of affiliation.
So that is why I am here.
Can I access my bank account by speaking to you?
Of course, dear [sir/lady].
However, I must inform you that because the Z.M.I. are paying for my services, they require anyone not part of the Institute to pay an access fee to open their bank account.

But, as our goal as travelling bankers is to make our customers' lives more convenient, we have accomodated to your needs. We know you will be busy creating runes and do not wish to carry money with you. The charge to open your account is the small amount of twenty of one type of rune. The type of rune is up to you.
Would you like to pay the price of twenty runes to open your bank account?

o: I'd like to access my bank account, please.
I'd like to check my PIN settings.

o.x: Bank PIN

o: I'd like to access my bank account, please.

o.title: It costs twenty runes of one type. Do you wish to continue?

o: I'd like to check my PIN settings.

o.x: Bank PIN

o: I'd like to see my Collection box.

nodes.x: What's that ladder next to the altar for?
An...archaeological dig. Yeah, a dig.
Why?
Next to a Chaos Altar? That's a bit odd. Can I go down and have a look?
Well...I suppose. See, we found this ancient altar, but it was pretty broken so the Z.M.I. sent some of its researchers to try and repair it.
How'd that work out for them?
Pretty well - only one died. Still, They got it working...sort of. This ancient technology can be tricky.
What do you mean, 'sort of'? Altars either work or don't work.
This one works, just not as you'd expect. You put pure essence in, but get random runes back. Some of them we don't even know how to craft!
Sounds like a pretty good deal. Can I give it a go?

I don't think so. The mages don't like outsiders going in; they'll probably attack you. They only patrol the short path, though, so if you used the long path, through a tunnel near the entrance, you'd probably be safe.
Thanks.
Greetings.

o.x: I'm glad to see you taking this so well. Most of the recently deceased are more upset.
Yes, I'm afraid that you are.
Calm down, calm down. You're just dead.

nodes.x: Fortunately for you, it is not yet your time.

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Great! How do I get back?

o.x: It is not your time. Destiny awaits you. I will not claim you. Yet.
Right... thanks.

nodes.x: You can go back now. When you leave here, you'll return to the town.
When you die you keep some of your items, but you lose others.
I lose my stuff?
Your valuable gear will be dropped wherever it is you died. However, you can choose three of those items to keep.
You can see which items will drop and which will be kept in the deathkeep interface in your Worn Inventory.
When you return to the world of living, you have a short time limit to return to the site of your death and reclaim your dropped gear.
Whenever you die with items that could drop, you'll see an interface allowing you to choose which ones to keep.
You can selectively take your items one at a time, take them all with the 'take all' button, or re-equip your gear and take the rest of your items with the 'Equip all' button.
Take the portal behind you and return to the world of the living.

nodes.x: Hello there! Welcome to my humble abode. How can I help you?

nodes.title: Choose an option:
o: I have a question about Summoning...

o.title: Choose an option:
o: So, what's Summoning all about then?

o.x: In general? Or did you have a specific topic in mind?
Well, you already know about Summoning in general; otherwise, we would not be having this conversation!
Effectively, the skill can be broken into three main parts: summoned familiars, charged items and pets.
Summoned familiars are spiritual animals that can be called to you from the spirit plane, to serve you for a period of time.
These animals can also perform a special move, which is specific to the species. For example, a spirit wolf can perform the Howl special move if you are holding the correct Howl scroll.
Charged items contain summoning power, but in a stable form.
They can be used to physically store any scrolls you have.
Those are the main effects of Summoning.
Are you still following me?
Yes, I think so.
I can supply you with pouches and spirit shards, but you will have to bring your own charms and secondary ingredients.
Many creatures drop charms when you kill them in combat. There are many different charms in the world: gold, blue, green, crimson and even some specialist ones like obsidian.
I'll be sure to keep my eyes open for them.
The best way to raise your Summoning level is to infuse pouches.
You will still learn a little from summoning a familiar, as well as using a scroll and transforming the summoning pouches into scrolls.
But nothing is more potent than infusing a spirit into a Summoning pouch in the first place.
Do you understand?
Sure!
Good!
Where was I?
Ah, yes, the last part of Summoning: the pets. The more you practice the skill, the more you will comprehend the natural world around you.

This is reflected in your increased ability to raise animals as pets. It takes a skilled summoner to be able to raise some of Gielinor's more exotic animals, such as the lizards of Karamja, or even dragons!
Now that I've given you this overview, do you want to know about anything specific?
Summoned familiars are at the very core of Summoning. Each familiar is different, and the more powerful the summoner, the more powerful the familiar they can summon.
The animals themselves are not real, in the sense that you or I are real; they are spirits drawn from the spirit plane.
As a result, they have powers that the animals they resemble do not.
They cannot remain in this world indefinitely; they require a constant supply of energy to maintain their link to the spirit plane.
This energy is drained from your Summoning skill points.
Your level of the Summoning skill is not drained, and you can refresh your points back up to your maximum level at an obelisk whenever you wish.
So, my Summoning skill points are like food to them?
Yes, that is an appropriate analogy.
The more powerful the familiar, the more it must 'feed' and the more 'food' it will need to be satisfied.
As a result, only the most powerful summoners are able to maintain a link from a familiar to the spirit plane, since they are able to provide more 'food' with each Summoning level they gain.
I'm starting to get a little hungry now.
As you gain mastery of the skill you will be able to have familiars out for the full time they exist. And still have some points over to re-summon them afterwards, if you wish.
This is because you are able to feed them the energy they need and have leftovers to spare!
Great!
So, what can these familiars do?
Why not ask me to count every blade of grass on a lawn?
The familiars each have unique abilities and even the most experienced summoner will not know them all.
Well, can you give me some hints?
Well, some familiars are able to fight with you in combat. They will keep an eye out to see if you are fighting and will intervene, if they can.
Other familiars will not fight, for various reasons, but they may provide bonuses in other tasks. Some will even carry your items for you, if you need them to.
Amazing!
Would you like to know anything else about Summoning?
Well, if a Summoning pouch is split apart at an obelisk, then the energy it contained will reconstitute itself - transform - into a scroll.
This scroll can then be used to make your familiar perform its special move.
For example, spirit wolves are able to Howl, scaring away an opponent for a short period of time.
Or longer, in the case of that giant wolpertinger.
Indeed!
Well, each familiar has its own special move, and you can only use scrolls on the familiar that it applies to.
For example, a spirit wolf will only look at you oddly if you wish it to perform a dreadfowl special move.
So, what sort of special moves are there?
The special moves are as varied as the familiars themselves.
A good rule of thumb is that if a familiar helps you in combat, then its special move is likely to damage attackers when you use a scroll.
On the other hand, if a familiar is more peaceful by nature, then its special move might heal or provide means to train your other skills - that sort of thing.
Are the familiar's special moves similar to its normal abilities?
In general, no. But some familiars' special moves can be a more powerful version of their normal ability.
Take the spirit wolf, for example. Its special move and its normal ability are essentially the same.
However, the special move can be used on any nearby opponent, while the normal ability only works on those opponents you are currently fighting.
If your familiar is fighting with you, it will use its normal ability whenever it can.
It won't however, use its special move unless you have expressly asked it to, by activating a scroll.
I see. Thanks for the information.
Would you like to know anything else about Summoning?
Charged items are very simple to create, if you have the correct Crafting level.
If not, then you can simply buy a set of antlers or a lizard skull from me. You can take an item that can be charged, usually a headdress, and attach scrolls to them.
The scrolls are then stored in the headdress. Aggressive combat scrolls, however, are the only ones that can be used in this way.
Why is that?
Well, a scroll in a charged item will only be activated when it is hit with enough power.

Since this can only happen from the impact of combat, it makes sense that only combat-based scrolls can be stored here. The activated scroll will then be sensed by your familiar, and it will defend you.
What sort of impact are we talking about here?
Oh, nothing too serious: stabbings, explosions, arrows to the torso - that sort of thing.
What?
Oh, come now; a strapping lad like you will barely feel it. Your opponent, however, will certainly feel the power of your retaliation!
Anyway, one impact is not enough; it will take a series of strikes to activate the power in the charged item.
So, will this allow familiars to perform the special moves of other familiars? Or will it work if I have no familiar out?
No. As with the normal method of instigating a special move, the correct scroll is required for the correct familiar.
Even if some dreadfowl scroll power was hanging in the air, a spirit wolf would not be able to do anything with it.
What happens when the item runs out of charge? Do they disintegrate or something?
Only if you've made them shoddily!
The items should be useful for a long time. When you run out of charges, you simply need to attach more scrolls.
That's a relief.
Would you like to know anything else about Summoning?
Well, these are not really an element of the skill, as such, but more like a side-effect of training.
Essentially, the higher the Summoning level an adventurer has, the more they become in tune with nature.
As a result, they can approach animals that would otherwise run away from them.
This means that you will be able to befriend and raise various animals from around the world.
So, what will I need to do to raise these pets?
Oh, most of them will be quite content to follow you around. You just have to feed them and make sure they are generally healthy.
It is the goal of every summoner to be able to raise a dragon, yet few have been able to perform this feat.
Wow! Imagine riding around on a dragon - even fighting with it!
That's not the right attitude at all!
What?
When you raise a pet it becomes your responsibility - your friend.
You can't ride into battle on your friend, or make them fight for you. These are not spiritual familiars: if they die, they die!
I didn't realise.
Well, now you know.
Pets do not fight for you, cast spells or have strange abilities, and you may certainly not ride around on them. They are animals you raise from birth to follow you wherever you go.
Remember that and take good care of them.
I will!
Would you like to know anything else about Summoning?

The Orb Proj...I beg your pardon, The Great Orb Project? It's truly fascinating. Wizards Acantha and Vief have found that energy leaks out of some of the Runecrafting altars. They are recruiting teams of experienced runecrafters such as yourself, to force the energy back in.
Join one of the teams by speaking to Wizard Acantha of Wizard Vief. When the wizards have enough helpers, I will open a portal to the Air Altar.
The energy appears in the form of floating orbs. These can be moved by means of wands that attract or repel them. Acantha or Vief will give you one of each wand.
Your goal is to move the correct colour orb to the altar stone, while keeping the other orbs away. Wizard Acantha favours the green orbs, while Wizard Vief favours the yellow ones.
You will also have a third wand, which allows you to create magical barriers to block the opposing team's orbs.
After two minutes, the team that absorbed the most orbs wins that altar. I then open the portal to the next altar in the sequence. After you have visited all eight altars, you will be returned here.

o.title: Select an option

o.x: What's in it for me?
A fair question. We have agreed on a token scheme that allows you to choose from several rewards. When you return from the last altar, your senior wizard will give you a number of tokens.

You will get 50 tokens per altar that your team captured, provided that you contributed to the capture in some way. You will get an extra 100 tokens if your team captured more altars overall, or 50 extra if it is a draw.
You can exchange the tokens for rewards by speaking to me.
You may also find rune essence appearing in your inventory at the end of each round. This is a side-product of the absorption process and you are free to use it as you wish.

I also offer teleport tablets to the various altars.

What theories has he come up with?

His boldest theory is that the altars are not endless pools of energy, as we though they were. His research notes seem to be in order, but I find myself seriously questioning the validity of that statement.
Why?
Many of the current theories on the altars are based on the long-held assumption that the altars are everlasting.
If that assumption is proven to be untrue, it sets our work back by quite a margin.
The trouble is, the implications of him being correct are so great we cannot ignore his theories until we have either proven or disproven them.
What implications are these?
The human ability to perform magic is something that helps protect us from those that wish us harm. Without runes, we would not be able to perform magic, and that would be a rather dire situation.
Is there nothing we can do?
Wizard Finix has come up with a proposed solution. He has come up with a method of siphoning runic energy from sources other than the altars.
Wizard Finix believes that the world around us is made up of runic energy, but his studies came to a halt when he failed to siphon runic energy from Gielinor.
Do we know why it didn't work?

Nobody knows for sure. Some believe that his theory is incorrect. Other believe that it could be correct, but that it would take a runecrafter of immense talent to siphon runic energy from Gielinor itself.
Whoever is right, I have found myself with no choice but to open the Runespan up for investigation into this siphoning method.
The Runespan?
The Runespan is a plane in which the runecrafting Guild is situated. It is a chaotic plane with a runic energy flying around, unbound to anything, which makes it perfect for siphoning training.
Hopefully, if we can train up enough runecrafters, one day we may be able to siphon energy from Gielinor.

o.title: What would you like to ask about?

o.x: (If gauntlets haven't been lost:)
(If gauntlets have been lost:)

I wanted to ask if there were any more of those mystical gauntlets you could part with? I really appreciate the skill and effort your sons put into their craft and would like to honour this by having one pair of each type of gauntlets.

I am flattered on behalf of my sons, but although there are more gauntlets that have been kept in the family, the others are not mine to part with. They belong to each of my sons to use as they see fit, and they alone can decide what they do with theirs.
I suppose I could pay them a visit. Thank you.
(Before completing Defender of Varrock:)
(After completing Defender of Varrock:)

nodes.x: If you've worked hard towards your cause, perhaps you'd be interested in some rewards?
What would you like to say?
Take this Slayer collection log. It will allow you to keep track of all your rare drops from Slayer monsters.
'Ello, and what are you after then?
Zamorak, aid me!
Zamorak, aid me!
Hello. What are you doing here?
Err, nothing much, I'm just here on business. Heard Draynor's a nice place to visit.
I just do the washing around here.
'Ello, and what are you after then?
Hi Chuck. How's it going?
Ah, Player. It's good to see you again.

b.x: Before you speak, I wanted to mention that a fellow agent of mine is stationed on the iceberg.
He is there to help you spy on penguins, but he is also in charge of an intelligence gathering unit that is interrogating a recent arrival of KGP agents.
He may need your help hunting penguins.
Okay, I'll keep an eye out for him the next time I'm on the iceberg.

nodes.title: Choose an option:

o.x: Have you heard anything from Gordon recently?
He sends in reports when he can, via magic carpet.
The penguins are trying to repair their T.A.R.D.I.S., but as you can imagine, it's almost impossible for them to get spare parts out there.
Gielinor is safe for the time being!

b: First time after unlocking Invention if the quest was completed before doing so:

b.x: Ah, I see you've finally become learned about Invention, here I've got something for
You receive 10k XP in Invention for your unknowing skills demonstrated in Back to the Freezer.

o.x: I thought Larry might hang around the zoo again. Where's he gone off to?
We believe he has learned the location of the penguins' secret base on Acheron. We've taken him to the PBJ HQ to debrief him.

b: If Player does not own Sheldon the Penguin:

b.x: What about his baby penguin? What will happen to Sheldon?
That abomination? I don't know. Larry wouldn't let us dispose of it. It seems perhaps his allegiance isn't as strong as it used to be.

b: If Player owns Sheldon the Penguin:

b.x: How is that abomination of a penguin Larry wouldn't let us dispose of? Has it shown any signs of treachery yet?
Sheldon? Oh not at all; he's an excellent companion actually.
Never fear. I will remain here to pick up the pieces after it eventually betrays you.

o.x: I wanted to talk to you about the penguin spies.

b: If Player does not own a spy device

b.x: You should take this device for spying on the penguins. It should come in handy as it has a number of useful functions that will help you on your mission. First, it will provide hints to all the penguin locations. It can't get an exact lock on, but it should give you the general area to begin your search. Once you're in the area, you can start a scan which will search your immediate vicinity and identify any penguins nearby. As you spot more penguins, I will be offer an upgrade to scan range and a new zap function which will freeze any penguins in place.

b: If Player has lost or destroyed their spy device

b.x: Hm... you appear to be missing your penguin spy device?
I only turned around for a second...
You're lucky Larry made plenty of them. From what I can tell they are mostly made out of tin foil anyway.

o.title: Select an option
o: I'm having trouble finding the penguins, can I have a hint?
{{Tact|(Only if the first option wasn't selected last:)}}
What do I need to do again?

o.x: What do I need to do again?
You humans do have a short attention span, don't you?
The penguins have dispatched spies all over the world. I need brave adventurers to find them and report their locations to me, as I cannot leave this cage.
Whenever you spot a penguin, spy on it. They're well trained and will change their positions every week, so keep your eyes peeled.
I'll give you a device that can track the penguin spies and offer you hints on their locations. Penguins are worth between 1 and 3 Penguin Points depending how difficult they are to find.
Report back here and I will reward you for your efforts.
Finally, you may see a polar bear on your travels. If you report his location to me I will reward you with an extra Penguin Point. He's one of ours, but I like to keep tabs on our spies, too.
Never mind.
Very well.

o: I've lost the clockwork book, could I have another?

b: If you don't own the clockwork book

b.x: I've lost the clockwork book, could I have another?
Fortunately, Larry put a spell on it which returned it to me when you lost it. Here it is.

b: If the player does not have the Ransom letter:

nodes.title: I want to speak to Larry about:

b.x: You need to be level 10 Hunter to start this quest.
You need to be level 30 Agility to start this quest.
I'm looking for an experienced adventurer and you're not it. Come back when you are more capable.
You need to be level 34 Construction to start this quest.
I'm looking for an experienced adventurer and you're not it. Come back when you are more capable.

o.x: What do you want?
Uh, I just wanted to as-
SHHHHHH! They're listening. Keep your voice down.
*whispers* Who's listening?
Never mind.
Are you the inquisitive sort? Are you willing to go on an expedition for me?
What would I need to do on this expedition?
The zoo has granted me permission to study penguins abroad. It's my, er...understanding that there are many penguins located around the world.
Why do you want to find penguins around the world?
I need to see if they're organis-, I mean, if they're migrating or something like that.
You think they're organised? They're just penguins!
Do not underestimate them! They're clever and tricky and LISTENING! I know they're up to something.
That's why I'm recruiting brave adventurers to find these penguins and tell me of their locations.
Well, I don't think they're organised, but I do travel all over the world. I could give you a hand finding them. What do I need to do?
Whenever you spot a penguin, spy on it. They're well trained and will change their positions every week, so keep your eyes peeled.
I'll give you a device that can track the penguin spies and offer you hints on their locations. Penguins are worth between 1 and 3 Penguin Points depending how difficult they are to find.
Report back here and I will reward you for your efforts.
Great, I'll get started right away.

b.x: I need to give you a device but you don't have any space. Come and talk to me once you have made space, or you can claim one from the shop.
Hold on, there. Take this device.
Larry hands you a penguin spy device.
You should take this device for spying on the penguins. It should come in handy as it has a number of useful functions that will help you on your mission.
First, it will provide hints to all the penguin locations. It can't get an exact lock on, but it should give you the general area to begin your search.
Once you're in the area, you can start a scan which will search your immediate vicinity and identify any penguins nearby.
As you spot more penguins, I will be offer an upgrade to the scan range and a new zap function which will freeze any penguins in place.

nodes.x: How sweet I roamed from fen to fen, And tasted all the Myre's pride, 'Till I the queen of love did ken, Who in the spirit beams did glide!
She shew'd me lilies in her hair, And blushing roses for her brow; She led me through her gardens fair, Where all her silver blooms do grow.
With sweet Myre dews my wings were wet, And Phoebus' kiss did slowly fade; She'd caught me in her silken net, And trap'd me as this silver shade.
She loves to sit and hear me sing, Then laughing, sports and plays with me; Then stretches out her silver wing, And mocks my loss of liberty.
The ghost does not seem to be aware of your presence, but you sense that this might be a good place to have a rest.
Who are you?
Can I ask you some questions about resting?
Can I ask you some questions about running?
That's all for now.
Hello, visitor. You should speak to Commander Veldaban if you need something.
Sorry, human. This is a private mining area.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Who owns this mining area?

b.x: It's jointly owned by the mining companies of the Consortium.
Dondakan bought it after he struck big with his cannon in the south mines. He's keeping it exclusive, though.

o: How much would it cost you for you to look the other way?

o.x: How much would it cost you for you to look the other way?
It would end up costing me my job. Move along now.
Goodbye.

nodes.x: Go downstairs and speak to Commander Veldaban. Your business is with him.
Good day to you! Welcome to my fishing shop. Welcome to my fishing shop. Would you like to buy some fishing equipment or sell some fish?

o: Can I see your fishing supplies?

o.x: Lumbridge Fishing Supplies

nodes.x: Player! Great to see you.

nodes.title: Choose an option:

o.x: I'm Gwir the scribe.
Have you been writing anything interesting recently?
I find all literature interesting, but lately I've been puzzling over recent elven history. I'm working to document it as clearly as I can, so that it's recorded for future generations.

o.title: What would you like to say?
o: Can I help you at all?

o.x: Actually, don't worry.

o: Can I help you at all?

o.x: Can I help you at all?

o: Can you remind me of events so far?

o.x: Bye.

nodes.x: Yes? What do you want? I'm very busy!

o.x: What is this place?
This is the sawmill training area, where we take the more qualified woodcutters on work experience.
Work experience?
Yeah. You work, you gain experience. You DO NOT gain planks, as I have to tell everyone.
Not even a few...
NO PLANKS!
Okay, okay.
Who are you?
The name's Jill. I'm the sawmill overseer.
Pleased to meet y-
I'm in charge of this place, so no fooling around!
What should I be doing?

Well, first grab a job from the board. There's short and long jobs: pick whichever you fancy. Then you stock up on wood from the piles and stack it in the hopper. The machine will do its magic and, before you know it, you'll have a stack of planks at the other end. Take these, with a saw, to the workbench to cut the planks you need. All the finished planks go straight into the cart, but you can take out any excess planks and use them for the next batch, if you like. Just let me know when you're ready to send an order.
Bye.
Nothing, thanks.

nodes.x: Hello!

Who are you?
I'm Phil.
And I'm Delphie!

nodes.x: Hannibus, can you help here?

(Hannibus's eyes glaze over and another voice comes from his mouth.)
Adamant dragon's voice: Where are they? They took them! My babies. My babies.
Hannibus, are you okay?
It's... difficult. She is in so much pain. She has no voice of her own, so I'm lending her mine.
Adamant dragons's voice: They took them from me! They took my babies. What is a mother without her children?
Greetings.

o.x: I'm glad to see you taking this so well. Most of the recently deceased are more upset.
Yes, I'm afraid that you are.
Calm down, calm down. You're just dead.

nodes.x: Fortunately for you, it is not yet your time.

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Great! How do I get back?

o.x: It is not your time. Destiny awaits you. I will not claim you. Yet.

nodes.x: You can go back now. When you leave here, you'll return to the town.
When you die you keep some of your items, but you lose others.
I lose my stuff?
Your valuable gear will be dropped wherever it is you died. However, you can choose three of those items to keep.
You can see which items will drop and which will be kept in the deathkeep interface in your Worn Inventory.
When you return to the world of living, you have a short time limit to return to the site of your death and reclaim your dropped gear.
Whenever you die with items that could drop, you'll see an interface allowing you to choose which ones to keep.
You can selectively take your items one at a time, take them all with the 'take all' button, or re-equip your gear and take the rest of your items with the 'Equip all' button.
Take the portal behind you and return to the world of the living.

b.x: I'm afraid you'll need to be a member to claim any rewards for the task set.

So you have. I have upgraded the aura for you.
Marmaros hands you an aura, 2,000 Dungeoneering tokens, and a lamp.
There you go, may it protect you as well as Thok's does his. Oh, and someone gave me this lamp, but it's of no use to me.
Thanks!

When you are wearing the aura in Daemonheim you will waste fewer arrows and automatically grind bones. It will also let you through the magical barrier over near the yew trees to the east. In addition to this, because you

completed the medium task set, you may now bind one potion and I've also had a word with the smuggler who'll help you out with some runes for each floor. Finally, you'll find your ring of kinship has got a bit more powerful with its secondary role.

b: If the player doesn't have rewards to claim:

b.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the Achievement System.

o.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o.title: Choose an option:
o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.

o.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Daemonheim set, you are presented with an aura.
This aura will become increasingly useful as you complete greater difficulties of task sets.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of its uses.
You may also see what rewards a set item provides by hovering over the Rewards icon for its Exploration Achievement set in the Achievements interface.

o: How do I claim these rewards?

o.x: How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all tasks within a particular difficulty set, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Daemonheim set's tasks are simple, some require certain skill levels, and others require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Daemonheim set rewards, speak to Drangund the Dungeoneering Tutor, Talsar, Thok or myself.

b.x: Before we carry on, let me give you this.
Oh, your hands are full? Come back when you've got space in your inventory.
He hands you a ring.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: What is this place?
This is a place of treasures, fierce battles and bitter defeats.
We fought our way into the dungeons beneath this place.
Those of us who made it out alive...
...called this place Daemonheim.
Daemonheim?
Yes. It resembles the Niflheim of our stories: The Halls of the Dead.
The creatures within, however, are very much alive...
...unlike my fallen brothers and sisters.
What can I do here?
Beneath these ruins you will find a multitude of dungeons, filled with strange creatures and resources.
Unfortunately, due to the taint that permeates this place, we cannot risk you taking items in or out of Daemonheim.

o.title: Select an Option
o: How will I survive without my kit?

o.x: How will I survive without my kit?
When we were within Daemonheim, we found a number of unknown resources. You can use your skills to fashion them into armour and weapons to keep your party alive.
Our contact within the dungeon can give you guidance on each of the items you find. He might even give you some gear to start you off.

o: Why can't I take my kit in?

o.x: Why can't I take my kit in?
Within Daemonheim there is a taint. The metal, wood, even the plantlife are not of this world. We cannot risk exposing the surface to them.
Equally, if we allowed you to take items inside, we could not allow you to return with them.
For this reason, our seers have erected a barrier. Nothing in, nothing out without express permission.
What does this ring do?
Raiding these forsaken dungeons can be a lot more rewarding if you're fighting alongside friends and allies. It should be more fun and you'll gain experience faster.
The ring shows others that you are interested in raiding a dungeon. It allows you to form, join and manage a raiding party.
We've also set up rooms with the specific purpose of finding a party for you.
Would you like me to show you? It's the fastest way into the dungeons of Daemonheim.
Yes, please.
It's this way.
No thanks, not right now.
Suit yourself.

o: (If the player has unlocked at least one dungeoneering journal) Show me the journals I've found.

nodes.x: What you want with Thok?

o.x: What is this place?
This is camp. This where warriors rest and prepare for onslaught.
Thok wait here to reward those who survive Daemonheim, who show might as great as Thok's.
Daemonheim?
It mean Demon Halls. Name not quite right, as there worse things than demons in Daemonheim. It less a hall and more a pit, too. Some say it has no end, but Thok know better.
What can I do here?

Up path is Daemonheim. It hold more treasure than Thok can put in his pockets, which is lucky for you, but it guarded by countless monsters, which is unlucky for you. First-timers should talk to tutor before going into castle.

In Daemonheim you make second gatestone and teleport to it. Also in Daemonehim then bury bones of dead enemies - you get prayer. Also, let you through magical barrier in Brimhaven Dungeon - Thok try head-butting
but now he share the secret.
Thanks! What else does it do?

For doing all tasks your ring of kinship made better! Also Thok persuade smuggler to take less monies for stuff. If you really think you as good as Thok, you try hard mode...but me not think your head hard enough for that.
