nodes.title: Choose an option:
o: What can you tell me about this place?

o.x: What can you tell me about this place?

b: If the player is on complexity 1:

b.x: This floor is less complex than most, and gives you a good introduction to Daemonheim.
Combat will be the only challenge you'll face, so I've given you a selection of melee, ranged and magical gear.

b.title: Select an Option

o.x: Thanks.
Well, it's not entirely selfless. For me, it's...a long term investment.
I don't need your help.
Haha! Well, take it or leave it; it's no skin off my back.

o: I was expecting more of a challenge.

o.x: I was expecting more of a challenge, perhaps something to test my other skills.
All in good time, Player. This floor may not be complex, but, as you get deeper, you'll need to use all your skills to survive.

b: If the player is on complexity 2:

b.x: On this floor, you'll be able to fish cave creatures and chop down the creeping trees that grow up the dungeon walls.
I'll also give you access to some stock from my shop.
With the resources available, you should be able to supplement your food supplies by lighting fires and cooking the fish you find.

b.title: Select an Option
o: How are there trees growing underground?

o.x: How are there trees growing underground?
From what I can tell, they're not native to this plane. Perhaps, like the fish, they were brought through the portals that are dotted about Daemonheim.

o: Where did the fish come from?

o.x: Where did the fish come from?
I think the past inhabitants of this dungeon brought them through a portal.
They're remarkably nutritious, even if they don't look appetising.

o: I was expecting more of a challenge.

o.x: I was expecting more of a challenge, perhaps something to test my other skills.
All in good time, Player. This floor may be simple, but, as you get deeper, you'll need to use all your skills to survive.

b: If the player is on complexity 3:

b.x: On this floor, you can mine rocks for ore and fashion your own weapons.
I've also expanded my shop stock to include fletching tools for making ranged weapons, and rune essence for crafting magical runes.

b.title: Select an Option
o: How do I make melee weapons?

o.x: How do I make melee weapons?
Take a pickaxe to the rocks in the dungeon, then smelt the resulting ores in the furnace over there.
Finally, grab a hammer and use the smelted bar on the nearby anvil. You can shape the metal into a number of weapons and tools.

o: How do I make ranged equipment?

o.x: How do I make ranged equipment?
Fletching bows and arrows is easy when you know how. Just grab a knife and use it on a log to make flightless arrow shafts or an unstrung bow.
You'll need to add bowstrings to your bows, or feathers and arrowheads to your arrows.
How do I craft runes?
Runecrafting is a powerful skill which is easy to practise within these dungeon walls.
Daemonheim sits on a site of extreme elemental and chaotic power. This can be focused and channelled through the altar in this room.
Simply buy some rune essence from my shop - I sell them in special pouches for convenience - and imbue them at the nearby altar. The resulting runes can be used to cast magical spells.

o: I was still expecting more of a challenge.

o.x: I was expecting more of a challenge, perhaps something to test my other skills.
All in good time, Player. This floor may be simple, but, as you get deeper, you'll need to use all your skills to survive.

b: If the player is on complexity 4:

b.x: This floor of Daemonheim is home to a species of creature called the bovimastyx. They are non-aggressive, but have thick hides that are perfect for crafting into ranged armour.
There are also a number of plants that farmers can harvest. These textiles can be woven into cloth for use in magic robes.
Finally, you have access to the full range of melee armour via smithing.

b.title: Select an Option
o: Tell me about bovimastyx and ranged armour.

o.x: Tell me more about bovimastyx and ranged armour.
Bovimastyx are large cratures that are easy to trap for those with experience in hunting.
You can attack them normally, but you'll be more likely to get hides if you can fletch a suitable trap and get them to step on it.

o: Tell me about textiles and mage robes.

o.x: Tell me more about textiles and mage robes.
Otherworldly plants have taken root here, and their stringy leaves and stems are perfect for spinning.
The result is cloth with remarkable magical properties. It's even mildly resistant to melee damage.
Just take a needle and thread to craft it into magic robes.

o: I was still expecting more of a challenge.

o.x: I was expecting more of a challenge, perhaps something to test my other skills.
All in good time, Player. This floor may not be complex, but, as you get deeper, you'll need to use all your skills to survive.

b: If the player is on complexity 5:

b.x: This dungeon floor gives you a taste of everything there is to offer.
You'll find herbs for potions, chests to unlock, seeds and spores for farming, and we're deep enough for the summoning of familiars to be possible.
You may also find puzzle rooms, keys and strange doors. Some may lead to rooms that are off the beaten path - optional, as it were.

b.title: Select an Option

o.x: Tell me about the herbs.
You can find herbs in a number of areas down here, and many have beneficial properties when mixed with the right reagents.

You'll need to fill a vial from my shop with water from the tap there. Pop your herb and a suitable secondary item into the vial to create a potion. If you can't find the secondary item you want, I'm also selling them in the
shop.
Tell me about these chests.
Locked chests are hard to come by, but the items within them are usually worth the effort.
If you've got a trained thief in your party, you can pick the locks and get the loot inside.

o: Tell me about farming with seeds and spores.

o.x: Tell me about farming with seeds and spores.
It's hard to grow much here in the dark, but the occupants in this place have found a way.
If you can find the relevant seeds, you can grow potatoes, mushrooms, and herbs in the various farming patches. These can be cooked and combined with fish to improve your food.
The soil in Daemonheim is extremely fertile: magically so. Simply pop the seed in the ground and it'll become full-grown in just a couple of minutes.
Tell me about summoning familiars in Daemonheim.
Summoning familiars requires a pouch and spirit shards, available from my shop. You'll also need a specific charm which can be retrieved from fallen enemies.
Depending on the familiar you're looking to summon, you'll need a summoning secondary item, like ore, wood, textiles, hides, broken bags or food.
Take these items to the summoning obelisk in this room. The finished pouch will enable you to summon a gorajo to help you out.
What's a gora-jo?
It's gora-ho, and they're helpful humanoid creatures from another plane. They seem eager to help when summoned and have their own reasons for disrupting activities in Daemonheim.

o: Tell me about puzzle rooms, keys and strange doors.

o.x: Tell me about puzzle rooms, keys and strange doors.
The founders of this place left rooms to challenge the mind, not just the sword-arm. Be careful in them: many hold penalties for failure.
You'll also find doors that are locked, protected or beyond reach. You'll need to find a key or use your skills to progress.
Don't feel that you need to explore every room. Some may be optional, while others may require skills that none of you have right now.

b: If the player is on complexity 6:

b.x: You know all I can teach you already, friend, having conquered many floors yourself.

o.x: Who are you?
A friend.
Okay, what are you doing here, friend?
I'm here to help out.
With what?
Well, let's say you find yourself in need of adventuring kit, and you've a heavy pile of rusty coins weighing you down. I can help you with both of those problems. Savvy?
Ah, so you're a trader.
Keep it down, you fool!
Yes, I'm a trader. But I'm not supposed to be trading here.
If you want my goods, you'll learn not to talk about me.
Right, got you.
Is there anything else you can do for me?
Well, there's the job I'm supposed to be doing down here.
Which is?
Say you chance upon an object you know little about. Show it to me, and I'll tell you what it's used for.
That's good to know.
I can also offer hints about the behaviour of powerful opponents you might meet in the area. I've spent a long time down here, observing them.
I'll be sure to come back if I find a particularly strong opponent, then.
You'd be wise to, Player.
How do you know my name?
Nothing gets in or out of Daemonheim without me knowing about it.
Fair enough. Back to my other questions.

o: Do I have any rewards to claim?

b.x: I have no rewards for you at the moment.

o.x: I'm here to trade.

b: If the player is on complexity 1:

b.x: Sorry, but I don't have anything to sell.

b: If the player is not on complexity 1:

b.x: Shop (Smuggler)

o.title: Choose an option:
o: What great foes await me in this area?

o.x: What great foes await me in this area?
There are a number of terrible foes known to lurk at this depth of Daemonheim. I have seen one such foe lurking about this floor.

b: If the boss is Gluttonous behemoth:

b.x: The gluttonous behemoth is a great beast with a huge appetite. It will fight using powerful melee attacks, and it has some magical ability.

When wounded, the behemoth will eat in an effort to heal itself. It always has a stockpile of food nearby, so you'll need to stand between the two to stop it from healing. A warning to you: it will ferociously attack anyone blocking
its path.

b: If the boss is Astea Frostweb:

b.x: Astea Frostweb is a mage with a considerable dominion over ice. She will attack with powerful frost-based magicks and she will attempt to freeze you on the spot.

She also has the power to summon ice spiders to her aid, and will call them more frequently against foes who attempt to prevent her magical damage. If that wasn't enough, she can also call upon divine protection from
melee, ranged or magic.

b: If the boss is Icy Bones:

b.x: Icy Bones is a slow but strong ice troll. He will use ranged attacks unless he catches you, in which case he will pummel you with his club.
He can also trap you by raising stalagmites from the ground. If he succeeds, you'll need to be well protected from melee attacks. It might be better to stay out of his reach.

b: If the boss is Luminescent Icefiend:

b.x: The luminescent icefiend is a larger, more powerful variant of the icefiends wandering Daemonheim. It uses magic and ranged attacks with equal proficiency.

It will use a devastating spell at certain pain thresholds. Encasing itself in ice, it will become immune to all damage and rain down icicles from above. It is best to avoid these icicles at all costs!

b: If the boss is Plane-freezer Lakhrahnaz:

b.x: Plane-freezer Lakhrahnaz is a strange creature known as a stalker. It is resistant to ranged and magic attacks, but, unfortunately, striking it with your sword won't be easy.

It has frozen the area around it, which has become too slippery to walk on. You must overcome its variety of melee, ranged and magic attacks, as well as the slippery floor of its lair, to get up close and strike at the beast.

b: If the boss is To'Kash the Bloodchiller:

b.x: To'Kash the Bloodchiller is a powerful demon. Like all of its kind, it is susceptible to magic. The demon uses magical as well as melee attacks.
To'Kash has the power to flash-freeze the air's moisture, encasing its victims in blocks of ice. If this happens, I hope you have a friend with you.
You can break a fellow adventurer out of the ice and free them without harming them. If To'Kash frees them, however, he is far from gentle.

b: If the boss is Skeletal horde:

b.x: There is a room full of tunnels with skeletons pouring in. A healer of the gorajo tribe is trying to fight back. She will help you, so long as you are close to her.
Her healing is most effective when she's concentrating on only one target. As you defeat more skeletons, watch for the signal that it is time to block a tunnel.

b: If the boss is Hobgoblin Geomancer:

b.x: The Hobgoblin Geomancer is a powerful hobgoblin. He carries a spear and conjures various spells. He also has the ability to temporarily sever your link to the gods.
Aside from disabling your prayers, he'll sometimes snare you to the spot, so carrying a ranged weapon might be an advantage.

b: If the boss is Bulwark beast:

b.x: The bulwark beast is a stalwart behemoth. His outer shell is as hard as rock and standard weapons won't penetrate it.
Your best plan would be either to mine away his shell with pickaxes or get around his protection by using magical spells.

b: If the boss is Unholy cursebearer:

b.x: The unholy cursebearer is a powerful user of magic. It will constantly drain your strength while you are close to it. You can restore this strength by worshipping the cursebearer, but this will only make it stronger.

Rammernaut is a brutish human. He carries a huge maul and only uses melee attacks, giving magic users the advantage if they take him on. He's known to get very angry if the gods try to influence the outcome of his
fights.
If he gets enraged, he'll look to charge down his opponents. Best you try to get him to run into a wall whenever he charges blindly.

Stomp is an enormous behemoth. Not all if him can fit through the portal to our realm. As he takes damage, you'll find that the lodestones powering the portal will turn on. If you take the associated stones from the floor
and put them into the lodestones, the portal will weaken. Do this enough times and... well, you'll see.

b: If the boss is Har'Lakk the Riftsplitter:

b.x: Har'Lakk the Riftsplitter is a mighty demon. He uses massive magical energy to summon hazardous portals which you would do well to avoid. Magic is his strength as well as his weakness.

b: If the boss is Lexicus Runewright:

b.x: Lexicus Runewright is, well, mad. He is a powerful librarimancer and is obsessed with books, often using them as weapons. Since he uses magic to do this, you'll find stabbing weapons or ranged attacks are effective in defeating him.
Sagittare is a skilled mercenary. He is extremely fast, and can render you immobile. It's best that you try to protect against his magical arrows and figure how to chase him about the room.

b: If the boss is Night-gazer Khighorahk:

b.x: Night-gazer Khighorahk is a stalker that cloaks itself in a shield of shadows. Illumination is its weakness, so keep the torches in the corners of the room lit. This will weaken it and, when weakened fully, it'll make its last stand.

b: If the boss is Shadow-Forger Ihlakhizan:

b.x: is a creature of both day and night. Be careful when it flashes, as that is a sign that it will try to blind you. It's best to find something to hide behind to prevent massive damage.

b: If the boss is Bal'lak the Pummeller:

b.x: Bal'lak the Pummeller is a potent demon. Its defences increase over time, and its weapons open rifts in the ground, through which noxious gases rise. It doesn't seem to like the fumes itself, however, so, if you have a
defensive party member, lure Bal'lak over them.

b: If the boss is Skeletal trio:

b.x: The skeletal trio fight as any adventurer would, switching targets and defences to counter their opponents' tactics. You'll need to use magic, ranged, melee and wits to kill off the trio effectively.

b: If the boss is Runebound behemoth:

b.x: The runebound behemoth is a beast enhanced by mages. It is still tied to the locations that bind it, so operate one class of pillar to remove its defences for a while.

A powerful zombie named lords over a dark mausoleum. As you damage him, watch out for the burning effect to the ground about him. As he gets closer to death, he'll call on the deceased and choose graves
around him. If you don't bless these chosen graves before he rises again, they'll explode and damage anyone near them.
Necrolords weave rotten flesh and bone into armour and weaponry; a meaty shield keeps swords at bay, a bony sword makes rangers pay.

b: If the boss is Flesh-spoiler Haasghenahk:

b.x: Be wary of Flesh-spoiler Haasghenahk. It is somewhat unstable, and liable to burst. Stabbing attacks will help make it explode quicker; just be careful, as there is more inside than meets the eye.

b: If the boss is Yk'Lagor the Thunderous:

b.x: Yk'Lagor the Thunderous is a powerful demon, contained by evil mages trying to siphon his power as he remains passive. If you distract enough of the mages pinning him down, their power won't be enough and he'll break free.
Watch out as he unleashes true power: if you don't hide from his attacks, you can expect death or a longer fight.
Blink will run forever if not stopped, and cannot be hit while he is running. Use something in the room to stop him and then damage him before he runs off again.

b: If the boss is Warped Gulega:

b.x: The warped gulega is a demented familiar from a long-forgotten plane. You'll find that it has great resistance to your attacks. This doesn't apply to things from its own plane, so you'll find familiars are extremely effective
against it.

The dreadnauts were human once, but are now screaming monsters. It's best to stay behind him, as he can only kill what he sees in front of him. If you are a quick mage, you'll find running around and firing spells is effective.

b: If the boss is Hope devourer:

b.x: The hope devourers feed on faith and fill all with despair. If you see it growl, it would be wise to show that you are not relying on your hope, turning off prayers before he sucks the power from you.

b: If the boss is World-gorger Shukarhazh:

b.x: The World-gorger's strengths and weaknesses leak into the world about it. Destroying the eyes on the walls will change its defences to different combat styles; use this to your advantage.

b: If the boss is Kal'Ger the Warmonger:

b.x: Kal'Ger the Warmonger possesses knowledge of how to forge great primal weaponry. He can fly around the room, changing weapons and attack styles; so, keep this in mind and change to new styles to defeat him quickly. If you use
protect prayers too often he might enrage, so be careful how you use them. As weapons are his strength, wearing armour might be yours...

o.x: Player: Who are you and why are you here?
Ahhh, when I were a young'un my name were Nigel but, these days, folks mostly call me Stiles.

Long time ago, in Draynor Village, there were three brothers who'd exchange yer stuff for bitty bits o' paper, like these new-fangled banknotes we've got today. Niles, Miles an' Giles they called themselves.
They be long gone, like the golden days, but they were an inspiration to me, so I took this trade myself, an' I changed my name to Stiles.
But why are you here, in this place?
The smell of yon bananas were drivin' me scatty, so I can't go too near the fishing spots.
A tough-lookin' geezer callin' himself a slayer master tried to give me a nosepeg once, but I bain't wearin' one o' them things. Ol' Stiles has a tender nose.
So, would ye like me to exchange yer fish now?

Ahhh, ol' Stiles has banknotes for yer lobbies, yer swordies and yer tuna. 'Tis a grand service I be offerin' here, and nary a penny do I ask in return.

nodes.x: Greetings, recruit! Have you come for some Conquest training?

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: What is this place?
This is the Conquest training facility. Here we train recruits, such as yourself, to develop their commanding skills.
What exactly is a Conquest?
A Conquest is the name we give to the training battles that are run here.
During a Conquest, you will command various troops in an effort to eliminate your opponent's troops.
How does that help me, exactly?
You'll learn to command troops and formulate tactics: skills that might become invaluable in our continued struggle against the Void.
Of course, by taking part in a Conquest, you will also earn Commendations to trade in for rewards, as you see fit.
Interesting.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

o: Could you give me a tutorial?

o.x: Could you give me a tutorial?
Certainly. I can give you a quick tutorial now, if you wish?
Yes please.
Very well, let us begin.
No thanks.
Very well. Is there something else I can help you with?

o: How do I start a Conquest?

o.x: How do I start a Conquest?
Head down the stairs to my right. You'll find two waiting chambers there.
In the southern waiting chamber you'll be able to issue challenges to potential opponents.
If they accept your challenge, you can agree on terms for the Conquest before you get started.
What about the other waiting chamber?
If you enter the northern waiting chamber, we'll automatically pair you with a suitably skilled opponent.
That doesn't seem too complicated.
Don't forget to speak with Knight Dorian to customise your forces first.
Customise my forces?
It's probably best if you speak with Knight Dorian to learn more about customising your forces.
Alright then.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

o: I'd like to spend some of my Commendations.

o.x: I'd like to spend some of my Commendations.
Certainly.
Commendation Rewards

nodes.x: Hmm, if we were to deploy in this formation-
Erm, excuse me?
Woah! Don't sneak up on me like that!
I was standing right here!
Yes, yes. Can I help you with something?

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: What is this place?
This is the Conquest training facility. If you want to learn more, best speak with Captain Ethar, to my right. He's more of a talker.
What do you do here?
I help organise recruits' forces so they can take them into Conquest training exercises.
I see.
Can I help you with anything else?
How do I recruit forces?
There are two steps to recruiting your forces. First, you form a squad; second, you choose which Commands to take with you.
How does that work?
I can help you with both steps. I'm the person to talk to if you want to select troops and Commands for a Conquest.
There are several different types of troop, each with their own strengths and weaknesses.
Bear in mind that powerful troops cost more. You must consider this when choosing the troops for your squad.
Can you give me an example?
Well, you could recruit several smaller troops, such as Scouts, for the cost of a larger trooper, such as a Knight.
So, how much is this going to cost me, recruiting these troops?
Oh don't worry about your bank balance, you don't need to 'pay' anything. This is just a training exercise, recruit.
We have assigned the various troops an arbitrary resource cost, just to simulate the expense of maintaining them in the field.
It's up to you to decide how you wish to balance your squad based on their cost.
What about if some of my troops fall in battle...how do I go about replacing them?
We're not about to go killing off our own forces! Remember, this is just a training exercise.
Troops defeated in combat will simply be removed from the Conquest and will be ready to fight again when you face a new opponent.
Right, I think I understand.
Great! Did you want to take a look at the recruitment options now?
Yes please.
Here, take a look.
Squad selection
No thanks.
Very well. Was there anything else I could help you with?
How do I deploy forces?
I can help you to develop a formation, organising the positions of your troops in a Conquest.
How does that work?
Once you have recruited troops for your squad, you can come and see me to organise where - and in what formation - they are deployed on the battlefield.
Would you like to try it now?
Yes please.
Here, take a look.
Squad formation

o: Could you set me up with the default squad?

There we are, you should be all set to go now.
Thanks!

o.x: Did I summon it, do you mean? Certainly not, although I am the only wizard in this Tower with the expertise to guard and study it.

o.title: Select an Option
o: How did it get here, then?

o.x: It's been here longer than anyone remembers. I daresay some foolish wizard summoned it while meddling with forces they did not fully understand.
Every time it's destroyed it reappears on the same spot, so we built a containment ward around it and left it there.

nodes.x: Who are you?
The name's Yaktwee.
Yaktwee Swinmari Cianta. Pleased to meet ya.

o.x: Well, I like it, and my parents thought it suited me.
Anyway, it's just something to call me by.
What are you doing here?

nodes.x: Hello.
Quickly - Tell me, is it still there?
Is what still where?
The THING, the THING! It was just outside my house! Has it gone away yet? Or is it still lurking out there, waiting for me to go outside?
I didn't see any THING out there, just a couple of guards. What did it look like?
Ohhh, it was HORRIBLE! It was an enormous THING, with TEETH and EYES and... and... and THINGS!
Um... would you care to be more specific?
I can't. I only saw it in the dark.
You only saw this THING in the dark?

I was sleeping peacefully one night, when suddenly I woke up and saw it through the window. It was LOOKING at me! I haven't dared go out since then. It's had me trapped in here for days! I've packed my
bags so I can escape, but the THING's still out there waiting for me to come out! If I have to stay in here much longer I'll go mad! MAD!! MAD!!
There's no THING outside. Just come out and get some fresh air before you go funny in the head.
You want me to go outside?
I think you might just have dreamed about the THING.
You want me to believe that it's not real?
Please come outside!
No! No! I know what you are! You're in league with the THING! It keeps sending people in here to trick me into going outside! They keep stealing from me too! GO AWAY!
I'm not trying to trick you!
Get thee gone, trickster!
Sheesh...

Heh heh heh. No use talking to de dead, dem has nuttin' you be wantin'. If you want to buy someting, come an' talk to me.

nodes.x: Choose an option:
Hi!
Ah, a new recruit! Good, you're just in time.
Uh, what? I'm no-
It's always good to see fresh blood on the ground. You can take over from Wilkins - he's never been quite right...ever since the explosion.
Explosion? What? I can't take over for anyone. I don't know what to do!
We all feel like that the first few days, lad/lass. You'll come to grips with it soon enough.
But I'm not a new recruit! I don't know what I'm doing! I don't even know who you are!
Why, I remember when I first joined the guard... Captain Murry threw me off the defence into th- Wait, what? You're not a new recruit? Hmm, now that you mention it, you are out of uniform, soldier.
That's because I don't have a uniform! I don't work for you.

Well, we can fix that soon enough. Lad/Lass. Would you like to join the Imperial Guard and defend Burthope from the most vile of creatures? Put your life on the line to keep at bay the scum of the earth? Risk your health to-
I get the idea!

nodes.title: Do you want to join the Imperial Guard?

o.x: Yes, I'll join the Imperial Guard.
Fantastic! You are in for the thrill of a lifetime. The adventure of the ages. The journ-
What do I have to do?
Hmm? Oh, of course. I'll make it quick. We can't dilly-dally. Monkey about. Sit on our bu-
*ahem* You were explaining?
Every month, you can come back here and help defend the gatehouse.
Why every month? Aren't trolls invading all the time?

Yes, but due to union regulations we can only have each shift work once a month. There are two things you can do to help the gatehouse. You may only choose to do one to gain a reward. You can still play the other, for practice, any time you like. So, things you can do to help defend the gatehouse... First, you can fight trolls. You stand alone in front of the gate and fight off as many trolls as you can until you die.
What? Until I die?
Well...maybe not die. Basically, we leave you out there until you 'almost' die, then drag you back in. That way you don't lose any of your stuff.
Okay, what's the other thing I can do?
Oh, that's much safer. Well, you won't die, but Norris did have a nervous breakdown a few weeks ago. I guess the strain of it got to him.
Oh no.
Basically, you run around repairing the gatehouse defences. Keep the oil drums full, repair barricade lines and gatehouse walls... You got all that?
That's the spirit! Which do you want to do? Remember: you'll only get rewarded for the first activity you complete each month.

o.x: No, I'd like a little more detail.

nodes.x: Good day, my friend! Good day!
It is my privilege to offer you access to an exclusive stock of the finest and most... nutritious... wares.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: Xuan's Fresh Produce

o: Can I ask about your stock?

o.x: Of course. Nothing would bring me greater joy!
Age-worn botanists in lands far beyond this grew these fantastic vegetables with such precision and skill that they can re-vitalise your life energy. Each is a treasure beyond value.
How do I use them?
Why, you eat them. When you consume one of my delicious vegetables, the nutritious energy will create a wondrous and most satiating glow.
The botanists call this effect 'fullness'. It is a curious bloated feeling. You may feel quite tired when 'full'. I would advise that you do not operate heavy machinery.
What powers do they have?
Each is unique! Some aid you with combat, some with training. Some are simply yummy in a casserole. I even heard of a vegetable which turned cannonballs into squid!
The power will not last forever. Some time after consuming one of my life-sustaining vegetables, you may find that the hunger rises again in you. How long depends on the size of the vegetable.
I'm also offering a special guarantee: should you discover a rotten vegetable in my stock, return it to me and I shall give you a full refund!
One hundred thousand apologies! I am Xuan. The land of my birth lies far from here, by my home now is New Varrock, for the ruler of this city does not allow me to leave.
You are most welcome. Please, return as often as you like.

nodes.x: I don't know who you are, but if I were you, I wouldn't enter this cave just like that! There are creatures down there that would make mincemeat of any normal person.
Besides, the inhabitants of this cave are a fantastic example of semi-symbiotic relationship and I'm just not going to let any old adventurer trample the place and destroy everything.
Maverick here can tell you all you need to know. All you have to do is ask.
'Sup?

b: If the player has not yet talked to Dotmatrix:

b.x: Er, I'm not sure. What's going on here?
Ask Beardie 'ere. I don't wanna spill his beans.
Okaaay.

b: After the player has talked to Dotmatrix:

b.x: Dotmatrix told me you'd have practical information on what's going on down there?
That I do, yeh. Ya'll need skills if you want to survive down there. Many skills. Which d'ya wanna know about?

o.x: Down in the caves, ya'll get them roots hanging down. With one of 'em hatchets, ya can give 'em the chop. They take a bit of hacking before ya get stuff off 'em. Hit'em once and they'll stop moving. Hit'em twice and you'll get

some wood. If them curly when you hack 'em, ya get firewood. If them straight, ya get a stick that's okay for fletching. At the back of the cave, there's that massive beastie. Queen, Beardie calls it. It's got roots around it
that feed it. If they go funny, like blue, spiked and twisted, cut'em. Beasties'll love ya for it. Don't cut them healthy ones tho', or the beasties'll get peeved. Fair, really. Anything else?
No, thanks.
Righto!

Them caves down there are mighty damp. No way to light a proper fire normally. But there are some corridors which are dry enough that ya can burn stuff in firepits. If you have one of them tinderboxes, or a hard root (that's

one of them straight roots that's been hardened on a fire), then it's easy. Just cut some of them curly roots, and light fires in the corridors. Ya'll find the dry patches easily enough. If ya just got the curly wood, hope for

some other nutter to light a fire in the corridors. Then ya just have to throw your roots in. Them fires keep mutated beasties away from healthy ones. Healthy beasties'll like ya for it. Anything else?

When you cut them straight roots, you get weapon material. Raw. What ya do is, ya harden them on a fire until they rock solid, yeah? Then ya fletch them. Ya'll need a knife. Ya'll get proper javelin-type shafts.

Primitive, yes, but efficient too. Once you got 'em shafts, ya need a vine. Ya get them from the funny vines behind the Queen, or by killing them mutated beasties. One shaft, one vine, you attach together and you have one killer

weapon. That's not all. Them mutated beasties may drop those boney-woody balls when ya kill them. Get two of these and one of the vines, and you get a great thing that tangles whatever you throw it at. They get stuck to the
ground, like by magic! Anything else?

Now, the mutated beasties down there are a right piece o' work, right? Without a high Slayer level, there's no way ya'll be able to attack them. They don't like being poked, that's fair, but they won't let ya get away with it if ya do.

They have a sharp bite, blighters, so ya think, 'fine, I'll range them', yeah? Not a bad idea; they don't like stuff being thrown at them from a distance. Them primitive weapons ya can fletch down there, will do good damage.

But that doesn't mean they can't get at ya if ya try to hide. They use magic to get ya! And if ya think that it's okay, ya can protect yourself from magic, well they can still get ya. They communicate to them roots in the room,

ya see, and bid the ones next to ya to whip ya. Now, ya can cut them roots a bit beforehand and they won't attack ya. But there are lots of them, and they will grow back, and move, and attack ya again. Blasted creatures,

them mutated beasties. And what d'ya get? Fruits and seeds and stuff ya can use for Fletching. Tho the male ones, the mightiest, I wouldn't be surprised if they could drop something awesome yeah? But ya'll have to try it for
yourself. I ain't goin' back in there for the life of me! Anything else?

Whatever ya do to help them healthy beasties, like cut bad roots, light fires or kill mutated beasties, they'll appreciate it. They not ungrateful creatures. They got an offering stone in the cave, and they'll put fruits and seeds

and stuff on it when ya do help them. Good to know if ya've taken a beating, yeah? Some of the fruits are special, too. Eat'em and you'll find they do nice things for ya. Try them and see. Tho them special fruits will become

plain and boring if you get too far away from the vine and its habitats. I guess the magic is only happenin' here. Finally, check around the back of the cave. Ya might find another way outta there, ya never know. Anything else?

nodes.x: Hello there, dearie! How can I make your Lumbridge day even more wonderful?
Hello to you too! What do you do here?
I'm the Lumbridge herald, my dear! It's my job to make Lumbridge a lovely place to be.
You need a parade? I'll arrange it! You need a fancy banner? I can do that too! You need a herald cape...
Herald cape? What's that?
Why, it's the latest and greatest thing in Lumbridge attire. We provide you with a lovely Lumbridge cape to wear around, for nothing!
And if you've been particularly handy around the area, we'll show you how to customise it into something more fabulous!
In fact, I hear that other cities, like Varrock and Falador, are also offering herald capes with their own special designs!
Naturally, our Lumbridge capes are much nicer.
Can I interest you in taking a cape?

o.x: Sure, I'll take it!
Wonderful! Let's take a look at the customisations we can do...
No, thanks.
Oh, gosh. Well, drop by again if you change your mind, sweetheart.

nodes.x: Welcome to Varrock, my [fine fellow/good lady]. How might I be of service?
Hello; a pleasure to meet you. What do you do here?
I'm glad you asked, for I have the distinct honour to be the Varrock herald.
It is my solemn duty to uphold and maintain the standards and practices of the royal court, whether it be royal events or herald capes.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
Clear off food sack.
What do you want?
What do you do here?
I bring goods in from outside. Need anything?

o.x: Trader's Goods
No, thanks.

nodes.x: What'll it be?
Excuse me?
A, B, AB? What? I've got fresh; pungent; any temperature or maturity you like.
Between you and me, I've even got some exclusive, quality non-Morytanian blood. Misthalin; know what I mean? Keep it between us, mind.
I don't think I...
Then stop wasting my time; I don't have all day.
(Begins with one of the following dialogues:)
Well, I guess so.

nodes.title: Select an Option

o.x: What do you do here?
(Continues with one of the following dialogues:)

o: I'm lost... Can you help me?

o.x: I'm lost... Can you help me?

Well, you're in sector [one/two/three/four/five/six], but if you were hoping for any other help then I'm very sorry. I find it hard enough to help myself. Life's so very hard here. Before too long they'll be wanting to have another blood tithing and then I'll feel just awful again.
What's a blood tithing?
You must be new here, else you'd know for sure. It's where we have to give a blood tithe to the vampyres. They do it on a weekly basis, a different sector each week so they don't kill us all off.

o: Do you know about the Myreque?

o.x: Do you know about the Myreque?
It's probably best not to talk about that, friend.
I need to make contact with them. Please don't worry - I'm on their side.
As are we all, but I really can't talk about them. It's not a subject easily broached here.

o: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

o.x: Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?

Yep, that's where we are at the moment. This place, Meiyerditch, is just one large ghetto. The city is sectioned off so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill us all off in one go.

o: What do you know about the vampyres?

o.x: What do you know about the vampyres?

They're monsters, I know that much. I've never known anything else, but I have a feeling it might be nice to not have to live in fear the whole time. Worrying if I'm going to make the next blood tithe quota. I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres, most likely converted from some sort of bipedal creature, probably human. Juvinates are initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to get some special powers. After that you have the vyrewatch - they're nasty... really nasty.

Hi there!
Am I dead? What's going on here?
Luckily for you, not at all! I've brought you here because - well - Death needs your help!
I'm standing in for him while he's absent, but I'm sure you know the guy. The Grim Reaper, the Collector of Souls... Whatever you like to call him. He retrieves souls from dying creatures, mainly.
So what does he need me for?

Well his instructions in case of absence aren't too clear. Not sure he ever expected to be gone, but I'm doing my best. It looks like there's an imbalance in the harmony of life and death. Too much life, as far as I can tell.
This seems like something you should probably be more sure of...
Oh, it'll be fine.
Anyway, Death's noticed you're a bit of a killing machine. Putting it simply, he wants you to kill some things.
I can do that! When do I start?
Straight away! First, let me give you this gem. It'll let you contact me or Death remotely, in case you need help or another assignment.
You receive a grim gem.
Before I give you your first assignment, I also need to know whether you're happy to team up with other adventurers. Don't worry, you can change your mind later.
Now for your first assignment.
Let's see what we've got. Right! We need X souls from the following battle: monster name. How does that sound?

o.x: Spinning plates?
That's right - there's a funny story behind them. Their shipment was held up by thieves.
The crate was marked 'Dragon Plates'. Apparently they thought it was some kind of armour, when really it's just a plate with a dragon on it!
(Diango's Toy Store opens.)
Wow, a kite!
You're not the first to say that...
Can I have one, please?
Well, I suppose I did order more than I need... It's yours for the bargain price of 100 coins.

o.title: Select an Option
o: That's a bargain! I'll take one.

o.x: That's a bargain! I'll take one.
(Diango's Toy Store opens.)

o: No, thanks, I don't want one.

o.x: No, thanks, I don't want one.
Party items, you say?

Yep! In a partnership with my pal Party Pete, we've decided to launch a whole range of partyware to help celebrate the Royal Wedding of the King Black Dragon and the Kalphite Queen. Confetti, bubble makers, fireworks, firecrackers. We even have a commemorative mug!
King Black Dragon and Kalphite... Wait, what?

Er, well, that's what I was told; perhaps our providers got it wrong. Mind you, it wouldn't be the first time. Like, this once, we were due to receive a shipment of dragon mail, and we got a pile of slightly singed letters instead.
Anyway, we've got all those items on sale, and I even have a suitable bouquet available for those who want to emulate the happy bride!
She had a bouquet? The Kalphite Queen? Big bug, beady-eyed, occasionally flies about when it's not laying eggs... Are we talking about the same creature?

Listen, partner, I'm not the one writing the advertising pitch here. I got the goods and been told what to say in order to sell them. It's not the most convincing pitch I've ever had to do, but, if you ask me, the products don't need a pitch. They speak for themselves. Have a butcher's.
(Diango's Toy Store opens.)

o: I'd like to check my items, please.

o.x: Sure thing, let me just see what you're missing.
(Diango's Item Retrieval opens.)

o: Can you check my bank for items?

o.x: Sure thing, let me see what I can take off your hands.
I'll look through items that I will hold onto, items that could go into a costume room in your house and junk items.
(Item Cleanup opens.)

nodes.x: Will you ever get to rest, Skully?
Probably not. I was cursed to live forever; this is all that is left of me.
Who would do such a thing?
Someone who had a bone to pick with me.
Bwahahaha!
I...suppose it's good that you can laugh about it.
Greetings.

o.x: I'm glad to see you taking this so well. Most of the recently deceased are more upset.
Yes, I'm afraid that you are.
Calm down, calm down. You're just dead.

nodes.x: Fortunately for you, it is not yet your time.

nodes.title: Select an Option
o: Great! How do I get back?

o.x: It is not your time. Destiny awaits you. I will not claim you. Yet.
Right... thanks.

nodes.x: You can go back now. When you leave here, you'll return to the town.
When you die you keep some of your items, but you lose others.
I lose my stuff?
Your valuable gear will be dropped wherever it is you died. However, you can choose three of those items to keep.
You can see which items will drop and which will be kept in the deathkeep interface in your Worn Inventory.
When you return to the world of living, you have a short time limit to return to the site of your death and reclaim your dropped gear.
Whenever you die with items that could drop, you'll see an interface allowing you to choose which ones to keep.
You can selectively take your items one at a time, take them all with the 'take all' button, or re-equip your gear and take the rest of your items with the 'Equip all' button.
Take the portal behind you and return to the world of the living.
